meta.title: Collateral Factors
meta.description: How the collateral factor of each Avana market is computed from its tokens' Aave V4 Core Hub factors and a pool risk factor, how Collateral Risk sets the borrow rate, and which caps also limit borrowing.

strings: Collateral Factors

How the collateral factor of each Avana market is computed from its tokens' Aave V4 Core Hub factors and a pool risk factor, how Collateral Risk sets the borrow rate, and which caps also limit borrowing.
Overview
Formula
Token Factors
Pool Risk Factor
Aave Configuration
Worked Example
Collateral Risk and Rate
Caps
Each market's collateral factor starts from the weakest of its tokens' Aave V4 Core Hub factors and is reduced by a pool risk factor of at most 40%.

Valuation and borrowing limits are calculated separately. The LPOracle reports the value of the liquidity each vault token represents, with no haircut. The vault-token reserve's collateral factor then sets how much of that value can support debt. Aave V4 uses one collateral factor for both borrowing and liquidation and calculates health per account. In Avana an account is one PositionProxy holding one market, so each market has its own collateral factor and health factor.
CF_LP = floor(min(CF₁, …, CFₙ) × poolRiskFactor / 10⁴)
Borrowing capacity = LP position value × CF_LP

All values are in basis points. CFᵢ is the collateral factor of each pool token, and the pool risk factor is set per pool. The result rounds down, so it is never above the formula and at most 1 bps below it, and Aave never lends more than the computed factor allows.

An LP position is only as good as its weakest token, so the smallest token factor bounds it. The pool risk factor then discounts for what an LP position adds on top of its tokens: price-path loss inside the pool, pool manipulation and the cost of unwinding liquidity during a liquidation. It is applied only here; the LPOracle reports the unhaircut value.
Token factors
Pool risk factor
CF_LP
USDC 7,800; USDT 7,500
2,812 (2,812.5 rounded down)
Both 7,800
4,000 (ceiling)
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.

Each token's factor is its Aave V4 Core Hub collateral factor, read by the risk reviewer at listing and stored in Avana's ParameterStore (bounds 1 to 9,999 bps). The source is recorded in the listing file. There is no automatic link to the Core Hub: factors are recalibrated manually through the timelock.

A GHO leg uses an explicit factor set in the listing payload, never the Core Hub GHO value, because the Core Hub does not list GHO as collateral at a usable value. Tokens with no Core Hub listing also use an explicit value set at listing.
Parameter
Bounds
Change
tokenCollateralFactorBps
Normal delay (5 days)
ghoLegCollateralFactorBps
Set per token in the listing payload; normal delay
poolRiskFactor
Lower at the short delay (12 hours); raise at the normal delay

The Aave V4 risk service providers set each pool's risk factor in the market's listing payload, within 1 to 4,000 bps, so the pool risk factor is at most 40%. It reflects the position's range, price sensitivity, pool depth and expected liquidation costs.

Avana draws on Gauntlet's analysis of LP collateral, which recommends conservative starting factors. When the borrowed asset is not one of the pool's own tokens, such as GHO borrowed against WETH/USDC, it suggests starting as low as 0.25 times the lower underlying factor. Final factors are calibrated per market with the service providers.

At the 40% ceiling, a pool of two tokens with 78% factors has a collateral factor of 31.2%. Borrowing to the Lens recommendation of health factor 1.10 then gives an opening loan-to-value of about 28.4% (31.2% divided by 1.10).

The Aave DAO sets the collateral factor on every dynamic key of the vault-token reserve, greater than 0 and at most the formula value. A key above it is drift: the RiskModule stops new-account pledges, borrowing and withdrawals with debt in that market, while repayment and liquidation continue on Aave's live values.

To cut a factor, Avana first lowers the pool risk factor at the short delay, which stops new borrowing against the market through the drift check. The Aave payload then edits every existing key of the reserve.
To raise a factor, the Avana change at the normal delay executes first and the Aave payload follows.

Listing margin: for every price route of either token (primary, alternate and standby), 10,000 minus CF_LP must exceed the route's published feed deviation plus its drift within one heartbeat. With CF_LP of 2,812 the headroom is 7,188 bps, well above a 350 bps alternate route.

Bonus bound: the maximum liquidation bonus times CF_LP, rounded up, must stay below 10,000 bps, so an account that first becomes liquidatable always holds enough collateral to pay the debt and the bonus. With a 105% maximum bonus and CF_LP of 3,000 the product is 3,150.
No vault-token reserve key may have collateral factor 0. Offboarding uses positive collateral-factor steps instead.

Market 3 is a USDC/USDT Aerodrome Slipstream market on the CDP Spoke "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" on Base. One whole vault token (10⁶ units) is worth $2.00, CF_LP is 3,120 bps, and USDC is priced at $0.9999.
Item
Value
Carol pledges an unstaked position with liquidity 10,000,000,000
10,000 whole vault tokens, $20,000
CF-weighted collateral
Recommended borrow shown by the Lens (health factor 1.10)
Protocol maximum (health factor 1.00)
Carol borrows 5,000 USDC (debt value $4,999.50)
The Lens previews add a small margin for interest accrued before the transaction is included, so the previews sit slightly below the plain ratios.
ARFC illustration
The ARFC uses a $100,000 USDC/USDT position with a lower token factor of 75.00% and a pool risk factor of 37.50%, giving 28.12% after rounding down. These figures are not proposed launch parameters.
Result

About 25,560 GHO

Each vault-token reserve also has a Collateral Risk value in bps, set by the risk reviewer in the Aave listing. It is not a haircut on collateral value: it sets the borrower's risk premium. Because each account holds one market, the account's premium is that market's Collateral Risk.
Borrowing rate = baseRate × (1 + riskPremium)

The GHO strategy is flat, so the rate does not depend on utilization. The Aave DAO keeps the GHO base rate at or above the Aave V4 Core Hub GHO base rate. This is not enforced on-chain; Avana monitoring alerts if it falls below.
Premium accrues on drawn debt and does not compound on itself.
Example: a loan backed by collateral with a 50% risk premium pays 6.75% at a 4.5% base rate. With a 5.50% base rate and a 15% premium, the effective rate is 6.325%.

The CDP Spoke's risk-premium threshold must be at least the highest Collateral Risk on the Spoke plus 1 bps, and is never lowered while debt in that asset exists. Otherwise Aave's premium check could make repay, borrow, withdraw and liquidation revert.
Avana adds no interest fee on any asset; all interest accrues to the lender.
An account's borrowing capacity also depends on its existing debt, oracle checks and available liquidity. These caps bound how much collateral and debt can exist:
Scope
Launch value
marketUsdCap
Regular pledge budget per market
Set per market in the listing payload
topUpSliceUsd
Budget reserved for rescue top-ups per market
tokenUsdCap
Exposure per pool token across every Spoke and market of a Hub
Set per token in the listing payload
depositorUsdCap
Exposure per depositor across a Hub
Set in the listing payload
minPledgeUsd
Smallest value of a pledge or top-up
stressFloorUsd
Lowest whole-token price used for cap charges and Hub supply-cap sizing
poolShareMaxBps
Avana's share of a pool's liquidity on a chain
No limit by default; a per-pool cap only where the listing sets one; alert above 25%
Hub supply cap
Vault-token units per market, sized at the stress floor
(market cap + slice) / stress floor, in whole tokens
Draw cap
Debt per CDP Spoke and debt asset
Within the credit line, flash liquidity and route depth
There is no borrower allowlist, no minimum debt and no daily borrow limit. Exposure is limited by these caps and by Aave's health-factor check. How the health factor is measured is explained in
Health Factor

meta.title: Custody and Vault Tokens
meta.description: How Avana holds LP positions, records their backing and represents them on Aave V4: LPVault, Collateralization, vault tokens, PositionProxy, ProxyManager and the Lock.

strings: Custody and Vault Tokens
How Avana holds LP positions, records their backing and represents them on Aave V4: LPVault, Collateralization, vault tokens, PositionProxy, ProxyManager and the Lock.
Overview
LPVault
Collateralization
Vault Tokens
VaultTokenFactory
PositionProxy
ProxyManager
Lock
Backing Invariant
Reconcile Example
Aave V4 accepts collateral only as ERC-20 reserves, while an AMM position is an NFT or a pool share. Avana separates custody of the position from the collateral record that Aave sees.

Seven immutable contract types on each chain hold a pledged position and turn it into Aave collateral. Each AMM protocol has one LPVault that holds its positions. One AMM-neutral Collateralization ledger records how many units each position backs. One vault token per market stands for those units one for one. The AaveAdapter mints vault tokens to the borrower's PositionProxy for that CDP Spoke and market, and the proxy supplies them to the CDP Spoke. The ProxyManager creates proxies, and the Lock stops one Avana call from re-entering another.
Contract
Instances
One per AMM protocol per chain
Holds every pledged position of its AMM protocol and knows each depositor of record
One per chain
Backing records, credited units, seizure order, exposure counters and the pending-settlement balance
Vault token
One per market
Transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20; one base unit per credited unit
Deploys vault tokens with CREATE3 and keeps the token and LPVault registries
One per wallet, CDP Spoke and market
The borrower's Aave account for one market; logic-free
Creates proxies with CREATE2 at predictable addresses
Shared reentrancy lock with two members, the AaveAdapter and LPVaultSwap

None of these contracts can be upgraded. Custody of positions, and the rule that a position returns only to its depositor of record, live in the immutable LPVaults and Collateralization, so no upgrade of the AaveAdapter, RiskModule or LPVaultSwap can change them.

An LPVault is the immutable custodian of every pledged position of one AMM protocol on one chain. At launch there are two: the Uniswap v3 LPVault on Ethereum and the Aerodrome Slipstream LPVault on Base. A later AMM protocol, or a later generation of position contracts that an existing LPVault does not name, gets a new LPVault with a new integration ID. Existing LPVaults, Collateralization and the Lock are not redeployed.

An LPVault has no proxy, owner, admin role, pause or rescue function. It takes every address it calls from its constructor immutables, including the AMM protocol's position manager and factory, so forks and other factory generations are rejected. It reads no pause state, breaker, address freeze or price, so seizures, fee collection and debt-free exits reach it in every state.
What it does
Function
Behavior
bindMarket
Called by the MarketRegistry at listing. Validates and stores the market's pool and exact shape once; a stored market never changes.
receivePosition
Pulls the position from its owner, checks that its pool and shape equal the market's exactly, records the owner as depositor of record and returns its units.
depositorOf
The custody map keyed by position key. It is non-zero only while the position backs an open record.
composition
Token amounts per unit at a given oracle price vector. The LPOracle compiles the same pricing library.
unwind
Removes exactly the units Collateralization debits and sends only their principal to LPVaultSwap or Collateralization, never a fee owed to the position.
releaseToDepositor
Removes the units of a partial removal and sends their principal to the depositor of record, with the depositor's per-token minimums.
returnPosition
Deletes the custody entry, then sends the whole position, with every live unit and every fee owed to it, to the depositor of record. It takes no recipient.
collectFees
Pays every separated fee of a custodied position to its depositor of record. Units, supply, caps and debt are unchanged.
returnStray
Sends a position that reached the LPVault without a record to the owner governance established, through a normal-delay timelock operation.
Exact-shape validation

For concentrated liquidity, a position is accepted only if its lower and upper ticks equal the market's range exactly. A position with any other range is refused even if it overlaps, because a narrow range valued at the market's per-unit price would be overvalued. For example, a market listed at [−10, 10] accepts a position at [−10, 10] and refuses one at [−9, 10]. On Base, a Slipstream position staked in a gauge is refused.
Fees and added liquidity

Trading fees belong to the depositor of record. Where the AMM protocol keeps fees apart from the position (Uniswap v3, Aerodrome Slipstream), the depositor collects them at any time, in every pause state, price state and breaker state, and liquidation never takes them. Where the AMM protocol rolls fees into the position, they stay in each unit's value and return with the position. Liquidity that anyone adds to a custodied position is not credited until the depositor calls the re-credit function, and it is never removed by a seizure; it returns to the depositor with the position.

Only Collateralization can call the functions that move a position, units, principal or fees, and only while the AaveAdapter or LPVaultSwap holds the Lock. The stray-position return is the only recovery path. It runs at the normal timelock delay, requires the Lock to be free, checks the stray condition at execution and can be cancelled by any canceller.

Collateralization is the immutable, AMM-neutral backing ledger of every pledged position on one chain. One instance serves every Hub, CDP Spoke, market and AMM integration on the chain. It reaches each AMM protocol only through that protocol's LPVault, and only the AaveAdapter and LPVaultSwap can call it.
Responsibility
How it works
Backing records

One record per pledged position, keyed by integration ID and position key: depositor, proxy, market, credited units, original charge and status. A record never moves to another depositor, proxy or market.
Credited units

The units the LPVault reports after it takes custody, less units removed by seizures and partial removals, plus units added by re-credit. The AaveAdapter mints exactly this number of vault-token base units.
Record limit
At most 16 open records per account and market. A 17th pledge reverts, rescue top-ups included; the borrower adds to an existing record with re-credit instead.
Largest-first seizure list
Each account keeps its records ordered by credited units, largest first. A seizure walks the list from the head and stops when the seized units are covered, so it touches only the records it debits.
Exposure counters
Market counters per vault token, and token and depositor counters keyed by Hub. Adding a CDP Spoke or market never multiplies a Hub-wide cap.
Pending-settlement balance
Token amounts removed for vault tokens that Aave seized but that were never settled. They keep those vault tokens backed until anyone calls the pending settlement.
Rescue units
Units added by a rescue top-up. They count fully in Aave's health factor and liquidation, and are valued at zero when Avana checks a new borrow.
Cap counters per Hub

Each pledge is charged in USD at a price of at least the market's stress floor ($1.00 per whole vault token by default). The charge is added to the market counter, to the counter of every pool token on that Hub and to the depositor's counter on that Hub. Example from the specification: with a Stable LP Hub token cap of $5,000,000 for USDC, a $3,000,000 pledge on one CDP Spoke and a $2,500,000 pledge on another both book against the same counter, so the second is refused ($5,500,000 is above $5,000,000).

Every exit releases exactly the charge its units carry, from the rescue slice first and then from the regular budget. Exit counters saturate at zero and never revert, and exits never call the RiskModule, the MarketRegistry or the ParameterStore, so a policy fault can never block a withdrawal or a liquidation.
Seizure checks

Before a liquidation, LPVaultSwap asks Collateralization to snapshot the proxy's supplied shares and the vault token's total supply. After Aave seizes and the AaveAdapter burns the seized units, Collateralization requires the share drop and the supply drop to each equal the seized units. It then debits the records largest-first and has the LPVault unwind exactly those units to LPVaultSwap. A record debited to zero stays open, so the depositor can still collect its fees and withdraw the position.
Reconcile on exit

A faulty LPVaultSwap could take seized vault tokens without settling them. The proxy's supplied shares would then be below its credited units. On the next withdrawal, partial removal, re-credit, repay with collateral, zero-credit release or seizure of that account, Collateralization treats the missing units as seized: it debits them largest-first, moves their token amounts into the market's pending-settlement balance and releases the rest. Any address can later call the pending settlement on LPVaultSwap, which burns the stranded vault tokens, swaps the tokens into the debt asset and adds the proceeds to the Coverage Spoke of the market's debt reserve. The caller receives nothing.
Partial release

A depositor can remove part of a pledged position's credited units while the position stays pledged. Collateralization debits the record, releases the charge those units carry and has the LPVault pay their principal to the depositor of record, each token at least the caller's minimum. The withdrawal of a whole position requires the units to equal the record's credited units; the app reads them from the release preview.

A vault token is the collateral-only ERC-20 that represents the credited units of one market inside Aave V4. There is exactly one vault token per CDP Spoke and market, and it is one collateral reserve of that Spoke on the Spoke's home Hub. It has no owner, admin, role, setter, pause, blocklist, permit, transfer hook, rebasing, fee on transfer or emissions. Its bindings (integration, LPVault, market key, Hub, Spoke, market ID, LPOracle, AaveAdapter, LPVaultSwap and Collateralization) are immutables, and Collateralization reads the market's identity only from them.
Units and decimals

One base unit equals one credited unit of the market. For Uniswap v3 and Aerodrome Slipstream a unit is one unit of the position's liquidity over the exact range. There is no conversion factor anywhere in mint, burn or transfer.

Decimals are fixed at listing: the smallest value from 6 to 18 at which one whole token is worth at least $1 at the listing's reference prices. A whole token is therefore worth between $1 and $10 at listing, and activation requires the oracle's whole-token price to be between $0.50 and $20.00.
Example: a USDC/USDT position with liquidity 5,000,000,000 mints 5,000,000,000 base units, which is 5,000 whole tokens at 6 decimals.
Mint and burn

Only the AaveAdapter mints and burns. It mints only to a registered proxy of the market, inside a pledge (exactly the credited units) or a re-credit (exactly the added units). It burns from a registered proxy after a withdrawal, partial removal or repay with collateral, and from LPVaultSwap after a seizure. A burn needs no allowance, and the token refuses a burn from the Hub. The registry of valid proxies lives in the token, is written only by the AaveAdapter on a proxy's first pledge into the market, and has no removal.
Transfer rule
Every balance change is on one of five paths. Every other transfer reverts, including zero-amount transfers and transfers by a spender with an allowance.
Path
From
When
Mint
None
Registered proxy
Pledge, re-credit
Supply
The CDP Spoke pulls the supply
Withdraw
Withdrawal, partial removal, repay with collateral
Seizure
LPVaultSwap
Aave liquidation
Burn
Registered proxy or LPVaultSwap
After a withdrawal or a seizure

Proxy-to-proxy transfers, transfers from LPVaultSwap back to the Hub and transfers to or from the AaveAdapter all revert. Because seized collateral can reach only LPVaultSwap, any other caller of the Aave liquidation reverts when the Hub tries to send it the seized tokens. The Spoke settings that close the remaining paths are described in
Hubs and Spokes
Supply bound

Total supply is at most the market's credited units plus its pending-settlement units, and equal to it while every seizure is settled in the same call. Between transactions vault tokens rest only in the Hub, except seized units held by LPVaultSwap after a seizure that was never settled.

The VaultTokenFactory is immutable and deploys every vault token of its chain. Only the AvanaTimelock can call it, in the same batch as the market's listing operation, at the normal delay of 5 days. It deploys with CREATE3, salted by the CDP Spoke and the market key, so each token address can be predicted and checked in the deployment manifest before the listing executes.
The market key is derived from the chain ID, integration ID, pool and exact shape. One pool listed with two ranges is two markets with two tokens.
The token registry maps each CDP Spoke and market key to one token for life and is never cleared. A market relisted on another Spoke gets a fresh token at a fresh address.
The LPVault registry maps each integration ID to one LPVault, written once by a timelock operation after checking that the LPVault names this chain's Collateralization and Lock.
Deployment reverts unless decimals are between 6 and 18 and the integration is registered.

A PositionProxy is the borrower's Aave V4 account for one market on one CDP Spoke. It holds that market's supplied vault tokens and the debt of every debt reserve the account borrows on that Spoke, under one health factor. A wallet that uses two markets has two proxies, so no market's collateral backs another market's debt.
Logic-free and immutable: no implementation pointer, initializer, upgrade path, delegatecall, receive function or role. It is never replaced, and no account moves between proxies.
Created with CREATE2 by the ProxyManager, one per wallet, CDP Spoke and market, on the wallet's first pledge into that market.
Its four immutables are the AaveAdapter, the wallet, the Spoke and the market ID. They never change.
Its one state-changing function, execute, accepts calls only from the chain's AaveAdapter, including for its bound wallet. The wallet never calls the proxy directly.

It reads no state and calls no Avana contract or price source. All account logic lives in the AaveAdapter, which upgrades only through the timelock, so a fix reaches every proxy at once and no exit depends on code inside the proxy.
A borrower who loses its wallet key can never withdraw its positions. Its debt can still be repaid by any payer or cleared by liquidation.

The ProxyManager is the only creator of PositionProxies on its chain. It is immutable, with no owner, role, pause or setter. Only the AaveAdapter can ask it to deploy, and it refuses a wallet that the MarketRegistry has frozen. It keeps no wallet-to-proxy map: the AaveAdapter keeps the binding, and each vault token keeps its registry of valid proxies.
salt = keccak256(abi.encode(wallet, spoke, marketId))

The prediction view returns a proxy address before deployment. Because the binding is part of both the salt and the constructor arguments, whoever triggers the creation, the proxy at that address is bound to that wallet, Spoke and market. A second deployment for the same triple reverts.

One immutable reentrancy lock per chain is shared by every Avana contract that moves assets or changes accounting. It has exactly two members, the AaveAdapter and LPVaultSwap. Each of their outer entry points acquires the Lock first and releases it last. While it is held, Collateralization and the LPVaults accept calls only from their named caller, and any attempt to start a second outer entry point in the same call tree reverts.
AaveAdapter entry points: pledge, recredit, borrow, repay, withdraw, removeLiquidity, repayAllAndWithdraw, repayWithCollateral, collectFees and releaseZeroCredit.
LPVaultSwap entry points: liquidate, liquidatePermissionless and settlePending.
A new CDP Spoke, market or LPVault uses the same Lock with no redeploy and no membership change.
The Lock is not a pause. It never blocks a protocol action at the start of a transaction.
For every market, at the end of every transaction:
vaultToken.totalSupply ≤ totalCredited + pendingUnits

Each pledge, withdrawal, partial removal, re-credit, repay with collateral and settlement leaves the gap (credited plus pending, minus supply) unchanged, and the AaveAdapter checks this after each call. Equality holds while every seizure is settled in the same call. The one-sided form keeps a market working if a faulty settlement path ever burned units it did not settle: the liquidity behind such a burn stays in custody, so circulating vault tokens stay more than fully backed.

Each record also keeps its live units at or above its credited units. A pledge sets credited equal to live units, an addition by anyone raises live units only, and every removal lowers both by exactly the units debited. The Lens reports vault-token supply next to the liquidity held, so anyone can check the backing of each market.
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.

This example from the specification shows how an unsettled seizure is handled. Alice pledges two USDC/USDT positions: record 1 with 5,000,000,000 units and record 2 with 4,000,000,000 units. After a depeg, a faulty LPVaultSwap takes 1,575,000,000 seized units without settling them.
Step
Spoke supply
Records 1 / 2
Pending units
Total supply
After both pledges
Unsettled seizure
Alice repays and withdraws record 1 with 3,425,000,000 units
Alice withdraws record 2
Anyone calls the pending settlement

In the third step the shortfall is 1,575,000,000 units. Collateralization debits it from record 1 at the head of the list, moves the matching token amounts into the pending-settlement balance and returns the rest of the position to Alice with all of its fees. The 1,575,000,000 outstanding vault tokens stay backed until the settlement burns them and sends the recovered debt asset to the Coverage Spoke.
How Avana holds LP positions in LPVaults, records their backing in Collateralization and represents them on Aave V4 with vault tokens held by per-market PositionProxies.

meta.title: Health Factor
meta.description: How Aave V4 measures the health factor of each Avana account, the borrow limits Avana applies on top, rescue top-ups, and worked numbers for borrowing, withdrawal and partial removal.

strings: Health Factor
How Aave V4 measures the health factor of each Avana account, the borrow limits Avana applies on top, rescue top-ups, and worked numbers for borrowing, withdrawal and partial removal.
Overview
Calculation
Borrow Limits
Worked Numbers
Rescue Top-Ups
Account Limits
Prices and Health
User Actions
Aave V4 computes one health factor per account. In Avana an account is one PositionProxy holding one market, so each market a wallet uses has its own health factor.

The health factor compares an account's collateral, weighted by its collateral factor, with its total debt over every debt reserve. Aave V4 computes it on the CDP Spoke with standard accounting. An account below 1.00 can be liquidated, partially, through LPVaultSwap.

Each wallet has one PositionProxy per CDP Spoke and market, and each proxy is a separate Aave account. A price failure, breaker or liquidation in one market never changes another market's account. A token price shared by two markets moves both by design; the per-Hub token caps bound that shared exposure.
healthFactor = (collateral value × CF) / Σ debt value of every debt reserve
Collateral value is the account's supplied vault tokens at the market's LPOracle price, with no haircut.

Each debt reserve is valued at its own Aave price: GHO at Aave's fixed $1, any other debt asset through its DebtOracle. A rise in a debt asset's price lowers the health factor with no collateral move.
Every rounding is against the account: the result is rounded down, and debt rounds up.
With no debt the health factor is the maximum value. Debt-free means the account has zero debt on every debt reserve.

Aave's own rule is the only on-chain limit Avana relies on: Aave refuses any borrow or withdrawal that would leave the health factor below 1.00. Avana sets no opening health floor of its own. The borrower chooses its headroom with the minimum health factor it passes to each borrow, withdrawal with debt or partial removal with debt.
Limit
Value
Where
Aave health-factor threshold
On-chain, in the CDP Spoke
minHealthFactor
Chosen by the caller
On-chain argument, checked by the RiskModule after the Spoke call
hardHealthFloor
0 (off) on every launch market; bounds 1.00 – 1.25 when set
Optional per-market floor, set only if stress tests justify it
Recommended borrow
Shown by the Lens next to the maximum at 1.00; never enforced

After a borrow or a withdrawal with debt, the RiskModule requires the health factor, with rescue units valued at zero, to be at least the largest of 1.00, the market's hard floor and the caller's minimum. Example: with $100,000 of collateral at a 70% collateral factor, the Lens shows $63,636 recommended ($70,000 / 1.10, rounded down) and $70,000 maximum.
A hard floor is raised or enabled at the short delay of 12 hours and lowered at the normal delay, by at most 0.03 per step; disabling it sets it to 0 in one step.
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.
Market 3 is a USDC/USDT Aerodrome Slipstream market on Base. One whole vault token is worth $2.00, CF_LP is 3,120 bps, USDC is priced at $0.9999, and there is no hard floor.
Borrow
Step
Result
Carol pledges $20,000 of collateral
CF-weighted collateral $6,240
Lens borrow preview
Recommended 5,673.29 USDC (HF 1.10); maximum 6,209.56 USDC (HF 1.00)
Carol borrows 5,000 USDC with a minimum health factor of 1.20
A borrow of 5,700 USDC instead
HF 1.0948, below her 1.20; reverts with HealthFactorTooLow
Withdraw
Carol adds a second position of $5,000. Her account holds $25,000 of collateral, $7,800 CF-weighted, against 5,000 USDC of debt, a health factor of 1.5602.
Action
Withdraw the $5,000 position with a minimum of 1.20
HF 1.2481; the position and its fees return to Carol
Withdraw the $20,000 position instead
HF would be 0.3120; Aave reverts with HealthFactorBelowThreshold
Repay all and withdraw in one call
Debt-free exit; reads no pause state, breaker, freeze, price or sequencer gate
Partial removal

From the same two-position account (HF 1.5602), Carol removes 2,000 whole tokens (about 2,000 USDC and 2,000 USDT) from her first position and keeps it pledged. The record falls to 8,000,000,000 units, collateral falls to $21,000 and CF-weighted collateral to $6,552, so the health factor is 6,552 / 4,999.50 = 1.3105, above her 1.20 minimum. The remaining record must still be worth at least the $10 minimum pledge.
Adding collateral is a borrower's cheapest way out of liquidation, so containment never refuses it. A rescue top-up is a pledge into an account with debt whose health factor is below
rescueHealthFactor
, which is fixed at 1.10. Its charge is capped at the amount that brings the account back to 1.10.
It passes a Hub in the Frozen or Paused (General) state, a tripped circuit breaker, the pool-share cap and an address freeze. A Hub paused for a suspected mint-path exploit refuses it.
It needs only $10 or the market minimum pledge, whichever is lower, and can use the market's reserved top-up slice (10% of the market cap) when the regular budget is full.
The record cap still applies.

The units it adds are rescue units. Aave counts them in full for health and liquidation, but Avana values them at zero when it checks a new borrow, a withdrawal with debt or a partial removal with debt, so they never support new debt.

Example: an account at health factor 1.2000 with $10,000 of debt holds $1,000 of rescue units at a 3,120 bps collateral factor. Excluding them removes $312 of CF-weighted collateral, so the health factor Avana checks for new debt is 1.1688.
One collateral market per account: the proxy's market.

At most 16 open records (positions) per account and market. A 17th pledge reverts with TooManyRecords; the borrower adds to an existing position with re-credit instead. The cap keeps a seizure of a whole account within one transaction: 16 records cost at most 5.15M gas, under 31% of the 16.78M per-transaction limit.
The number of debt reserves per account is bounded by the CDP Spoke's per-account reserve limit, set by the Aave DAO.
No minimum debt. Any borrow above 0 that passes the other checks is accepted. Avana's own keepers liquidate every account below 1.00 whatever its size and pay the gas.

Aave values every reserve at the price its source serves. Under a failing price the oracles serve conservative prices, so the health factor can only move against the borrower, while nothing is ever seized or repaid at those prices.
Price state
Collateral in Aave
Non-GHO debt in Aave
Live, routes agree
Accepted price
Routes disagree
Built from the lower route answers
Higher route answer
Cached (up to 1 hour)
Last accepted price
Expired
Worthless (the smallest price Aave accepts)
Last accepted price raised by the asset's stress rise

Borrowing and withdrawals with debt need fresh, agreeing prices for the market and every debt reserve of the account. After an Expired price recovers, and for one hour after a Base sequencer restart, only accounts below health factor 0.95 can be liquidated, which gives borrowers time to act.
Borrowing more lowers the health factor.
Repaying raises it immediately. Anyone can repay any account's debt, and no Avana pause, breaker, freeze or price state blocks repayment.
Pledging another position, a rescue top-up or a re-credit of added liquidity raises it.
Repaying with collateral repays debt from part of a pledged position in one flash-funded call, and the health factor after the call cannot be lower than before it.
Withdrawing or removing liquidity with debt must leave the health factor at or above the caller's minimum and 1.00.
For how each market's collateral factor is set, see
Collateral Factors
How Aave V4 measures each Avana account's health factor, the limits Avana applies on top, rescue top-ups and worked numbers for borrow, withdrawal and partial removal.

meta.title: Incentives
meta.description: Who gets paid what in Avana: the keeper reward from each liquidation's oracle gain, the borrower's surplus, Avana's keeper and coverage funding, and interest to lenders.

strings: Incentives
Who gets paid what in Avana: the keeper reward from each liquidation's oracle gain, the borrower's surplus, Avana's keeper and coverage funding, and interest to lenders.
Overview
Keeper Reward
Borrower Surplus
Avana's Keepers
Coverage Funding
Lenders
Not Included
The payments Avana's contracts make, who receives each one, and what Avana Labs pays for itself.

Avana's contracts pay out in one place: the settlement of a liquidation. After the debt and the flash loan are repaid, LPVaultSwap splits the realized surplus between Avana's fee recipient, the caller and the borrower, all in the debt asset repaid. Interest goes to lenders, and Avana Labs pays for its own keepers and funds the First-Loss Reserves.
Participant
Receives
Pays or provides
Liquidation caller
Keeper reward from the oracle gain
Gas, swap outcome and any shortfall top-up
Borrower
Any recovery above the oracle value of the seizure; all LP fees
Interest and the liquidation bonus on seized collateral
Avana Labs
20% of the oracle gain; app fee outside the contracts
Its own keeper gas; First-Loss Reserve capital
Aave DAO
All interest on its credit lines
The credit-line liquidity

Aave sizes each seizure at the oracle price, so the bonus it pays is the oracle gain: the oracle value of the seized units, less the debt repaid and the flash premium. The caller's reward is that gain after Avana's 20% share, up to what the swaps actually realized.
keeper reward = min(S, G) − A
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.

In the Ethereum example of 1,950 USDC repaid against a vault token at $2.10, the oracle gain is 96.525 USDC, the realized surplus 89.325 USDC and Avana's fee 19.305 USDC, so the keeper receives 70.02 USDC.

The same reward applies to approved keepers and to any address using the permissionless entry point. A caller that covers a shortfall from its own funds is held to its own spend limit and minimum payout. A reward that the token refuses to deliver is held in the payout escrow for the caller to claim.

Value the seized collateral produces above its oracle value, for example because a swap route paid better than the oracle price, belongs to the borrower whose collateral produced it. LPVaultSwap sends it to the borrower's wallet in the same transaction.
borrower surplus = max(0, S − G)

In the same example, swaps returning 2,052 USDC instead of 2,040.30 would give a surplus of 101.025 USDC: Avana's fee stays 19.305, the keeper receives 77.22 and the borrower 4.5 USDC. The borrower also keeps the rest of the position and all of its separated fees.

Liquidation never depends on a keeper making a profit. Avana runs its own approved keeper on each chain and liquidates every account below health factor 1, whatever its size, paying the gas as an operating cost from its keeper budget. The budget is set with the Aave V4 risk service providers in the keeper agreement, and monitoring warns at 50% and pages at 25% remaining.
One liquidation of a single record uses about 1,550,000 gas; one of the largest account (16 records) at most 5,150,000.
Each chain needs at least one active keeper. Up to 32 keepers can be approved per chain through the timelock, including a standby keeper on separate infrastructure.
Permissionless callers pay their own gas and receive no reimbursement.

Avana Labs funds the Coverage Spoke (Avana Umbrella) of each Hub and debt asset, in that asset, before any draw cap on the pair rises above 0. The Aave DAO controls it. It covers recorded deficits within 72 hours and is Avana's only on-chain loss layer. The coverage ratio and minimum are set in the funding ARFC with Aave's service providers.

Value recovered from an unsettled seizure also goes to the Coverage Spoke, not to Avana or the caller: the pending settlement pays its caller nothing, and its conversion is held to an oracle-based floor, so no one profits from an unsettled seizure.
All interest on a credit line accrues to its lender, the Aave DAO for GHO. Avana takes no share of it. Fee details are in
Platform Fees
Vault tokens have no emissions and no issuance schedule. They are minted only against credited units and burned on withdrawal, partial removal, repay with collateral or seizure.
Vault tokens cannot be traded: they move only between a registered proxy, the Hub and LPVaultSwap.
There is no fee on borrow interest and no Avana fee on repay with collateral.
There is no settlement budget: a caller that needs to cover a rounding gap at final settlement pays it through its own shortfall top-up.
The keeper reward from each liquidation's oracle gain, the borrower's surplus, Avana's own keepers and First-Loss Reserve funding, and interest to lenders.

meta.title: Lend Spoke
meta.description: The supply-only Aave V4 Spoke through which the Aave DAO treasury supplies each credit line to the Avana Hubs, and how draw caps divide each line.

strings: Lend Spoke
The supply-only Aave V4 Spoke through which the Aave DAO treasury supplies each credit line to the Avana Hubs, and how draw caps divide each line.
Overview
Credit Lines
Line Sizes
Draw Caps
Funding Order
Interest
Recall and Growth
Public Deposits
A supply-only Aave V4 Spoke, owned by the Aave DAO, through which the DAO treasury supplies each credit line that Avana borrowers draw from.

Each chain has one Lend Spoke. It is a standard Aave V4 Spoke owned by the Aave DAO, and it only supplies: its draw cap is 0 on every Hub asset. Its reserves point to Hub and asset pairs and can list any asset. The lender of each line, the GHO Reserve and Aave DAO for GHO, supplies the line amount through it directly, and the resulting position and its interest belong to that lender.
Only Avana CDP Spokes have draw caps on a credit-line asset. The other Spokes registered on it (the Lend Spoke, that asset's Coverage Spoke and the asset's fee receiver) have draw cap 0.
No Avana contract or role has authority over any supply cap, draw cap, interest rate or Lend Spoke position. These are Aave DAO decisions.

A credit line is a draw cap per Hub, asset and CDP Spoke. The Lend Spoke's supply cap on a Hub and asset equals the line, and the draw caps of every CDP Spoke that draws that pair sum to at most the line.
LendSpoke.addCap(hub, asset) = creditLine(hub, asset)
Σ over CDP Spokes of drawCap(hub, asset, spoke) ≤ creditLine(hub, asset)
With one CDP Spoke per chain and AMM protocol at launch, each Spoke's draw cap on a debt asset is that asset's whole line on the chain.
Credit-line sizes come from Aave governance. Avana proposes values, and the funding ARFC, prepared with the Aave V4 risk service providers, sets the final ones.
Chain
Launch GHO line
Ethereum
Avana Stable LP Hub
2,000,000 GHO; final value set in the funding ARFC
Base
Set in the funding ARFC, within the GHO flash liquidity of the Base Aave V3 Pool and the depth of the Base swap routes
Other debt assets get their lines at their own listing, through the enable-debt-reserve operation, once the Aave DAO approves their credit line, caps, price source and swap routes.

Each debt reserve's draw cap is at most the flash liquidity of its asset in the chain's Aave V3 Pool and the depth of its swap routes, measured at listing, so every borrowed amount can be flash-borrowed and swapped back in one liquidation.

The Hub admits a draw only if the Spoke's drawn debt, premium, uncovered deficit and the new amount fit under its draw cap. Accrued interest and recorded deficits use up capacity until they are repaid or covered.
The sums are checked by Avana's MarketRegistry when a debt reserve is enabled and on every cap change, and by the drift check.
Monitoring alerts when the debt drawn on a reserve, including interest and premium, reaches 90% of its draw cap. Only borrowing of that asset fails at the cap.
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.

On Ethereum with a 2,000,000 GHO line, the Lend Spoke supply cap is 2,000,000 and the CDP Spoke "Uniswap v3 Stable" has a draw cap of 2,000,000. With 1,900,000 GHO drawn, 3,000 GHO of premium and a 475 GHO uncovered deficit, a 100,000 GHO borrow would bring the total to 2,003,475 and reverts. The largest borrow that passes is 96,525 GHO.
Before any CDP Spoke draw cap on a Hub and asset rises above 0, two things must be true:
The lender has filled the Lend Spoke supply cap with the full line, so no outside supply fits under the cap.
The Coverage Spoke (Avana Umbrella) of that Hub and asset is funded by Avana Labs to at least its minimum, and its balance satisfies the coverage ratio.
fundedBalance × 10⁴ ≥ coverageRatioBps × Σ drawCap

The ratio and the minimum are set in the funding ARFC with Aave's service providers. As an illustrative guide only, a 20% ratio needs 400,000 GHO of funded reserve for a 2,000,000 GHO draw cap. The check runs when a debt reserve is enabled, on every recorded draw-cap raise and on every borrow.

All interest on a credit line accrues to its lender. For GHO that is the Aave DAO. Each debt asset's fee receiver is an Aave DAO treasury address and its liquidity fee is set by the DAO. Avana charges no fee on borrow interest on any asset, and no interest-fee parameter exists.

The GHO rate is flat: it does not depend on utilization. The Aave DAO sets the base rate at or above the Aave V4 Core Hub GHO base rate when each proposal executes, and each borrower pays its risk premium on top. Every other debt asset's rate strategy is set by the Aave DAO in the proposal that lists it. How the premium is set is explained in
Collateral Factors

To recall a line, the Aave DAO lowers the CDP Spoke draw caps on that Hub and asset to 0 and can change rates. The asset returns to Hub liquidity as borrowers repay or are liquidated, and the Lend Spoke can withdraw only unborrowed funds. There is no forced repayment, and repayment, withdrawal and liquidation stay open.

Raising a line takes an Aave DAO proposal on that chain that raises the Lend Spoke supply cap and the CDP Spoke draw caps together, keeping each draw cap within flash liquidity and route depth. Avana's timelock has no authority over any of them. The ARFC sets out these phases for GHO:
Phase
Capacity
Conditions for expansion
Launch
2M GHO on Ethereum; Base line set in the funding ARFC
Audit and launch requirements met, with oracle availability, borrowing activity and liquidation-route performance reported to governance
Initial target
Demonstrated borrowing demand, acceptable concentration and execution costs, and a recommendation from the risk reviewers
Expansion
Continued operation within approved limits, satisfactory risk reporting and further governance approval

The funding proposal defines the measurement periods and thresholds for these conditions, the authority to adjust capacity, repayment terms and interest allocation. At every phase each chain's draw caps stay within its flash liquidity and the coverage ratio holds.

Public lender deposits are not offered at launch. Because the lender fills the supply cap with the whole line before borrowing opens, no outside supply fits under it. Public lending through the Lend Spoke is supported by the design and can be enabled later through Aave governance.
How the Aave DAO supplies each credit line through the supply-only Lend Spoke, how CDP Spoke draw caps divide it, and how lines are funded, recalled and grown.

meta.title: Hubs and Spokes
meta.description: The Aave V4 Hubs and Spokes Avana runs on: Avana Hubs, CDP Spokes, the Lend Spoke, Coverage Spokes, the three required settings, credit lines, the contract call graph and asset flows.

strings: Hubs and Spokes
The Aave V4 Hubs and Spokes Avana runs on: Avana Hubs, CDP Spokes, the Lend Spoke, Coverage Spokes, the three required settings, credit lines, the contract call graph and asset flows.
Overview
Avana Hubs
CDP Spokes
Lend Spoke
Coverage Spokes
Vault-Token Fee Receiver
Required Settings
Credit Lines
Cross-Hub Lines
Call Graph
Asset Flows
Avana runs on standard, unmodified Aave V4 Hubs and Spokes that the Aave DAO owns and configures. Avana's own contracts handle custody, valuation and liquidation around them.

Every Hub, Spoke, AaveOracle and configurator Avana uses is unmodified Aave V4 at a pinned release, deployed and owned by the Aave DAO. Avana proposes their configuration and checks it on-chain, but holds no role on them and is not a lender. Each chain Avana runs on has the same set of Aave-side contracts:
Contract
How many
Role
Avana Hub
Holds the vault tokens of its markets and the debt-asset liquidity of its credit lines
CDP Spoke
One per chain, Hub, AMM protocol and risk tier
Lists several markets as collateral reserves and the approved debt reserves
One per chain
Supply-only Spoke through which the DAO treasury supplies each credit line
Coverage Spoke (Avana Umbrella)
One per Hub and debt asset
Supply-only Spoke holding the First-Loss Reserve that covers recorded deficits
Vault-token fee receiver
One per vault-token asset
Aave treasury Spoke registered with zero caps

An Avana Hub holds only one vault-token asset per market of its CDP Spokes and each credit-line asset the Lend Spoke supplies to it. Liquidity is organized into three Hub tiers because stable, correlated and volatile LP positions carry different risks. A chain can host any of the three.
Positions
Status
Avana Stable LP Hub
Stablecoin and blue-chip pools with tight pricing, low slippage and minimal impermanent loss
Launch, on Ethereum and on Base
Avana Correlated LP Hub
Pools of assets that move together, with tighter risk bands
Added later on any chain
Avana Volatile LP Hub
Major DeFi assets and governance-token pools with wider ranges, under stricter exposure limits

Each Hub has its own application pause state in Avana's MarketRegistry, and the token and depositor caps are counted per Hub across all of its CDP Spokes and markets. A market belongs to one Hub for life; a later Hub gets new markets, and users move by repaying, withdrawing and pledging again.

A CDP Spoke is one standard Aave V4 Spoke per chain, Hub, AMM protocol and risk tier, with exactly one home Hub. It lists several markets. A market is one pool with one exact position range, and each market is one non-borrowable vault-token reserve of its Spoke. The Spoke also lists the debt reserves recorded for it, GHO first. Each account (one PositionProxy) holds exactly one market, so every market has its own health factor.
Chain
Launch CDP Spoke
Ethereum
Uniswap v3 Stable
Uniswap v3 positions from the canonical position manager, exact tick range
Base
Aerodrome Slipstream Stable
Unstaked Aerodrome Slipstream positions, exact tick range
Configuration

One liquidation configuration per Spoke, shared by all of its markets. Avana recommends a target health factor of 1.10 and a minimum liquidation bonus of at least 2%; the Aave DAO decides both in the listing AIP. A market that needs a different target or bonus curve gets its own Spoke.

The GHO reserve is listed before any vault-token reserve, so it is reserve 0. Other debt assets (USDC, USDT or WETH) become borrowable on a Spoke only through the enable-debt-reserve operation, once the Aave DAO approves their credit line, caps, price source and swap routes.
Debt reserves are borrowable with collateral factor 0, and the Spoke has no supply cap on them, so outside supply of a debt asset cannot become collateral.
The Spoke's AaveOracle reads each market's LPOracle, Aave's fixed $1 source for GHO, and a DebtOracle for any other debt asset.
The per-account reserve limit is set by the Aave DAO and bounds how many debt reserves one account can hold.
No liquidation-manager Spoke variant is used: the only one available allows one collateral reserve per Spoke, which cannot hold several markets.
Deployment operations

Avana adds a CDP Spoke, a market or a debt reserve only through three AvanaTimelock operations at the normal delay of 5 days, each paired with the Aave DAO payload of the same listing and followed by a 12-hour activation that re-checks the live Aave configuration.
Operation
What it does
deployCdpSpoke
Registers a standard Spoke and its AaveOracle, created by the Aave DAO payload, under a Hub with one AMM integration, after checking the three required settings and the Spoke implementation.
listCollateralMarket
Deploys the market's vault token and LPOracle, records the exact range, binds the AMM integration's LPVault and wires the Spoke reserve.
enableDebtReserve
Records the funding Hub and asset, checks the credit-line sums, the flash-liquidity and route-depth bounds, the Coverage Spoke funding and the swap routes, and enables borrowing.

Each chain has one supply-only Lend Spoke, owned by the Aave DAO. Its reserves point to Hub and asset pairs and can list any asset. The DAO treasury supplies each credit line through it, and its supply cap on each pair equals the line. Its draw cap is 0 on every asset. Public lender deposits are not offered at launch.
Credit-line sizes, recall and growth are described in

Each Hub and debt asset on each chain has one Coverage Spoke, the Avana Umbrella of that pair. Avana Umbrella is Avana's protocol safety module, named after Aave's Umbrella, whose design inspired it. It is a supply-only Spoke with draw cap 0, controlled by the Aave DAO and funded by Avana Labs in its own asset. Its supply is that pair's First-Loss Reserve.

Coverage Spokes are the only holders of the Hub's deficit-eliminator role. A Coverage Spoke burns its own shares to cover recorded deficits in its asset from every CDP Spoke that draws that asset from that Hub. A deficit is never covered with another asset's, Hub's or chain's reserve.

It is funded before any draw cap on its pair rises above 0, and must hold at least the coverage ratio times the sum of draw caps on that pair. The ratio and minimum are set in the funding ARFC with Aave's service providers; 20% is an illustrative guide only.
A Hub halt of a CDP Spoke does not stop coverage of that Spoke's deficit.
fundedBalance × 10⁴ ≥ coverageRatioBps × Σ drawCap

When the Aave DAO adds a vault token as a Hub asset, Aave registers the asset's fee receiver as a second Spoke on it with an unlimited supply cap. The listing payload sets that fee receiver's supply and draw caps to 0, and the vault-token asset has a liquidity fee of 0 and a valid interest-rate strategy, so the fee receiver never holds vault tokens.

Each vault-token asset therefore has exactly two registered Spokes: its CDP Spoke, the only one with non-zero caps, and the fee receiver. Both have draw cap 0, and the asset's drawn shares are 0. A second Spoke with caps on the asset could draw vault tokens out of the Hub and leave withdrawals and seizures unable to settle, so it counts as drift.

Liquidation of an Avana account is possible only through LPVaultSwap, because the vault token accepts seized collateral only to LPVaultSwap. The listing AIP sets three values on every vault-token reserve that keep this transfer rule the only gate:
Setting
Required value
Path it closes
receiveSharesEnabled
false
A liquidator taking Spoke supply shares instead of tokens, which moves no vault token
liquidationFee
0, or a fee paid to Avana's fee recipient
Fee shares moving to another address with no token transfer
Reinvestment controller
None (zero address)
A sweep moving the Hub's vault tokens to an address the token refuses
Drift check

The RiskModule compares the live Aave configuration with the values Avana's sizing assumes on every new-account pledge, borrow, withdrawal with debt and market activation. Monitoring checks the same values continuously. The checks include:
The three required settings, and that the vault-token reserve is not borrowable.
Draw cap 0 for every Spoke on the vault-token asset, exactly two Spokes on it, and no reinvestment controller on any Avana Hub asset.
Each reserve's price source: the market's LPOracle, the fixed GHO source, or the asset's DebtOracle.
Collateral risk below the Spoke's risk-premium threshold.
The CDP Spoke implementation is the approved standard Spoke, and its borrowable reserves equal the debt reserves Avana recorded.
The collateral factor is at most Avana's expected factor, the bonus bound holds, and the target health factor equals the recorded value.

When a check fails, new-account pledges, borrowing and withdrawals with debt in the affected market stop. Top-ups to indebted accounts, repayment, fee collection, debt-free withdrawal and liquidation continue, and monitoring raises an alarm. A change by the Aave DAO that would admit another liquidator is drift: the playbook asks the DAO to revert it.
Every borrowable asset comes from a capped credit line approved by the Aave DAO. A credit line is a draw cap per Hub, asset and CDP Spoke. For each debt asset on each funding Hub:
LendSpoke.addCap(hub, asset) = creditLine(hub, asset); Σ drawCap(hub, asset, spoke) ≤ creditLine(hub, asset)

Each debt reserve's draw cap is at most the flash liquidity of its asset in the chain's Aave V3 Pool and the depth of its swap routes, measured at listing, so every borrowed amount can be liquidated in one transaction.
CDP Spokes have supply cap 0 on debt assets; the Lend Spoke and the Coverage Spokes have draw cap 0.
The Hub admits a draw only if drawn debt, premium, uncovered deficit and the new amount fit under the draw cap, so interest and deficits use up capacity.
No Avana contract or role has authority over any Hub cap, interest rate or Lend Spoke position. Each cap is raised only by an Aave DAO proposal.
Monitoring alerts when the debt drawn on a reserve, including accrued interest and premium, reaches 90% of its draw cap.
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.

On Ethereum a 2,000,000 GHO line gives the Lend Spoke a supply cap of 2,000,000 and the single CDP Spoke a draw cap of 2,000,000. If that Spoke has 1,900,000 GHO drawn, 3,000 GHO of premium and a 475 GHO uncovered deficit, a 100,000 GHO borrow needs 2,003,475 and reverts. The largest borrow that passes is 96,525 GHO.

Each CDP Spoke has a home Hub for its collateral, and each debt reserve records its funding Hub. A debt reserve funded by its Spoke's home Hub is the normal case. A cross-Hub credit line, where the funding Hub differs from the home Hub, is fully specified and off at launch on every chain. While it is off, a debt reserve whose funding Hub is not its Spoke's home Hub is refused.

When enabled, the funding Hub owns the cap: one register in the chain's MarketRegistry sums every draw cap on that Hub and asset, whatever the drawing Spoke's home Hub. Each foreign draw cap is limited by its cross-Hub line, the total of cross-Hub lines is at most the funded balance of that pair's Coverage Spoke, a pause of the funding Hub stops every borrow of the line, and a line set to 0 closes at once while existing debt can still be repaid or liquidated.
Each callee accepts a call only from the caller shown. Wallets reach Aave only through the AaveAdapter, and liquidations reach Aave only through LPVaultSwap.
Flow
Who calls whom
Pledge

Wallet approves the LPVault for one position, then calls the AaveAdapter. The AaveAdapter has the ProxyManager deploy the proxy on a first pledge and registers it in the vault token. Collateralization has the LPVault take custody, pokes the LPOracle and asks the RiskModule to check the pledge. The AaveAdapter mints vault tokens to the proxy, which supplies them to the CDP Spoke; the Spoke moves them into the Hub.
Borrow

Wallet calls the AaveAdapter. The RiskModule runs the borrow checks and pokes the oracles. The proxy calls the Spoke borrow; the funding Hub sends the debt asset to the proxy, which forwards it to the receiver. The RiskModule then checks the health factor.
Repay
Any payer calls the AaveAdapter, which moves the amount to the proxy; the proxy repays the Spoke and refunds any unused amount to the payer.
Withdraw
Wallet calls the AaveAdapter. The proxy withdraws from the Spoke, the AaveAdapter burns the vault tokens, and Collateralization has the LPVault return the position to the depositor of record.
Fee collection
Depositor calls the AaveAdapter, which calls Collateralization, which has the LPVault collect fees to the depositor.
Pricing
The Spoke reads its AaveOracle, which reads the LPOracle, the fixed GHO source or a DebtOracle. Anyone can poke the oracles.
Liquidation

A keeper or any address calls LPVaultSwap. LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset through the flash source, has Collateralization snapshot the account and calls the Spoke liquidation. The Hub sends the seized vault tokens to LPVaultSwap, the AaveAdapter burns them, Collateralization debits the records and the LPVault unwinds the units to LPVaultSwap, which swaps through the swap routes and pays out.
Funding and coverage
The DAO treasury supplies through the Lend Spoke. Avana Labs or LPVaultSwap funds a Coverage Spoke, which eliminates deficits on its Hub.
Governance

The governance multisig or the Aave governance executor schedules on the AvanaTimelock; anyone executes once ready. Guardians call the MarketRegistry for pauses, freezes, breaker trips and standby switches.
Where each asset sits at each stage of a position's life, between transactions:
Stage
Position
Vault tokens
Debt asset
Before pledge
Wallet
None exist for this position
After pledge
LPVault, recorded in Collateralization; liquidity stays in the pool
In the home Hub, credited to the proxy
Unchanged
After borrow
LPVault
With the receiver; the funding Hub records the debt
After fee collection
Unchanged; fees went to the depositor
After repay
Back in the funding Hub
After withdrawal
Depositor of record, with all liquidity and uncollected fees
Burned
After partial liquidation
LPVault, with fewer credited units
Seized units burned; the rest in the Hub
Debt reduced; payouts in the debt asset to the fee recipient, the caller and any borrower surplus
After full seizure
LPVault, record open at 0 credited units with its fees
None for this position
Any remaining debt recorded as a deficit on the funding Hub
Deficit coverage
Not involved
Coverage Spoke shares burned against the deficit

A pledged position rests only in its LPVault. Vault tokens rest only in their market's home Hub. No Avana contract holds a debt asset between transactions except the payout escrow, for payouts a token refused, and none holds pool tokens except Collateralization, for the pending-settlement balance.
The Aave V4 Hubs and Spokes Avana runs on, the three settings that make LPVaultSwap the only liquidator, how credit lines are capped, and how calls and assets move.

Where No Fee Applies

Avana's share is computed from the oracle value of the seized units, not from what the caller's swaps returned, and it is never above the realized surplus:
G = max(0, V − D − φ)
S = max(0, R′ − D − φ)
A = min(floor(G × avanaFeeShareBps / 10⁴), S)
V is the oracle value of the seized units in the debt asset, D the debt repaid and φ the flash-loan premium.
R′ is the amount the unwind and swaps recovered, plus any shortfall top-up from the caller.
G is the oracle gain, the bonus Aave paid. S is the realized surplus.

Because the fee is measured on the oracle gain, a caller that routes or sandwiches its own swaps badly cannot lower it while the surplus covers it. Because it is capped at the surplus, the fee never makes a liquidation revert, and the debt is always repaid first.

meta.description: How Ask AI combines Aave MCP, Avana's RAG, and product calculations to explain markets and LP-backed positions.

strings: Ask AI
How Ask AI combines Aave MCP, Avana's RAG, and product calculations to explain markets and LP-backed positions.
Overview
Aave MCP
Avana knowledge and RAG
Market analysis
From analysis to action
Aave protocol data, Avana knowledge, and position calculations in one conversational interface.

Ask AI is Avana's conversational interface for questions about markets and positions. A request names the market, asset, or position to examine. Follow-up questions can clarify the inputs and assumptions. The response explains the available information. Protocol checks still determine whether a requested transaction can proceed.
Avana supports borrowing GHO and other enabled debt assets against Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base.

Wallet-specific questions depend on the selected wallet and network. Public market data describes the market. Balances and positions belong to an account on a particular network. A missing balance, price, or route leaves the associated calculation incomplete.

Ask AI uses Aave MCP alongside Avana's own retrieval system and product implementation. The Model Context Protocol provides a structured interface to external tools. Aave's server exposes v3 and v4 market information, including reserves, rates, available liquidity, and protocol structure. This gives Ask AI Aave-specific context for questions that also involve Avana markets or positions. See
Aave for Agents
and the
Aave MCP documentation

Aave data keeps its network, protocol version, and reserve context. It does not show that an asset is available in an Avana market. Avana CDP Spokes accept only vault tokens for approved Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base as collateral, and lend GHO and the debt assets enabled for each Spoke. Avana still applies its own market listing, LP valuation, and account checks. A capability of the upstream MCP server is not automatically an action in Ask AI. Available actions depend on Avana's integration and the supported product flows.

Avana's retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) searches Avana's protocol knowledge for material relevant to a question. It supplies that material as context for the answer. Retrieved passages explain the architecture, collateral rules, liquidation process, and product workflows. Each passage includes source information, so the explanation can be traced to its documentation. RAG supplies protocol knowledge, not live prices. Rates and balances come from the relevant data sources.

Avana's own position data and calculation logic provide the product-specific context. A borrowing question can combine Aave market information, retrieved explanations of LP collateral, and calculations for the selected position's GHO debt and borrowing capacity. Each input has a different role. A documentation passage explains a rule. A market response reports observed conditions. A position calculation applies the relevant inputs to an account or scenario.

Market comparisons can include the borrowing rate (BaseRate × (1 + UserRiskPremium)), the debt asset available to each CDP Spoke, and each market's Collateral Factor. A displayed fee yield is only one input. Debt interest and changes in the LP position also affect the result. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk, and liquidation risk. Input sources, timestamps, and scenario assumptions give the context needed to interpret the comparison.

Analysis and transaction execution are separate steps. For a supported action, the relevant product flow shows the account, network, assets, amounts, and costs for review. It then requests any required wallet approval. After submission, the transaction is confirmed and the position updates. In the sandbox at app.avana.cc, results are simulated and no onchain transaction is submitted.

strings: Prompt Examples
Write requests that make the market, position, and intended outcome clear.
Ask a specific question
Explore a scenario
Resolve missing details
Compare the borrowing cost and health factor for borrowing 1,000 GHO against my selected LP position.

This request identifies the intended borrow and links it to a selected collateral position. The asset and amount define the debt being evaluated. The position supplies the collateral context. Asking for the assumptions and included costs makes the result easier to trace to its inputs.
What happens to this position's health factor if its collateral value falls by 20% while debt stays the same?

This scenario changes collateral value and holds debt constant. That isolates the effect of collateral value on the health factor. For example, 25,000 GHO borrowed against a $100,000 position with a 35% Collateral Factor has a health factor of 1.40. A 20% fall in collateral value lowers it to 1.12. A larger debt balance or a different LP range is a separate scenario with different inputs. The result illustrates the stated assumptions. It is not an execution quote or a prediction of returns.
Which network and data timestamp does this estimate use, and which costs are excluded?

Network, timestamp, and cost coverage determine what an estimate represents. A follow-up request can resolve missing context before the result is used to prepare an action. The relevant product flow then provides the current transaction terms for review. Estimates in the sandbox at app.avana.cc use simulated assets.

A request sets the asset, network, amount, and position under consideration. It also states whether the user wants an explanation or simulation, or wants an action prepared. Missing or ambiguous details must be resolved before the request can be used in an execution flow.

The request determines which context is needed. Avana's RAG supplies protocol explanations. Aave MCP provides relevant Aave market information. Avana's product logic handles position calculations. Market rates change, quotes expire, and balances differ across networks. The selected account, source timestamps, missing inputs, and scenario assumptions therefore affect how to read the result. This matters most when you compare a simulation with a live position.

A supported transaction goes through three stages: preparation, submission, and confirmation. The product flow provides the transaction review and any required wallet approval. After confirmation, the updated balances and debt show the effect on the position. The sandbox at app.avana.cc shows simulated results and makes no onchain transactions.

Borrow an approved debt asset on the Aave V4 account that holds one market's collateral. GHO is the first debt asset; USDC, USDT and WETH can be enabled per CDP Spoke.

Each wallet has one PositionProxy per market, so each market is its own Aave account with its own health factor and nothing is cross-collateralized. A borrow goes wallet → AaveAdapter → the wallet's proxy for that market → CDP Spoke. The proxy holds no logic and executes only the Adapter's calls; every check lives in the AaveAdapter and the RiskModule.

The borrowed asset is drawn from the reserve's funding Hub into the proxy, and the proxy forwards exactly that amount to the receiver in the same call. A borrow changes no vault token, record or cap counter. There is no combined pledge-and-borrow call, no batched borrow and no multicall: pledge and borrow are separate calls, and each borrow names one debt reserve and carries its own nonce.

Avana enforces no opening health floor above Aave's 1.00. The Lens recommends borrowing to a health factor of 1.10 and shows the protocol maximum at 1.00 beside it. Interest raises the debt over time, so the health factor can fall even when collateral value does not change.

Any asset the CDP Spoke lists as a debt reserve can be borrowed. Governance enables a debt reserve per CDP Spoke with enableDebtReserve through the chain's Timelock. The call records the funding Hub and asset, and checks the credit line and the swap routes from every pool token of the Spoke's markets into the asset.
Asset
Decimals
Aave price source
Status

Each non-GHO debt reserve is priced by its own DebtOracle, which reads a primary, an alternate and a standby Chainlink route with the same freshness, failover and agreement rules as the collateral legs. When Expired, it serves the accepted price raised by debtStressRiseBps, so debt is never undervalued.

The draw is bounded by the Aave drawCap of the reserve's (funding Hub, asset, CDP Spoke), which is the credit line. At launch every debt reserve is funded by the Spoke's home Hub, such as the Avana Stable LP Hub.
One account can owe several debt reserves. The market's collateral, and only it, backs every debt reserve of that proxy.
borrow(uint256 marketId, uint256 debtReserveId, uint256 amount, address receiver, uint256 deadline, uint256 minHealthFactor, uint256 expectedNonce) returns (uint256 drawn)
Parameter
Type
Meaning
The call returns the amount drawn, which always equals the requested amount. The app keeps one pending borrow per proxy, because one nonce sequence per proxy covers every debt asset.

In execution order. The checks cover the account's market and every debt reserve the account owes, plus the one being borrowed. Before checking prices, the RiskModule pokes the market's LPOracle and each non-GHO DebtOracle so that a disagreement or failure first seen by this borrow starts its window on time.
Check
Rule
Error
Price freshness

Freshness is per feed. A Chainlink feed publishes on a deviation trigger or after its heartbeat, so the limit is the feed's own heartbeat plus a 1,800-second publication margin. Because a 24-hour feed can stay silent for a day while inside its deviation threshold, a borrow also needs the second source to agree.
86,400-second feeds (USDT/USD, GHO/USD and the Base stablecoin feeds): fresh for 88,200 seconds.
82,800-second feeds (USDC/USD and USDS/USD on Ethereum): fresh for 84,600 seconds.
3,600-second feeds (DAI/USD, ETH/USD): fresh for 5,400 seconds.

After the Spoke call, the RiskModule reads the account's health factor from Aave and removes the contribution of the account's rescue units, the collateral admitted through the top-up slice or a rescue exemption. Aave counts rescue units in full, but they never support new debt.
hfEx ≥ max(1.00, minHealthFactor, hardHealthFloor(marketId))

The hard floor is off (0) on every launch market and is set only for a market whose stress tests justify it. Aave's own borrow check already requires a health factor of at least 1.00, and a higher on-chain floor would refuse borrows Aave accepts without protecting solvency, which the liquidation path guarantees. A failure undoes the whole call, including the transfer to the receiver.
For the full calculation and how the collateral factor applies, see
Health Factor
The app shows two amounts from the Lens view previewBorrowRecommended, which takes the wallet, market, debt reserve and deadline and returns both:
Recommended: the borrow that leaves the rescue-excluded health factor at 1.10. It is a display value; no contract enforces it.

Maximum: the borrow that leaves Aave's health factor at 1.00 (or the market's hard floor) once interest has accrued to the deadline, with a margin so that a maximum borrow included before the deadline still passes the health check. The view previewBorrowMax returns this amount alone.
target × (1 + rate × (deadline − now)) × 1.005

Both round down, are capped by the reserve's drawCap headroom, and return 0 when the account's borrow gate fails. Example: $100,000 of collateral at a 70% collateral factor and no debt gives a maximum of $70,000 before the margin and a recommended $70,000 / 1.10 = $63,636.

Interest is Aave V4's: the debt reserve's drawn rate on its funding Hub plus the account's risk premium, which Aave refreshes on each borrow. Interest accrues every second and raises the debt to repay; the repay page shows how the live debt is read. Avana takes no fee on borrow interest.
Avana Labs charges an app fee in its own app, outside the contracts. No contract computes, holds or enforces it, and calling the contracts directly does not pay it.
Accrual and repayment are covered in
Repay Loans

State
Borrow

Breakers stop new debt at once and never stop liquidation, repay, top-ups or debt-free withdrawal. A temporary price or depth gate clears after 30 minutes of healthy observations; a deficit freeze stays until the guardian or the timelock reopens it.

Every failure reverts the whole transaction, including the nonce increment, every oracle poke and the transfer to the receiver.
Cause

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Carol's account in market 3 (USDC/USDT, Aerodrome Slipstream on Base) from the Deposit LP example holds 10,000 whole vault tokens at $2.00: collateral $20,000, CF-weighted $6,240, no debt and borrowNonce 0. The USDC debt reserve is funded by the Base Stable LP Hub's USDC credit line and priced by the USDC DebtOracle at $0.9999 on an 86,400-second feed (fresh for 88,200 seconds) with an agreeing second source. The USDC borrow rate is 6.00%. The Hub is in state None and the sequencer gate is Up.

Her app calls previewBorrowRecommended for USDC with a deadline of now + 600: recommended 6,240 / 1.10 / 0.9999 = 5,673.29 USDC (HF 1.10); maximum, with margin (1 + 0.06 × 600 / 31,536,000) × 1.005 = 1.0050011, is 6,240 / 1.0050011 / 0.9999 = 6,209.56 USDC (HF 1.00).
She borrows 5,000 USDC: borrow(3, r_USDC, 5,000,000,000, Carol, now + 600, 1.20e18, 0).
The Adapter reads the Hub state (None), the sequencer gate (Up), the freeze list, the account and the reserve, then consumes nonce 0.
The RiskModule pokes market 3's LPOracle and the USDC DebtOracle: both Live, the USDC round is 30,000 seconds old (at most 88,200), no drift, an active keeper, no breaker tripped.
No cap step runs: Carol's $20,000 charge has been booked since her pledge and a borrow books no charge.
The proxy borrows 5,000 USDC from the Spoke and forwards exactly 5,000 USDC to Carol.
Event Borrowed with nonce 0 and HF 1,248,124,812,481,248,124; borrowNonce becomes 1.
Failing variants
5,700 USDC gives HF 6,240 / 5,699.43 = 1.0948 and reverts with HealthFactorTooLow against Carol's own 1.20. With minHealthFactor 0 it succeeds.
A USDC/USD round 88,300 seconds old reverts with DebtPriceTooOld.
A Hub that is Frozen or Paused reverts with ApplicationFrozen or ApplicationPaused.
A tripped market breaker reverts with BreakerTripped.
1,800 seconds after a sequencer restart the borrow reverts with SequencerGrace; with the feed reporting down it reverts with SequencerDown.
A 1 USDC borrow succeeds: there is no minimum debt, and Avana's own keepers liquidate small accounts at Avana's gas cost.
Rescue units and the maximum

On an Ethereum market, wallet V owes 10,000 GHO against CF-weighted collateral of $12,000 (Aave HF 1.2000). $1,000 of the collateral is rescue units, worth $312 CF-weighted, so the rescue-excluded health factor is (12,000 − 312) / 10,000 = 1.1688. Borrowing 2,000 GHO would bring Aave's HF to 1.00 but the rescue-excluded HF to 0.974, so it reverts with HealthFactorTooLow. 1,688 GHO is the largest borrow the check allows. At a 5.00% GHO rate the Lens returns a recommended 625.45 GHO and a maximum of about 1,629.84 GHO.
