A pledged position keeps earning trading fees for its depositor. The depositor collects them at any time; they are never collateral and never seized.

While the LPVault holds a pledged position, its liquidity stays in the pool and earns trading fees. Uniswap v3 and Aerodrome Slipstream keep fees apart from the position's liquidity, as amounts owed per token. The depositor of record collects them through the AaveAdapter, and the pool pays them straight to the depositor's wallet.

The call goes wallet → AaveAdapter → Collateralization → LPVault → position manager. It never changes the position's liquidity, the vault-token supply, the record's credited units, the account's debt or its health factor. The PositionProxy is not involved: fees never pass through the Aave account.
collectFees(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, uint256 deadline) returns (uint256[] fees)
Only the depositor of record can call it. No role is required.
There is no recipient argument: fees always go to the depositor of record, so neither a caller nor a faulty Adapter can redirect them.
It returns one amount per pool token, in the market's token order; any amount may be 0.

For Uniswap v3 and Slipstream the LPVault calls the position manager's collect with the depositor as recipient and the maximum amount of each token. The pool updates the position's fees first, then pays every owed amount; nothing stays in the LPVault.
An unstaked Slipstream position's fees are already net of the pool's unstaked-fee share, which the pool sends to the gauge. Avana adds and deducts nothing.
The app can simulate the call to show the amounts before the depositor signs.

The fee path reads no pause state or reason, circuit breaker, address freeze, price state, sequencer gate, RiskModule, MarketRegistry, ParameterStore, LPOracle, PositionProxy or Aave state. None of them can hold a depositor's fees. Collection is available from the end of the pledge until the position is returned, including while the record has 0 credited units after a full seizure.
During a Base sequencer outage, the depositor can submit collectFees through the OP Stack L1 forced-inclusion path; it executes when included, because the fee path reads no sequencer gate.
State
Collect fees
Fees are not collateral. The LPOracle values a position's liquidity units only and never counts amounts owed to it, so collecting fees cannot move the health factor.

Fees are never seized. A liquidation, a reconcile on exit, a partial removal or a repay with collateral removes exactly its own units and pays out only the principal that removal returned. A collection cannot run between a removal and its payout, because both run under the same protocol lock.

Principal owed at pledge stays the depositor's. If a position is pledged with amounts already owed to it (uncollected fees, or principal removed earlier without a collect), those amounts are not credited, and collectFees pays them to the depositor with later fees.
Fees owed when a position is returned travel with the NFT; the depositor then collects them directly from the AMM protocol.

Some AMM protocols compound fees into the position instead of keeping them apart. For a market on such a protocol, collectFees reverts with FeesRolledIn before any state changes. The fees stay in the position: its unit count is unchanged, each unit is worth more, the LPOracle's composition values that, and the depositor receives the fees with the units on withdrawal. Both AMM protocols listed at launch, Uniswap v3 and Aerodrome Slipstream, keep fees separate.
Pool Burn with zero liquidity (only when the position has liquidity), then pool Collect.
A token Transfer from the pool to the depositor for each non-zero amount.
Position manager Collect.
FeesCollected(positionKey, depositor, amounts)
Every failure reverts the whole transaction, and the fees stay owed to the position.
Error
Cause

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Carol's first record in market 3 on Base is an unstaked Slipstream NFT with L = 10,000,000,000 (about $20,000), pledged 30 days ago. The amounts owed to it, net of the pool's unstaked-fee share, are 16.50 USDC and 15.95 USDT. Carol owes 5,024.657535 USDC on the account and its health factor is 1.2420. The Base sequencer has been down for 4 hours.
Carol's app simulates collectFees for the position and shows 16.50 USDC and 15.95 USDT to collect.

Carol submits collectFees(3, (I, key1), now + 600) through the L1 forced-inclusion path. When it is included, the Adapter takes the lock and checks the deadline; it reads no pause state, breaker, freeze, oracle or sequencer gate.
Collateralization checks that the record is open, the NFT is in custody and Carol is its depositor of record.
The LPVault calls the Slipstream position manager's collect with Carol as recipient, and the pool pays 16.50 USDC and 15.95 USDT to her.
The NFT's liquidity, the record's 10,000,000,000 credited units, the vault-token supply, the cap counters, her debt and her health factor of 1.2420 are unchanged.
Event FeesCollected(key1, Carol, [16,500,000, 15,950,000]).

The $32.45 collected over 30 days on $20,000 is 32.45 / 20,000 × 365 / 30 ≈ 1.97% a year, and none of it was collateral. A borrow forced in through L1 during the same outage reverts with SequencerDown. The same collection succeeds while the Base Stable LP Hub is Paused with reason MintPathSuspect, while a breaker of market 3 is tripped and while Carol's address is frozen. A call from any wallet other than Carol reverts with NotDepositor.
How a position comes into custody is described in
Deposit LP
How the depositor collects trading fees from a pledged position at any time, and why fees are never collateral.

What Stays Open During Pauses

The account for one wallet and market: proxy, borrowNonce, Aave health factor, collateral value, debt value, average collateral factor, risk premium, borrow count, debt on each approved debt reserve, gate status, breaker reasons, rescue units and whether the wallet is frozen.
The account's records, at most 16, in seizure order (largest credited first).
The market's price state, served and accepted price, feed ages, deviations, and any disagreement or grace window.
A debt reserve's Aave price source, price, source timestamp, age and freshness for borrowing and liquidation.
getBreakerStatus / getDebtBreakerStatus

previewBorrowRecommended / quoteRepayAll / previewRecredit / previewRepayWithCollateral
Previews for the next borrow, repay-all, re-credit or repay with collateral.
Every feed is fresh and the routes agree with the pool's TWAP.
Every action that passes its other checks. Borrow and withdraw-with-debt also need the second source to agree.
The pool's TWAP or a second route disagrees with the served price, or a stablecoin leaves its USD band.
Top-ups, rescue top-ups, repay and debt-free exits. New-account pledges only for a USD-band breach. Borrow and withdraw-with-debt are refused.
A feed is past its heartbeat plus 1,800 seconds; the oracle serves the last cached price.
Repay with funds and debt-free exits. Pledges, borrow, withdraw-with-debt, repay with collateral and liquidation of the market are refused.
Cached for longer than the cached window (1 hour), or a persistent route disagreement. The oracle serves a price of 1 (10^-8 USD per vault token), so Aave counts the collateral as worthless.
Repay with funds and debt-free exits only.
Grace after recovery
For 30 minutes after a feed publishes again, liquidation reaches only accounts below a health factor of 0.95, then every account below 1.00.
The state shows the grace end; borrowers use the window to repay or add collateral.
Carol calls removeLiquidity(3, (I, key1), 2,000,000,000, [1,990e6, 1,990e6], now + 600, 1.20e18).
The account has debt, so the pause, freeze and RiskModule pre-withdraw checks run: sequencer Up, oracles Live, no breaker.
The proxy withdraws 2,000,000,000 units from the Spoke and the Adapter burns them.

Collateralization debits record key1 to 8,000,000,000 units and releases $20,000 × 2 / 10 = $4,000 of charge. The LPVault removes the liquidity and pays about 2,000 USDC and 2,000 USDT to Carol, each at least 1,990.
The remaining record is worth $16,000, above the $10 minimum. Collateral is now $21,000 and CF-weighted $6,552, so HF = 6,552 / 4,999.50 = 1.3105, above 1.20.
Events: RecordReduced, UnitsReleased, CollateralReduced.
V previews with previewRepayWithCollateral(V, m_A, key31, 1,500,000,000, r_USDC): repays 2,968.505747 USDC, returns 29.41 USDC to V, and leaves HF 1.5735.
V calls repayWithCollateral with units 1,500,000,000, minAmounts [1,490e6, 1,490e6], minDebtRepaid 2,950e6 and minHealthFactor 1.30e18.
LPVaultSwap values 1,500 whole tokens at the oracle price vector: 1,500 USDC + 1,500 USDT = 3,000 USDC. After the 100 bps slippage allowance and a 0.01 USDC rounding allowance this is 2,969.99 USDC.
x = min(10,000, ⌊2,969.99 × 10^4 / 10,005⌋) = 2,968.505747 USDC. LPVaultSwap flash-borrows x through the chain's flash source; the premium is ⌈x × 5 / 10^4⌉ = 1.484253 USDC.
The proxy repays 2,968.505747 USDC: the debt falls to 7,031.494253 USDC before any collateral leaves.
The proxy withdraws the units, the Adapter burns them, and the LPVault unwinds 1,500 USDC + 1,500 USDT to LPVaultSwap.
The USDT leg swaps to 1,499.40 USDC (minimum 1,485). Recovered 2,999.40 USDC covers the loan and premium; 29.41 USDC goes to V.
Health check: 11,064 / 7,031.494253 = 1.5735, at least max(1.20, 1.30). Events: Deleveraged, RepaidWithCollateral.
New-account pledge
Refused (rescue-only breakers)
Rescue top-up
Repay (any payer)
Repay with collateral
Refused while Down
Withdraw or remove with debt
Debt-free withdraw or remove, repayAllAndWithdraw, releaseZeroCredit
Collect fees
Monitor an open loan and change its collateral: add collateral, re-credit liquidity you added, remove part of a position, or repay with your own collateral.

An account is one PositionProxy for one wallet and market, with one health factor. Its health factor changes when the LPOracle price of the market's vault token moves, when debt prices move, and as interest accrues. Below 1.00 the account can be liquidated.

To raise the health factor a borrower can repay any amount, pledge another position as a top-up, re-credit liquidity added to a pledged position, or repay with collateral. To take collateral out while debt remains, a borrower can withdraw a whole record or remove part of one, as long as the account stays above the health floor.
Health factor 1.10 is a guide, not a limit: the Lens recommends borrowing to 1.10, and an indebted account below 1.10 can use rescue top-ups. Liquidation starts below 1.00.
The Lens is a read-only contract, one per chain, for apps, keepers and monitoring. Its views never revert on a price state; they revert only while an Avana call is in flight in the same transaction.
View
Returns
The health factor and its formula are explained in
Health Factor

Each market's LPOracle reports a price state, and each non-GHO debt reserve's DebtOracle reports its own. The state decides which actions can run. Example values: a 24-hour stablecoin feed is fresh for 88,200 seconds, the cached window is 1 hour and the grace window is 30 minutes.
State
Meaning
What a borrower can do

A top-up is a pledge into an account that has debt. It uses the same pledge call as a first deposit and the same position rules (exact range, at most 16 records). Because added collateral only lowers risk, a top-up passes a Frozen Hub, a Base sequencer outage or grace window, and Aave configuration drift.
Rescue health factor and the slice

The rescue health factor is 1.10. While an indebted account is below it, a top-up may book its charge from the market's top-up slice (10% of the market cap) when the regular budget is full, but only up to the USD value that brings the account back to 1.10. A rescue top-up is a top-up below 1.10 whose charge is at most that restore amount and whose value is at least the smaller of minPledgeUsd and $10. It is the only pledge admitted under Paused with reason General, from a frozen wallet, under a rescue-only market breaker, above the pool-share cap or below minPledgeUsd.
Rescue units

Units admitted through the slice or a rescue exemption are rescue units. Aave counts them as collateral, so they protect the account from liquidation, but they count as zero for new borrowing and for withdrawals that leave debt: those checks use the health factor with rescue units valued at zero.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. An account owes 15,000 GHO against $50,000 of collateral at a 31.20% collateral factor, so its HF is 1.04. The regular budget is full. A $2,000 top-up books from the slice (the restore amount is $2,884.62), all of its units are rescue units, and HF becomes 1.0816. Under Paused with reason General, an $800 rescue top-up (restore amount $884.62) lifts HF to 1.0982, while a $1,000 pledge reverts with NotRescueTopUp.
Every check a pledge runs is listed in
Deposit LP

Liquidity added to a pledged NFT with the AMM protocol's increaseLiquidity is not collateral until the depositor of record calls recredit. The added units run every check of a top-up of that size, the Adapter mints and supplies exactly those units, and the record's charge basis is rebased. An account at 16 records adds collateral this way.
recredit(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, bytes topUp, uint256 deadline) returns (uint128 added)
For NFT positions the topUp argument is empty. Read the units, charge and whether only a rescue top-up can book them with previewRecredit before calling.
removeLiquidity takes part of one record's units out of the pool and pays the tokens to the depositor of record. The position stays pledged with its remaining units and its uncollected fees.
removeLiquidity(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, uint128 units, uint256[] minAmounts, uint256 deadline, uint256 minHealthFactor) returns (uint256[] amounts)
The units must be above 0 and below the record's credited units; removing every unit is a withdrawal.
The minimum amounts hold one entry per pool token, in the market's token order; each token paid must be at least its minimum.
Only the principal of the removed units is paid. Fees stay owed to the position and are collected separately.
Debt-free, the call reads no pause state, freeze, breaker, sequencer gate or price, and any remainder is allowed.

With debt, it runs the checks of a withdrawal with debt: a Paused Hub refuses it, a frozen wallet cannot make it, the RiskModule pre-checks apply (sequencer, Live prices, second sources, keepers, drift, breakers), the record left behind must be worth at least minPledgeUsd, and the rescue-excluded health factor after the call must be at least the largest of 1.00, minHealthFactor and the hard floor.
Failures:
PartialRemovalTooLarge
for units at or above the credited units,
AmountBelowMinimum
when a token falls below its minimum,
RecordBelowMinPledge
when the remaining record is worth less than minPledgeUsd, and
HealthFactorTooLow

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Carol holds record key1 (10,000,000,000 units, $20,000) and a top-up keyB (2,500,000,000 units, $5,000) in market 3 on Base: collateral $25,000, CF-weighted $7,800, debt 5,000 USDC valued at $4,999.50, HF 1.5602. She removes 2,000 whole tokens from key1 and keeps the NFT pledged.

repayWithCollateral repays one debt reserve with liquidity from one of the caller's own pledged positions, in one call. LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset through the chain's flash source, the proxy repays, the units are withdrawn and burned, the LPVault unwinds them, LPVaultSwap swaps every token that is not the debt asset at oracle-bounded prices, repays the flash loan and its premium, and sends the rest to the caller in the debt asset.
repayWithCollateral(RepayWithCollateralParams p) returns (uint256 debtRepaid, uint256 debtAssetToWallet)

The parameters are the market, the position, the units to release, the debt reserve, a minimum amount per pool token for the unwind, the smallest repayment accepted, the deadline and the minimum health factor after the call while debt remains. No approval of the debt asset is needed.
There is no liquidation bonus, no Avana fee in the contracts and no protocol budget draw. The borrower pays the flash premium and the swap cost.

The repay size is set by oracle prices: x = min(debt, ⌊Vnet × 10^4 / (10^4 + maxFlashFeeBps)⌋), where Vnet is the units' oracle value in the debt asset less the market's slippage allowance (100 bps at launch) and a rounding allowance. A pool trade cannot change it; a sandwich can only make a swap fail its minimum.
The flash premium must satisfy premium × 10^4 ≤ maxFlashFeeBps × x. maxFlashFeeBps is 10 at launch; the Aave V3 Pool charges 5 bps, and 0 once Avana's flash source holds the FLASH_BORROWER role.
The debt falls before any collateral leaves. While debt remains, Aave's health factor after the call must be at least the larger of its value before the call and minHealthFactor.

It runs under a Frozen Hub, under Paused with reason General, for a frozen wallet and under every circuit breaker, because it only lowers debt. It is refused under Paused with reason MintPathSuspect, while the market or the repaid reserve is Cached or Expired, and while the Base sequencer is down. When the flash source is short or paused, repay with funds instead.
DeleverageTooSmall
below the minimum repayment,
HealthFactorNotImproved
MinOutNotMet
for a swap leg below its oracle minimum,
DeleverageShortfall
FlashLiquidityShort
NothingToRepay
, and
ApplicationPaused
under MintPathSuspect only.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. On Ethereum, wallet V owes 10,000 USDC with CF-weighted collateral of $12,000 (HF 1.20). Record #31 is a Uniswap v3 USDC/USDT position at $2.00 per whole token. USDC is priced at $1.0000 and the flash premium is 5 bps.
With a minimum repayment of 3,000 USDC the same call reverts with DeleverageTooSmall(2,968,505,747, 3,000,000,000). With a zero flash premium, x is 2,969.99 USDC.

Pause states are set per Hub by the Emergency Guardian or the timelock. Frozen stops new accounts and new borrowing; Paused stops more. Circuit breakers stop new exposure only. Repayment, debt-free exits, fee collection and eligible liquidations stay open in every state below.
Action
Frozen
Paused (General)
Paused (MintPathSuspect)
Wallet frozen
Breaker tripped
Base sequencer Down or Grace

Avana cannot keep exits open when Aave itself blocks them: a pause of the vault-token reserve or a Hub halt of the CDP Spoke stops withdrawals, and a pause of a debt reserve stops repayment of that reserve. Liquidation never reads a pause state, breaker or address freeze; its own rules are in
Liquidation
How to monitor an open Avana loan and change its collateral: top-ups, re-credit, partial removal and repay with collateral.

toc.title: New Account, Top-Up and Rescue Top-Up

strings: Getting Started - Deposit LP

How to pledge an exact-range Uniswap v3 position on Ethereum or an unstaked Aerodrome Slipstream position on Base into Avana as collateral: eligibility, approvals, the pledge call, top-ups, re-credit, checks, events and failures.
Overview
Eligible Positions
Approvals
The Pledge Call
New Account, Top-Up and Rescue Top-Up
Re-Credit Added Liquidity
Pledge Checks
Availability by State
What Is Minted
Events
Failures
Lens Pre-Checks
Worked Example
Positions from the canonical Uniswap v3 position manager in a listed pool, with ticks equal to the market's range.
Aerodrome Slipstream
Unstaked positions only, from the position-manager generation the market pins. Token IDs repeat across Slipstream's position managers, so the key carries the generation in its high byte.
New-account pledge
The wallet has no proxy for the market yet, or its proxy has zero debt on every debt reserve. This includes a first pledge and more collateral for a debt-free account.

Refused while the Hub is Frozen, while the sequencer gate is Down or in Grace, and while the Aave configuration has drifted. Needs a Live price (or Drifting caused only by a USD-band breach) and room in the market's Regular budget.
The proxy has non-zero debt on at least one debt reserve.

Allowed while the Hub is Frozen, during a sequencer outage or grace window, and during Aave configuration drift, because added collateral only lowers risk. Needs a Live or Drifting price. While the account's health factor is below 1.10 it may use the top-up slice.
Rescue top-up
A top-up into an account whose health factor is below the rescue target of 1.10, whose charge is at most the USD that restores 1.10, and whose value is at least the smaller of minPledgeUsd and $10.

The only pledge admitted under Paused with reason General, from a frozen wallet, while a rescue-only market breaker is tripped, above the pool-share cap, or below minPledgeUsd. All of its units are rescue units, which never support new debt.
Market status
The market is Active in the MarketRegistry, not Offboarding or Closed.
MarketNotActive / MarketOffboarding

A new-account pledge needs Live, or Drifting caused only by a USD-band breach. A top-up needs Live or Drifting. Cached and Expired are refused. Each feed is fresh while its age is at most its own heartbeat plus 1,800 seconds (88,200 seconds for a 24-hour stablecoin feed).
Sequencer gate (Base)
A new-account pledge is refused while the Base sequencer is down and for 3,600 seconds after it restarts. Top-ups are not affected. Ethereum's gate is always Up.
SequencerDown / SequencerGrace
Minimum value
The pledge's value at the served LPOracle price, rounded down, is at least minPledgeUsd ($10 per market at launch). A rescue top-up needs at least the smaller of minPledgeUsd and $10.
The regular part of the charge fits the market's Regular budget, bounded by marketUsdCap. The charge is priced at no less than stressFloorUsd ($1.00 per whole vault token), rounded up.
Token and depositor caps
The regular part fits tokenUsdCap for each pool token and depositorUsdCap for the wallet. Both caps are counted once per Hub across every CDP Spoke and market.
Top-up slice

A new-account pledge must fit the Regular budget. A top-up may book part of its charge from topUpSliceUsd (10% of marketUsdCap) only while the account's health factor is below 1.10, and only up to the USD that restores 1.10. Units booked this way are rescue units.

Avana's combined credited liquidity in the pool, across all borrowers, Spokes and markets on the chain, stays at or below poolShareMaxBps of the pool's time-weighted liquidity. The chain default is 10,000 bps (no limit); a per-pool cap applies only where the listing sets one. Only a rescue top-up may exceed it.
PoolShareExceeded / PoolShareUnavailable
Record limit
An account holds at most 16 open records per market, so liquidating any account walks at most 16 records. An account at 16 records adds collateral with recredit.

The vault-token reserve is not paused or frozen, the home Hub's entry for the Spoke is active and not halted, the Hub addCap has room for the units, and the per-user reserve limit is not reached. For a new account, no approved debt reserve is paused.
AaveReserveUnavailable / HubSpokeUnavailable / HubAddCapReached / UserReservesLimit / DebtReservePaused
Configuration drift (new accounts)
The Aave configuration matches what Avana expects, including the standard-Spoke settings, and Hub shares equal assets for the vault token. Drift never stops a top-up or a rescue top-up.
ConfigDrift / HubSharesNotEqualAssets
Pause, freeze and breakers

Paused with reason MintPathSuspect refuses every pledge. Frozen refuses new-account pledges. Paused with reason General, a frozen wallet, or a tripped rescue-only market breaker admit only a rescue top-up.
ApplicationPaused / ApplicationFrozen / NotRescueTopUp / BreakerTripped

Allowed while the price is Live or Drifting

Refused (use recredit)
Pledge value below minPledgeUsd
Allowed down to $10
Regular budget full
Allowed from the slice, up to the amount that restores HF 1.10
ProxyDeployed, UserProxyCreated
ProxyManager, AaveAdapter
First pledge into the market only; always before the proxy's first supply.
First pledge of the proxy only: the proxy is registered in the market's vault token.
Transfer (NFT), PositionReceived
Position manager, LPVault
The NFT moves from the wallet to the LPVault.
PriceAccepted, PriceStateChanged, FailureRecorded, GraceStarted
Only when the oracle poke changes stored state.
The record is written with its units, charge and slice part.
Transfer, Supply, SetUsingAsCollateral
Vault token, Hub, Spoke
Units are minted to the proxy, supplied to the CDP Spoke and enabled as collateral.
The proxy's supply is confirmed.
The pledge is complete.
RecordRecredited, CollateralRecredited
Collateralization, AaveAdapter
Another Avana call is already running in the same transaction.
The block timestamp is past the deadline.
UnknownMarket / IntegrationMismatch / UnknownSpoke
The market has no vault token, the integration is not the market's, or the CDP Spoke is not approved.
The home Hub is Paused with reason MintPathSuspect.
The home Hub is Frozen and the pledge is a new-account pledge.
The account already holds 16 open records in the market.
The caller does not own the position, including a Slipstream NFT staked in a gauge.
RangeMismatch / ShapeMismatch
The position's pool or tick range is not exactly the market's.
PoolLocked / AlreadyPledged
The pool is inside its own callback, or the position already has an open record.
ZeroLiquidity / LiquidityAboveBound
The position has no liquidity, or more than the largest creditable amount.
The market is not active.
The price state does not allow this kind of pledge.
A new-account pledge on Base during a sequencer outage or the grace window after it.
The pledge is worth less than minPledgeUsd (or less than $10 for a rescue top-up).
CapExceeded / PoolShareExceeded / PoolShareUnavailable
A cap would be exceeded, or the pool's observation history does not cover the TWAP window.
The top-up needs the slice but is a new-account pledge, the account's HF is at least 1.10, the slice part exceeds the restore amount, or the slice is used up.
NotRescueTopUp / BreakerTripped
The pledge needs a rescue exemption and does not qualify as a rescue top-up.
A new-account pledge while the Aave configuration has drifted.
AaveReserveUnavailable / HubAddCapReached / UserReservesLimit
Aave's reserve, Hub or account limits refuse the supply.
CollateralNotEnabled / SupplyIncomplete / BackingMismatch
An Adapter post-check fails; the whole transaction reverts.
Deposit LP
Pledge an exact-range AMM position into the LPVault of its AMM protocol and use it as collateral on its market's CDP Spoke. The liquidity stays in the pool and keeps earning fees for you.

A pledge moves custody of one AMM position to the LPVault of its AMM protocol on the chain. The liquidity stays in the pool and keeps earning trading fees for the depositor. In one transaction, Collateralization records the position's units as backing, the AaveAdapter mints exactly that many vault-token units to the wallet's PositionProxy, and the proxy supplies them to the market's CDP Spoke and enables them as collateral. A pledge creates no debt; borrowing is a separate call.

A market is one chain, one AMM protocol, one pool and one exact tick range. Each market is one collateral reserve on one CDP Spoke. The AaveAdapter creates one PositionProxy per wallet and market on the first pledge and reuses it afterwards, so every market is its own Aave account with its own health factor. Nothing is cross-collateralized: a wallet that uses two markets has two proxies and two health factors.

Any wallet that owns the position can pledge it, including a Safe or another smart-contract wallet. There is no EOA-only check. An approved operator cannot pledge on the owner's behalf, because the LPVault takes the position only from the calling wallet.
Two AMM protocols are listed at launch, one per chain. A position is named by the market's integration ID together with a position key.
Chain
Position key
Notes
Exact range

The position's lower and upper ticks must equal the market's range exactly. A narrower range holds far less of each token per unit of liquidity, so crediting it at the market's per-unit value would overstate it. For example, a $10,000 position on the range [−10, 10] in a USDC/USDT market whose range is [−887,272, 887,272] has about 2,000 times as many liquidity units per dollar, and would be valued at about $20,006,000. The LPVault compares the ticks exactly and refuses it, and the NFT stays with its owner.
Not accepted
Aerodrome Slipstream positions staked in a gauge. The gauge owns a staked NFT, so the staker cannot pledge it; unstake it first.
Positions in another pool of the same token pair, or on any range other than the market's exact range.
Positions from any other position contract, including forks of Uniswap v3 or Slipstream, and from position-manager generations the market does not pin.
Pools whose tokens charge a fee on transfer, rebase, or run transfer hooks. Listing excludes these tokens.
Positions with no liquidity.

Before the pledge, the wallet approves the market's LPVault for exactly that position: a per-token approve (or a permit) on the position manager for that token ID. The app never asks for an approval of all NFTs. The LPVault is immutable, moves a position only on Collateralization's instruction, and records the calling wallet as depositor, so the position can only ever return to that wallet.

The LPVault pulls the NFT with a plain transfer, without a receiver hook, so wallets without an ERC-721 receiver hook (such as a Safe) work. No vault-token, debt-asset or other ERC-20 approval is needed for a pledge.
pledge(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, uint256 deadline) returns (address proxy, uint256 recordId, uint128 credited)

The position reference holds the market's integration ID and the position key. The deadline is the last valid block timestamp, in seconds on both chains: 600 seconds is 50 Ethereum blocks or 300 Base blocks. There is no amount, proxy or recipient argument. The proxy is resolved from the caller and the market, the credited units are read from the AMM integration after custody, and the depositor of record is the caller, so no argument can inflate backing.
In order, the call:
takes the protocol lock and checks the deadline, the market, the integration ID and the home Hub's pause state;
on the wallet's first pledge into the market, deploys its PositionProxy at the address the ProxyManager predicts and registers it in the market's vault token;
applies the Frozen gate and decides whether only a rescue top-up can pass;
has Collateralization ask the LPVault to take custody, check the pool and exact range, and read the position's liquidity as the credited units;
pokes the market's LPOracle and runs the RiskModule's pledge checks;
writes the record and books its USD charge;
mints exactly the credited units to the proxy, supplies them to the CDP Spoke and enables them as collateral;
checks that the proxy holds no leftover tokens or allowance and that the market's backing gap is unchanged, then releases the lock.
Any failure reverts the whole transaction: the position stays with the wallet, and no record, mint, supply or proxy deployment persists.
All three kinds of pledge use the same entry point. The RiskModule classifies the pledge from the account's Aave borrow count at the time of the call.
Kind
When it applies
Rules

The rescue target health factor of 1.10 is the level the Lens recommends borrowing to. It is not an opening floor: Avana enforces no health factor above Aave's 1.00 when you borrow. Paused with reason MintPathSuspect refuses every pledge, rescue top-ups included, because every pledge mints vault tokens.

Anyone can add liquidity to a pledged Uniswap v3 or Slipstream position with the AMM protocol's increaseLiquidity. Added liquidity stays with the position but is not collateral until the depositor of record re-credits it:
recredit(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, bytes topUp, uint256 deadline) returns (uint128 added)

For NFT positions the topUp argument is empty. Collateralization reads the position's live liquidity and credits the units above the record's credited units. The added units run every check of a top-up of that size (or of a new-account pledge if the account has no debt), including the sequencer gate and the rescue rule. The Adapter then mints and supplies exactly the added units, and the record's charge basis is rebased so that later exits release exactly what was booked. Units admitted through the slice or a rescue exemption are rescue units.

An account that already holds 16 records adds collateral this way instead of with a new position. Before calling, the app can read the units, charge and whether only a rescue top-up can book them with the Lens view previewRecredit. If any check fails, nothing is minted or booked and the added liquidity stays with the position uncredited.

The AaveAdapter applies the call bounds, pause state and address freeze. The RiskModule applies every other check and its error reaches the caller unchanged. Example values below are launch defaults; each market's parameters are set at listing.
Check
Rule
Error

The USD charge is booked at the larger of the oracle price and the stress floor, so a pledge made while the pool trades low still consumes cap at no less than $1.00 per whole token. The Hub addCap for the vault token is sized above the market's Regular and slice budgets at that floor, so a pledge inside Avana's budget fits under it. Avana sets no limit on the number of markets per wallet.
With several states at once, the most restrictive applies. Each market is its own account, so a wallet's other markets never gate a pledge.
State
New account
Top-up
A frozen debt reserve, an exhausted credit line, a short or paused flash source and an unavailable swap route do not block any pledge.

The credited units are the position's concentrated liquidity L. The AaveAdapter mints exactly that many base units of the market's vault token to the proxy, and the proxy supplies them all to the CDP Spoke and enables the reserve as collateral. Each market has its own vault token; a whole vault token is 10^d base units, where d is the token's decimals (6 in the examples below). The LPOracle values one unit from the AMM integration's composition at oracle prices, never from spot reserves.
Uncollected fees, and any principal already owed to the position when it is pledged, are not credited. They stay owed to the position and the depositor collects them at any time.

The record stores the depositor, proxy, vault token, credited units, original units, USD charge, pledge time and rescue units. The depositor, proxy and vault token never change while the record is open.
The record joins the account's seizure list, ordered by credited units, largest first.
A debt-free account's charge stays in the market's Regular budget until it withdraws. There is no idle budget and no call that moves it.
In emission order. Indexers key positions by chain ID, integration ID and position key, and attribute Spoke events only to proxies announced by UserProxyCreated, not to the transaction sender.
Event
Contract
Meaning
Every failure reverts the whole transaction and the position stays with the wallet. Errors from the position manager, pool, Spoke and Hub pass through unchanged.
Cause
The Lens is a read-only contract, one per chain, that an app calls before signing. Its views never revert on a price state, and the pledge itself repeats every check on-chain.
getPriceState
: the market's price state, served and accepted price, and feed ages, read with the market's vault token.
getCapHeadroom
: the market, token and depositor headroom, minPledgeUsd and Aave cap headroom, read with the market's vault token and the depositor.
predictProxy
: the wallet's proxy address for the market and whether it is deployed yet.
previewRecredit
: the units a re-credit would add, their charge, and whether only a rescue top-up can book them.
getAccount
: after the pledge, the account's collateral, Aave health factor and gate status.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Market 3 is a USDC/USDT Aerodrome Slipstream market on Base, on the Aerodrome Slipstream Stable CDP Spoke of the Base Stable LP Hub, with tick spacing 1 and range [−887,272, 887,272]. One whole vault token (10^6 units) is worth $2.00. The collateral factor is 3,120 bps (31.20%), minPledgeUsd is $10 and marketUsdCap is $5,000,000 with $1,000,000 booked. The pool has an illustrative per-pool cap of 1,000 bps. Market supply is 400,000,000,000 units and the pool's in-range liquidity is 20,000,000,000,000. The Hub state is None and the sequencer gate is Up.
Carol has no proxy in market 3. She holds an unstaked Slipstream NFT with L = 10,000,000,000 (about 10,000 USDC and 10,000 USDT).

Her app reads the Lens: the market is Live (the USDC/USD feed last published 72,000 seconds ago, fresh until 88,200), Regular headroom is $4,000,000, the minimum pledge is $10, and predictProxy returns her proxy address.
She approves the Slipstream LPVault for her NFT on the Slipstream position manager, then calls pledge on market 3 with her position and a deadline of now + 600.
The ProxyManager deploys her proxy P and the vault token registers it. The LPVault checks the key's generation byte, the pool and the exact ticks, takes the NFT and reads 10,000,000,000 units.
Collateralization books $20,000 in Regular and in the USDC, USDT and depositor counters. The Adapter mints 10,000,000,000 units to P, which supplies them and enables them as collateral.
Events: ProxyDeployed, UserProxyCreated, ProxyAdded, PositionReceived, CollateralPledged, CollateralSupplied, CollateralAdded.
The account now shows collateral $20,000 and CF-weighted collateral $6,240. The Lens recommends borrowing up to $5,672.73 of debt value (HF 1.10) and shows the protocol maximum of $6,240 (HF 1.00).
Failing variants
An NFT with L = 4,000,000 is worth $8 and reverts with BelowMinPledge(800,000,000, 1,000,000,000).
A 17th record in the same market reverts with TooManyRecords.
A gauge-staked NFT reverts with NotPositionOwner.
An NFT on the range [−10, 10] reverts with RangeMismatch.
The same first pledge 1,800 seconds after a Base sequencer restart reverts with SequencerGrace.
In each failing case the NFT stays with Carol.
Top-up from the slice and rescue top-up

On an Ethereum market with the same parameters, an account owes 15,000 GHO against $50,000 of collateral, so its health factor is 15,600 / 15,000 = 1.04. The market's Regular budget is full and the Hub is Frozen. A second NFT worth $2,000 is a top-up, so the Frozen gate passes. The CF-weighted value missing to reach 1.10 is (1.10 − 1.04) × 15,000 = $900, which ⌈900 / 0.3120⌉ = $2,884.61538462 of collateral restores. The whole $2,000 books from the slice, all of its units are rescue units, and the health factor becomes $52,000 × 31.20% / 15,000 = 1.0816. A $4,000 top-up in the same state reverts with SliceNotAvailable, because its slice part exceeds $2,884.62.

The guardian then pauses the Hub with reason General. At HF 1.0816, ⌈276 / 0.3120⌉ = $884.62 restores 1.10. An $800 pledge is a rescue top-up and lifts the health factor to 1.0982. A $1,000 pledge in the same state, and a new-account pledge by another wallet, revert with NotRescueTopUp. Under reason MintPathSuspect every pledge reverts with ApplicationPaused.
The next step is to borrow against the new collateral. Continue to
Borrow Assets
How to pledge an exact-range Uniswap v3 or Aerodrome Slipstream position into Avana as collateral, what is checked and what is minted.

toc.title: Repay All with a Spend Cap

strings: Repay Loans
How to repay debt on an Avana account: the repay call, repay-all with a spend cap and refund, interest accrual, repayment by any payer, why no Avana pause can block it, failures and worked examples.
Overview
The Repay Call
Repay All with a Spend Cap
Interest Accrual
What Can Block a Repay
Repayment by Another Payer
Events
Failures
Worked Examples
The wallet whose account is repaid. It need not be the caller.
The account's market. With the borrower it names the account.
The debt reserve repaid (GHO, USDC, USDT, WETH or another reserve the Spoke lends).
The most the payer allows to be pulled in this call, in the asset's base units.
True clears the reserve's whole live debt or reverts; false repays up to the cap.
Last valid block timestamp, in seconds on both chains.
Take the protocol lock and check the deadline. The caller becomes the payer.
Resolve the borrower's proxy for the market from the Adapter's own storage.
Read the live debt D of the reserve from the Spoke: drawn debt plus premium, accrued to the block, rounded up. If D is 0, return 0 with no transfer and no event.
Size the pull: a partial repay pulls min(maxRepaySpend, D); a repay-all pulls the whole cap, or reverts before any transfer if D is above it.
Move the funds from the payer straight to the borrower's proxy and measure what arrived.
Have the proxy approve the Spoke for exactly that amount and repay its own account. Aave restores premium first, then drawn debt, and takes at most the debt.
Reset the approval to 0 and refund whatever Aave did not take to the payer, in the same call.
For a repay-all, require the reserve's debt to be 0. If the account is now debt-free on every reserve, mark it debt-free.
Emit Repaid and release the lock.
Hub None, Frozen, Paused (General) or Paused (MintPathSuspect)
Payer or borrower is a frozen address
Any market or debt breaker tripped
Base sequencer Down (forced in through L1) or in Grace
Any price state, stale feeds, USD-band breach
Market Offboarding, liquidation halted, configuration drift, Hub shares not equal to assets
Faulty MarketRegistry, RiskModule or ParameterStore
Allowed: none of them is called
Aave vault-token reserve paused or frozen, repaid reserve frozen, drawCap exhausted
Repaid debt reserve paused on Aave
Refused by Aave (ReservePaused)
The Hub halts or deactivates the CDP Spoke
Refused by Aave (SpokeHalted)
A broken AaveAdapter implementation
Refused until fixed by an Adapter upgrade through the chain's Timelock, which every proxy uses at once
Repay-all with a live debt above maxRepaySpend. It reverts before any transfer.
Repay-all left debt in the reserve, for example when a token transfer fee made the received amount smaller than the debt.
A partial repay with debt outstanding and maxRepaySpend of 0.
The borrower has no account in the market.
DeadlineExpired / LockHeld
Call bounds.
UnitsMismatch / BalanceDeltaMismatch
The proxy received 0 or more than the pulled amount, or its balance did not return to its starting value.
The payer's allowance or balance is below the amount pulled; the token's own error passes through.
ReservePaused / SpokeNotActive / SpokeHalted
Aave blocks the repay.
A third party called the Spoke's repay directly for the proxy instead of going through the AaveAdapter.
Repay any amount of one debt reserve, or all of it, through the AaveAdapter. Any address can pay, and no Avana pause, breaker, freeze, price or sequencer state can block it.

A repay moves the debt asset from the payer to the borrower's PositionProxy, which repays its own account on the CDP Spoke; Aave returns the asset to the reserve's funding Hub. The payer is always the caller. Any address can repay any account: the borrower, another wallet of the borrower, a rescue service or the protocol. A payer can never borrow or move collateral, because those calls act only on the caller's own account.

Each call repays one debt reserve of one account and leaves the account's other reserves untouched. Avana has no minimum debt, so a partial repay may leave any remainder. A repay changes no vault token, position, record or booked charge.
A borrower can also repay with liquidity from one of their own pledged positions, without bringing funds. That path is described under repay with collateral on the
Manage Loans
page.
repay(address borrower, uint256 marketId, uint256 debtReserveId, uint256 maxRepaySpend, bool repayAll, uint256 deadline) returns (uint256 spent)
Parameter
Type
Meaning
The payer approves the AaveAdapter for the debt asset beforehand; there is no permit path. The call returns the amount Aave took. In order, it does the following:

Debt keeps accruing between signing and inclusion, so a cap equal to the debt quoted at signing would always fall short. Instead, the app reads a cap quoted to the deadline from the Lens and sets both the approval and maxRepaySpend to it:
quoteRepayAll(borrower, marketId, debtReserveId, deadline) = ⌈debt × (1 + rate × (deadline − now)) × 1.001⌉

A repay-all pulls the whole cap, Aave takes the live debt at inclusion, and the proxy refunds the difference to the payer in the same call. The payer never spends more than it signed for, and an approval of exactly the cap ends at 0, so no standing allowance remains. If another payer repays first, the borrower's own repay-all only pays what is left.
To repay every debt reserve and take a position back in one call, use repayAllAndWithdraw, described in
Withdraw Collateral

Interest is Aave V4's and accrues every second: the reserve's drawn rate on its funding Hub plus the account's risk premium. The live debt read by a repay is drawn debt plus premium, accrued to the block and rounded up. A repay restores premium first, then drawn debt; when the drawn shares reach 0 the reserve is no longer marked as borrowed.
Avana takes no fee on interest and the repay call charges no fee. Avana Labs charges an app fee in its own app, outside the contracts; calling the contracts directly does not pay it.

Example values: 5,000 USDC borrowed at 6.00% is ⌈5,000,000,000 × (1 + 0.06 × 30 / 365)⌉ = 5,024,657,535 base units (5,024.657535 USDC) after 30 days. 8,000 GHO at 5.00% is 8,032.876712 GHO after 30 days.

Repay never reads a pause state, a circuit breaker, the address freeze, the sequencer gate or any other MarketRegistry view, and never calls the RiskModule, an oracle or the ParameterStore. The account binding (Spoke, vault token, reserve) comes from the Adapter's own storage written when the proxy was created. So no Avana pause, breaker, freeze, price state or registry fault can block a repay; only Aave can.
State
Repay with funds

The proxy holds no logic and has no upgrade path; it only forwards the Adapter's calls. Aave's listing agreement uses a reserve freeze and a drawCap of 0 for containment, which leave repayment open, and keeps reserve pauses and Spoke halts for a faulty Spoke.

Any payer repays through the AaveAdapter with the borrower's address. The funds are pulled from the payer, never from the borrower, and any refund goes back to the payer. This lets a borrower's other wallets, a rescue service or the protocol save an account near liquidation, including one whose key is lost.
Calling the Spoke's repay directly for a proxy fails with Unauthorized, because Aave accepts repayment only from the position owner or an approved position manager, and proxies approve none.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. On Ethereum, a rescue service R repays 3,000 GHO of wallet W's market-A account while the Avana Stable LP Hub is Paused with reason MintPathSuspect, a GHO debt breaker is tripped and W is a frozen address. The call reads none of these states: 3,000 GHO are pulled from R, W's debt falls to 5,032.88 GHO, the event is Repaid with R as payer and W as borrower, and W's collateral does not move. If W's own repay-all with a cap of 8,040 GHO lands later in the same block, Aave takes only the remaining 5,032.876712 GHO and W gets 3,007.123288 GHO back.
The asset's Transfer from the payer to the proxy, and the proxy's approval of the Spoke.
Hub Restore and Spoke Repay, in Aave's order.
The approval reset and, when non-zero, the refund Transfer from the proxy to the payer.
Collateralization's DebtFree, only when the account is left with no debt on any reserve.
Repaid(payer, borrower, marketId, debtReserveId, spent, debtAfter, repayAll)
Error
Cause
A repay at zero debt, including debt another payer or a liquidation cleared first, is not a failure: it returns 0 with no token movement.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Carol's account in market 3 on Base, 30 days after she borrowed 5,000 USDC at 6.00%: live debt 5,024,657,535 base units, HF 6,240 / (5,024.657535 × 0.9999) = 1.2420.
Repay all

Carol approves the AaveAdapter for exactly 5,029,687,935 USDC base units and calls repay(Carol, 3, r_USDC, 5,029,687,935, true, now + 600). No pause state, breaker, freeze, price or sequencer gate is read.
The call is included 4 seconds (2 Base blocks) later, when the live debt is 5,024,657,573.
The Adapter pulls 5,029,687,935 into Carol's proxy; Aave takes 5,024,657,573; 5,030,362 is returned to Carol in the same call.
The account has no debt left, so Collateralization marks it debt-free. Event Repaid(Carol, Carol, 3, r_USDC, 5,024,657,573, 0, true). Carol's allowance to the Adapter is 0.
Carol's $20,000 charge stays booked until she withdraws; her NFTs can now leave through a debt-free withdrawal.
Variants
A partial repay of 2,000 USDC leaves 3,024,657,535; any remainder is accepted because there is no minimum debt.
A repay-all with a cap of 5,020,000,000 reverts with RepayExceedsMax(5,024,657,535, 5,020,000,000) before any transfer.
A repay-all that leaves debt in the reserve reverts with DebtRemaining.
While the Base sequencer is down, Carol can force the same repay in from L1 and it succeeds.
On Ethereum, the same quote included 24 seconds (2 blocks) later finds a debt of 5,024,657,765 and refunds 5,030,170.
A repay after a liquidation already cleared the debt returns 0 with no transfer, approval or event.
The third-party example above shows a rescue service repaying while the Hub is paused, a breaker is tripped and the borrower is frozen.
How to repay part or all of a debt reserve on Avana, by any payer, in every Avana pause state.

Allowed after reconcile
The units argument is not the record's credited units after reconcile. Read it from previewRelease.
Units of 0; a record with no credited units uses releaseZeroCredit.
NoProxy / UnknownMarket / IntegrationMismatch
The wallet has no account in the market, or the position reference is not the market's.
RecordNotFound / NotRecordProxy / InvalidVaultToken
Debt remains and the home Hub is Paused.
Debt remains and the wallet is frozen.
Debt remains and the Base sequencer is down or within its grace window.

BreakerTripped / DebtBreakerTripped / LiquidationHalted / ConfigDrift

Aave refuses a withdrawal that would leave its health factor below 1.00.
