repayAllAndWithdraw left debt on a reserve the call did not name.
The reserve and cap arrays differ in length.
NotDepositor / RecordHasCredit
A zero-credit release by someone other than the depositor, or for a record that still has credited units.
Reconcile on exit needed to unwind units while the pool was inside its own callback.
The market's backing gap changed; the whole call reverts.
ReservePaused / SpokeHalted / SpokeNotActive
Aave blocks the withdrawal; handled by an emergency playbook with the Aave Guardian.
Take a whole pledged position back, with its fees. A debt-free account can always leave; an account with debt can leave while it stays healthy and the withdraw-with-debt checks pass.

A withdrawal closes one record: the proxy withdraws exactly the record's credited units from the CDP Spoke, the AaveAdapter burns them, Collateralization releases the record and its USD charge, and the LPVault returns the whole position to the depositor of record. Only the wallet whose proxy holds the record, which is always its depositor, can withdraw it. Nobody else, including governance and keepers, can move a position that has a record.
Call
Partial removal is described in
Manage Loans
withdraw(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, uint256 units, uint256 deadline, uint256 minHealthFactor)
The position reference names the record's position by integration ID and position key. One position per call.
The units must equal the record's credited units after reconcile, read from Collateralization's previewRelease. The whole position is released, never part of it.
The deadline is a timestamp: 600 seconds is 300 Base blocks or 50 Ethereum blocks.
The minimum health factor applies only when debt remains; 0 means no extra bound.

The market's vault token, Spoke and reserve come from the Adapter's own binding and the vault token's immutables, with no MarketRegistry read, so a faulty registry can neither block the exit nor substitute another token.

The account is debt-free when Aave reports a borrow count of 0 for the proxy. Aave's count covers every reserve the account owes, so a registry that lists no debt reserves cannot make an indebted account look debt-free.
Debt-free

No pause state, circuit breaker, address freeze, sequencer gate, price, MarketRegistry view or RiskModule check is read. A debt-free withdrawal works in every Avana state and every price state. Only Aave can stop it, by pausing the vault-token reserve or halting the CDP Spoke. When the last record leaves, the reserve is disabled as collateral for the proxy.
With debt

Collateral that leaves an indebted account can no longer be seized, so a withdrawal with debt is closed whenever liquidation of the account could not run or a breaker stops new exposure. The checks are the borrow checks without the Offboarding and Aave-frozen refusals:
Check
Rule
Error

The health check runs after the record is released, with the account's remaining rescue units valued at zero. In an Offboarding market Aave applies the ramped-down liquidation threshold, so a withdrawal with debt needs more remaining collateral as the ramp advances.
repayAllAndWithdraw(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, uint256 units, uint256[] debtReserveIds, uint256[] maxRepaySpends, uint256 deadline)

For each named debt reserve the call runs a repay-all with the caller as payer and borrower, under that reserve's own cap, and refunds the unused part in the same call. The app sets each cap, and its approval, to the Lens quoteRepayAll value. If Aave still reports any debt, the call reverts with DebtRemaining for the first borrowed reserve. Otherwise it makes a debt-free withdrawal.

It reads no pause state, breaker, freeze, sequencer gate, price or MarketRegistry view and calls no RiskModule function. It therefore works under a Frozen or Paused Hub, under any breaker, for a frozen wallet and during a Base sequencer grace window. Any failure reverts all of it.
releaseZeroCredit(uint256 marketId, PositionRef position, uint256 deadline)

When a record has no credited units left, normally after a full seizure, the depositor of record takes the position back with this call. It mints, burns and supplies nothing, makes no Spoke withdrawal and no debt check, and reads no pause state, freeze, breaker or price. It is available in every Avana and Aave state, every sequencer state and in a Closed market. The position returns with its uncollected fees and any liquidity donated to it.

Inside every withdrawal, zero-credit release and partial removal, Collateralization compares the account's credited units with its Aave supply. Supply can only fall below credit if a seizure was never settled. In every normal exit the two match and nothing is written.

When units are missing, Collateralization debits the account's records largest-first by the missing amount, unwinds those units into the market's pending-settlement balance and releases their charge. The seized vault tokens in circulation stay backed by the tokens in that balance. A record debited to 0 stays open, so its depositor can still collect fees and use releaseZeroCredit. Anyone can later call LPVaultSwap's settlePending, which burns the stranded vault tokens, converts the pending tokens into the market's settlement debt asset and funds that asset's Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke). The borrower and the caller receive nothing from it.
The position itself: for Uniswap v3 and Slipstream, the NFT, transferred from the LPVault to the depositor of record without a receiver hook. A Slipstream NFT returns unstaked, as it was pledged.
Its uncollected fees and any principal owed to it. The withdrawal neither collects nor unwinds, so these travel with the NFT and the depositor collects them directly from the AMM protocol.
Any liquidity donated to the position and never re-credited.
The record's USD charge is released from the market's budget (slice part first, then Regular) and from the token and depositor counters.

For a withdrawal with debt, the most restrictive state over the account's market and every debt reserve it owes applies. No Avana pause, breaker or freeze reaches pending settlement or liquidation in any row.
State
Debt-free withdraw, remove or repayAllAndWithdraw
Withdraw or remove with debt
Zero-credit release
With debt: LPOracle and DebtOracle state events when a poke changes stored state.
Hub Remove and Spoke Withdraw; the vault token's Transfer to the proxy and its burn.
CollateralDisabled, when a debt-free account's last record leaves the reserve.
RecordDebited and SeizureReconciled, only when reconcile on exit found missing units.
The NFT's Transfer to the depositor, then LPVault PositionReturned and Collateralization CollateralReleased.
CollateralWithdrawn(wallet, marketId, vaultToken, positionKey, units, withDebt, healthFactorAfter)
The health factor in CollateralWithdrawn is the maximum uint256 value on the debt-free branch. repayAllAndWithdraw first emits one Repaid per reserve that moved funds.
Every failure reverts the whole transaction; the record, counters, tokens and position stay as they were.
Cause

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Carol's account in market 3 (USDC/USDT, Aerodrome Slipstream on Base, $2.00 per whole vault token, collateral factor 31.20%) holds two records: key1 with 10,000,000,000 units ($20,000) and a top-up keyB with 2,500,000,000 units ($5,000). Collateral is $25,000, CF-weighted $7,800, debt 5,000 USDC valued at $4,999.50, so HF = 7,800 / 4,999.50 = 1.5602. Both feeds last published 30,000 seconds ago (fresh until 88,200), the Hub is in state None and the sequencer gate is Up.
The app reads getAccount and getPriceState: market Live, and removing keyB leaves CF-weighted $6,240 and HF 1.2481.
Carol calls withdraw(3, (I, keyB), 2,500,000,000, now + 600, 1.20e18). The units come from previewRelease.
The account has debt (borrow count 1), so the gates run: Hub not Paused, Carol not frozen, then the RiskModule pre-check finds the sequencer Up, both oracles Live and no breaker tripped.
The proxy withdraws 2,500,000,000 units from the Spoke and the Adapter burns them.
Collateralization closes record keyB and releases its $5,000 charge. The LPVault returns the NFT to Carol with every fee it has accrued.
Events PositionReturned, CollateralReleased and CollateralWithdrawn with HF 1,248,124,812,481,248,124. Carol now holds one record, collateral $20,000.
Failing case and the debt-free route
Withdrawing key1 instead leaves CF-weighted $1,560 and HF 1,560 / 4,999.50 = 0.3120, so Aave reverts with HealthFactorBelowThreshold.

1,200 seconds after a sequencer restart, withdraw reverts with SequencerGrace. repayAllAndWithdraw(3, (I, keyB), 2,500,000,000, [r_USDC], [cap], now + 600) repays the USDC debt and returns the NFT at once, because a debt-free exit reads no gate.

The same withdrawal while the Hub is Paused, while Carol is frozen, or while the market's pool-share breaker is tripped reverts with ApplicationPaused, AddressIsFrozen or BreakerTripped; repayAllAndWithdraw succeeds in each of these states. Under a Frozen Hub the withdrawal with debt succeeds.
How the repay-all cap is quoted is explained in
Repay Loans
How to take a pledged position back from Avana, with and without debt, and what you receive.

meta.title: Allowed LP Pools
meta.description: Which pools and ranges Avana lists as collateral at launch, the listing criteria and excluded tokens, the AMM integration interface, Uniswap v3 and Aerodrome Slipstream specifics, and the guards for AMMs that are not yet listed.

strings: Allowed LP Pools

Which pools and ranges Avana lists as collateral at launch, the listing criteria and excluded tokens, the AMM integration interface, Uniswap v3 and Aerodrome Slipstream specifics, and the guards for AMMs that are not yet listed.
Overview
Launch Markets
Market = Pool + Exact Range
Listing Criteria
Collateral Factor
Excluded Tokens
AMM Integration Interface
Uniswap v3 Specifics
Aerodrome Slipstream Specifics
AMMs Not Yet Listed
Avana lists one exact pool and tick range at a time. Each market passes its AMM protocol's listing rules, a five-day public review and an on-chain match check before it accepts collateral.

Avana launches on Ethereum and Base, each with one Avana Stable LP Hub. Uniswap v3 positions are accepted on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base. Correlated LP and Volatile LP Hubs can be added later, each with its own CDP Spokes.

A pool is not approved as a whole. Each market is one pool plus one exact position shape, with its own vault token, collateral reserve, price feed, caps and swap routes. The core design also supports Uniswap v2, Curve StableSwap-NG, Balancer and Uniswap v4, but none of them is listed until its integration passes the guards described below.
How a market is registered, activated, offboarded and closed is described on the market lifecycle page:
Market Lifecycle
Chain
CDP Spoke
Positions
Ethereum
Avana Stable LP Hub
Uniswap v3 Stable
Uniswap v3 NFT positions of the canonical position manager
Base
Aerodrome Slipstream Stable
Unstaked Aerodrome Slipstream NFT positions of an allowlisted position-manager generation

Launch pools are stablecoin pools that meet the listing rules, including USDC/USDT and pools containing GHO. Every token of a Stable LP Hub market is an approved USD-pegged stable, so its price is capped at $1 for valuation and the USD band applies.
GHO pools: the collateral factor of a GHO leg is an explicit value,
ghoLegCollateralFactorBps
, set per token in the listing payload (between 1 and 9,999 bps), used in place of an Aave Core Hub value.
GHO markets stay Live while GHO trades above $1, because valuation and the band's upper bound use the capped price.
GHO is the first debt asset of each CDP Spoke. USDC, USDT or WETH can be enabled per Spoke as further debt reserves.

For concentrated liquidity, a market fixes one tick range, which can be the full usable range or a bounded one. A pledge is accepted only when the position's lower and upper ticks equal the market's exactly. A position wider or narrower by any number of ticks is never credited. Without this rule, a narrow-range position worth $10,000 would be credited at the market's per-unit value, about 979 times too high.
The pool is derived from the position itself through the integration's pinned factory; a caller-supplied pool is never used.
Both ticks must be aligned to the pool's tick spacing using signed arithmetic. A check on an unsigned cast would accept misaligned negative ticks, such as −516 for spacing 10.
Both ticks must lie inside the usable range for the spacing, and the lower tick must be below the upper tick.
At most one market exists per CDP Spoke, pool and range. The same pool and range can be listed again only on another CDP Spoke.

Before a listing is scheduled, the Aave V4 risk service providers publish a listing package with numeric thresholds and evidence for each rule: pool age, TVL, depth, feed heartbeat and deviation, stress slippage, a manipulation-cost study, a TWAP tolerance backtest, a shock table for the market's exact range and a cap stress test.
Area
Rule
Pool
Created by the integration's pinned factory, with a standard tick spacing and sufficient liquidity history
Price feeds
For each token, a primary direct TOKEN/USD Chainlink feed, an independent alternate route and a standby route, each leg with its published heartbeat recorded
Second source
For each token, an independent second source (another oracle network, or a TWAP of a deep pool other than the market's own) whose history over past stress periods stayed within its tolerance
TWAP history
The pool's observation buffer covers the 1,800-second window at the chain's block time: 151 observations on Ethereum, 901 on Base. Avana pays to raise it at listing.
Manipulation cost
The pool's liquidity within the studied price band is at least the minimum a per-pool manipulation-cost study sets
Listing margin
One minus the collateral factor exceeds the feed deviation threshold plus heartbeat drift
Swap routes

For each pool token and each debt asset the Spoke lends, a primary and a backup swap route, each proven deep at stress size with the range fully one-sided. No route trades through the market's own pool.
Issuer probe
Each token records a probe: a pause flag for issuers that can pause transfers (USDC), the fee rate for USDT, none otherwise (GHO, DAI)
Caps
Market, token and depositor USD caps, a pool-share limit (10% of the pool by default) and the Hub add cap, set by the risk service providers
Minimum pledge
$10 per pledge at launch, so every record is worth its liquidation gas
Records
At most 16 records per account and market, so one liquidation of the largest account fits in a transaction
Vault-token value
One whole vault token must be worth between $0.50 and $20.00 at activation
Token count
Between 2 and 8 tokens per pool, the limit set by
MAX_POOL_TOKENS
The LPOracle values each position with no haircut. All risk adjustment is in the reserve's collateral factor, computed over the market's tokens:
CF = ⌊min(CFᵢ) × poolRiskFactor⌋
Each token's factor is its Aave V4 Core Hub collateral factor, the explicit GHO leg factor, or for a token without a Core Hub factor, a value the risk service providers set.
The pool risk factor has a ceiling of 0.40.

Example: token factors of 78% and a pool risk factor of 0.40 give a collateral factor of 31.2%. That is a maximum loan-to-value of 31.2% at health factor 1.00 and a recommended 28.4% at the Lens's health factor of 1.10.
The LPVaults, Collateralization and LPVaultSwap account by received balances and forward every token in the same call, so tokens that change balances on their own are excluded:
Fee-on-transfer tokens
Rebasing tokens
Tokens with transfer hooks
Tokens whose transfer returns false instead of reverting

Native ETH is held as WETH, and a rate token such as a liquid staking token is priced through its rate feed times the underlying feed. USDC and USDT are accepted issuer-upgradeable exceptions with monitoring and an issuer probe.

USDT's fee rate must be 0 at listing. Every amount Avana receives is measured by balance change, so if the fee is switched on later, settlement and repay complete at the reduced amounts while the issuer breaker stops new exposure to the token.

An AMM integration is Avana's code for one AMM protocol on one chain: one immutable LPVault that holds every pledged position of that protocol, plus the pricing library compiled into both the LPVault and the protocol's LPOracle implementation. The core (Collateralization, vault tokens, the AaveAdapter, LPVaultSwap and the LPOracle base) depends only on this interface. Adding an AMM protocol adds one LPVault, one pricing library and one LPOracle implementation; nothing else changes.
Part
Functions
Used for
Custody
bindMarket, receivePosition, validatePosition, topUpPosition, returnPosition, returnStray
Binding a market at listing; taking, checking and returning positions
Composition
composition
Token amounts a number of units holds at an oracle price vector, from oracle prices only
Unwind
unwind, releaseToDepositor, unitsOf
Removing exactly the given units for seizure, repay with collateral and partial removal
Fees
collectFees
Paying accrued fees to the depositor of record
Risk metadata
riskMetadata, riskStatus, checkReadSafe, consistencyDeviation
Range status, pool lock, pool share and time-weighted depth for the RiskModule, the LPOracle and the Lens
Every record, event and index is keyed by the integration identifier and a position key, never by a bare NFT token ID.
One vault-token base unit is backed by one credited unit: liquidity for concentrated liquidity, LP-token base units for fungible LP shares.
checkReadSafe
reverts while the pool is inside its own reentrancy lock; Collateralization calls it before every custody, read and removal, and the LPOracle before every quote.
The LPVault accepts positions of the canonical NonfungiblePositionManager only, never a fork. Its position key is the token ID.

A market's pool must come from the canonical factory and match the address derived from the factory's init code hash. Tick spacing must be that of a standard fee tier: fee 100 → 1, 500 → 10, 3,000 → 60, 10,000 → 200.
Every custody, removal and liquidity read under the Lock checks the pool's 7-field slot0 and reverts with
PoolLocked
The borrower approves the LPVault for that one token ID, or signs a position-manager permit. The LPVault pulls with a plain transfer, so wallets without a receiver hook work.

A removal decreases liquidity and immediately collects only the principal it returned, so fees stay owed to the NFT. Fee collection pays all owed amounts to the depositor of record, including principal left owed before the pledge, which was never credited.
An NFT sent to the LPVault outside a pledge is never credited; the timelock can return it.
Slipstream reuses the Uniswap v3 tick and liquidity math, so every Uniswap v3 rule applies with the position manager and factory of the market's pinned generation in their place. The differences:
Uniswap v3
Slipstream
Pool lookup
By fee
Position field 5
Signed tick spacing, decoded with Slipstream's own layout
slot0
7 fields
6 fields; the lock flag is field 6, so a v3 decoder would read the wrong word
Swap fee
Fixed by the fee tier
Dynamic; always read live from the pool, never derived from the spacing
Position managers
Three generations, each with its own factory, fixed in the LPVault's immutable allowlist
Staking
None
Gauge-staked positions are refused
Tick spacings
Any spacing the factory enables, for example 1, 50, 100, 200, 2000

Generation-prefixed position key: the position key carries the generation in its high byte, so the LPVault always calls the right position manager even though token IDs overlap between generations. A pledge from another generation reverts with
PoolMismatch
Unstaked positions only: a pledge reverts with
PositionEncumbered
when the owner is a gauge. The LPVault never stakes or approves a custodied NFT, so a pledged position stays unstaked until it returns to its depositor.
Lock check: every custody, removal and quote reverts with
Fees of an unstaked position are reduced by the pool's staked share and its unstaked fee. Fees are never collateral, so this changes only the borrower's yield, which the Lens reports per market.

The interface supports four more AMM protocols. No market of any of them is listed until its integration page, fork tests of every guard on its chain and its seizure gas measurement exist, followed by risk review and governance approval. Every one also needs the per-block quote-change cap.
Pricing
Guards before listing
Uniswap v2
Fair reserves at the oracle ratio, 2·√(r0·r1·p0·p1) per effective supply
Reserves read only through
getReserves()

, never from token balances; supply includes the pending protocol-fee mint; borrowing refused while the spot price is more than 1% off the oracle ratio; minimum supply; quote-change cap at most 1%; consistency from cumulative prices
Curve StableSwap-NG
Lower bound: the cheapest coin's price × D per supply

Reentrancy-locked pool call before every read; a reverting D is a price failure; no rate token without a capped rate feed; native ETH wrapped; at most 8 coins; consistency from the pool's price oracle
Balancer weighted and stable
Weighted invariant per actual supply; stable pools as Curve
Vault reentrancy check before every read; actual supply including pending fee BPT; feed-only consistency check for weighted pools
Uniswap v4
As Uniswap v3, over the position's range

Hook-free pool or an allowlisted immutable hook with no remove-liquidity hooks and no deltas; no subscribed positions; pool manager must be locked for every read; feed-only consistency check unless the hook is an oracle hook
Uniswap v2, Curve and Balancer positions are fungible LP shares. Their LPVault books one custody entry per deposit, and fees compound into the pool, so fee collection reverts with
FeesRolledIn
Pools hold between 2 and 8 tokens. Every n-token array in the oracle, RiskModule and Collateralization is bounded by

Tokenized stocks with market-hours feeds are not listed at launch. A future listing must stop new borrowing while the reference market is closed, pause new activity around corporate actions, and have the issuer allowlist every Avana contract that holds the token.
Launch markets, listing criteria, excluded tokens and AMM integration rules.

meta.title: AppKit
meta.description: How AppKit passes wallet and market context from a partner application into Avana's borrowing flow, and what stays in the contracts.

strings: AppKit
How AppKit passes wallet and market context from a partner application into Avana's borrowing flow, and what stays in the contracts.
Overview
Integration Model
Partner Controls
Implementation Notes
Launch Notes
How partners link users into Avana's borrowing flow from their own position views. Borrowing, risk and liquidation rules stay in the contracts.

AppKit connects DEXs, wallets and portfolio applications to Avana's LP-backed borrowing flow on Ethereum and Base. The partner application chooses where the entry point appears and passes the user's wallet and market context. Borrowing itself runs through the AaveAdapter and the market's CDP Spoke on Aave V4: GHO first, and USDC, USDT or WETH where a CDP Spoke has enabled them.

AppKit is a frontend integration. It does not change which pools are listed, how positions are valued or how they are liquidated. Users can also call the contracts directly, without AppKit or Avana's frontend.
Intent capture

A partner places the borrowing entry point beside an LP position, portfolio or swap view. That view supplies the position and market context for the handoff. Only Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and unstaked Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base whose tick range matches a listed market exactly can be pledged.
Protocol handoff

The partner passes the wallet, chain and market into Avana so the borrowing flow opens with the relevant account and market selected. Each wallet has one account per market, so the market fixes the account the user will borrow on.
Partner economics
Any partner arrangement is off-chain. No contract carries a borrow, interest or frontend fee, and partner arrangements do not change Aave V4 borrowing terms, risk parameters or liquidation rules.

Partners control how the borrowing entry point is presented and the guidance around it. Those choices affect how users reach the flow. Collateral eligibility, price states and every transaction check stay in Avana's contracts and Aave V4.
Where the credit surface appears in the product
Which user segments see the borrow entry point
How much education or explanation appears alongside the handoff
Whether the product uses a full embedded handoff or a lighter context-preserving entry point

An AppKit integration connects an existing position view to the matching Avana borrowing flow. These notes cover context transfer and the boundary between the partner interface and Avana's protocol operations.
Read account, price-state, cap and preview data from the Lens rather than recomputing collateral values or health factors in the partner interface.
Show the recommended borrow at health factor 1.10 next to the protocol maximum at 1.00, as the Lens returns them.
Build transactions with the calldata builders in
packages/protocol
from the verified deployment manifest. Never take a transaction target or calldata from a backend.

Request only exact approvals: one position to the market's LPVault for a pledge, and the exact repay amount to the AaveAdapter for a repay. Never an operator approval for all tokens or an unlimited allowance.
Show when a market is not Live, a Hub is paused or frozen, or a breaker is tripped, so users understand why a pledge or borrow would revert.
The full integration guide, with contracts, approvals and events, is on the integrations overview:
Integrations

Before enabling the integration, verify the complete path from the partner's position view to Avana's borrowing flow on each chain. The interface must make the selected account, the market and the transition to Avana clear.

Include hidden entry points, direct links, positions whose range does not match a listed market, staked Slipstream positions, and missing wallet, market or collateral context in that review. These cases decide whether the flow opens with the information needed to evaluate a borrow.
Developer integration guide for embedding AppKit inside partner product surfaces.

meta.title: Lens
meta.description: The Lens is Avana's read-only periphery contract: single-call views of accounts, markets, prices, risk and liquidation, and previews sized to stay valid until a transaction's deadline.

strings: Lens
The Lens is Avana's read-only periphery contract: single-call views of accounts, markets, prices, risk and liquidation, and previews sized to stay valid until a transaction's deadline.
Overview
Account Views
Market Views
Price and State Views
Risk Views
Liquidation Preview
Borrower Previews
Constants and Errors
Example Session
A read-only view contract, one per chain, for the app, keepers, monitoring and the public backing proof. Every result is advisory; the target contract re-checks it.

The Lens is an immutable, read-only periphery contract, one per chain. It gathers state from every Avana contract, the CDP Spokes, Hubs and oracles into single-call views, and returns previews that carry the margins needed to stay valid between the block they were read at and the block that includes the transaction.

The Lens sits outside the audited core. No core contract calls it, stores its address or depends on what it returns, and nothing it returns authorizes an action. A Lens bug can mislead a user or keeper into a transaction that reverts or pays less than shown; it cannot move value. It is reviewed and tested as periphery.
A new Lens is a new deployment, made when a dependency's interface changes. Replacing it needs no governance action; the verified deployment manifest records the address consumers use.
Every returned struct carries the block number and timestamp it was read at. The Lens emits no events and moves no tokens.
Every view reverts with
Locked
while an Avana call holds the protocol Lock, so no view reads half-updated state.
Positions are named by the AMM integration's position key: the token ID for Uniswap v3, and the generation-prefixed token ID for Aerodrome Slipstream.
Function
Arguments
Returns
predictProxy
wallet, marketId
The wallet's proxy address for the market and whether it is deployed. The address is exact before deployment, so an app can show an account before it exists.
getAccount
The account view: proxy, borrow nonce, Aave account data, debt in each approved debt reserve, gate status, the market position, breaker reasons, rescue units and whether the wallet is frozen
getRecords
proxy, offset, limit
One page of the account's records (at most 16) in seizure-list order, with credited units after reconciliation
getEscrowClaimable
account, tokens
Unclaimed payouts held for the account by the payout escrow, one amount per requested token
checkBacking
vaultToken
The market-level backing check and the Aave configuration check, including the three standard-Spoke settings, as raw values and pass or fail flags
checkRecordBacking
vaultToken, offset, limit
For one page of record IDs: custody of each position and its live liquidity against its credited units
getPendingSettlement
The pending-settlement balance of reconciled seizures and whether LPVaultSwap holds enough units to settle it
getCapHeadroom
vaultToken, depositor
Avana USD cap headroom (market, token, depositor, pool share), the minimum pledge value, top-up slice headroom, the Hub add-cap headroom and the draw-cap headroom of every approved debt reserve
getPriceState

The market's price state, liquidation state, reasons, served and accepted prices, input ages against both age limits, deviations, the disagreement pause and its expiry, the grace window and the sequencer status. Served is at most accepted whenever the state is not Live.
getDebtPriceState
spoke, debtReserveId
A debt reserve's Aave price source, price, source timestamp, age and freshness flags for borrowing and liquidation. A fixed source such as GHO reports age 0 and both flags true.
getApplicationState
The Hub's pause state: None, Frozen or Paused
getPauseReason
The pause reason: 0 None, 1 General (rescue top-ups only), 2 MintPathSuspect (every pledge, top-up and re-credit refused)
Liquidation, pending settlement, repay, fee collection and debt-free withdrawal are open in every pause state. The meaning of each price state is on the price states page:
Price States
getBreakerStatus
marketId
The market breaker's reason bitmap (conditions true now, temporary gates still recovering, latched freezes) and when the last temporary gate reopens. A tripped breaker blocks only new activity.
getDebtBreakerStatus
The same for a debt reserve
isFrozenAddress
account
Whether the address is frozen in the MarketRegistry
getTailCoverage
debtAsset
The funded First-Loss Reserve of a debt asset against its largest one-token tail exposure: funded balance, minimum, worst token, exposure and coverage ratio. Rounding never overstates coverage.
uncoveredDeficit
hub, asset
The deficit the Hub has recorded for the asset above what its Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke) holds
getHubAssetExposure
The exposure of a Hub and asset across every Spoke drawing on it, with its coverage check
previewLiquidation(proxy, debtReserveId, deadline)

returns every liquidation gate, Aave's sizing and ready-to-send liquidation parameters for one account, its market and one debt reserve, with the expected seizure, flash amount and premium, recovery floor and payouts, all in the debt asset. A caller without keeper tooling can submit a correct call from it.
Gates read fresh prices only for the seized market and the repaid debt reserve; the account's other reserves count at their served prices.
The expected repayment follows the pinned Aave V4 liquidation formulas: target health factor, dynamic bonus, caps and the dust rule.
When the expected repayment is the whole debt, the whole collateral is seized, or the remainder would be close to Aave's dust threshold, the debt to cover is the whole debt plus 5% (
LENS_DUST_MARGIN_BPS

The parameters use a flash loan for the whole amount, capped by the flash source's available liquidity with the rest funded by the caller. The route mode is primary-then-backup when every primary swap route is usable, otherwise backup only.
All amounts are 0 when the account's health factor is at least 1.00.
The preview is advisory: LPVaultSwap recomputes and enforces every check, Aave sizes the seizure inside its liquidation call, and settlement uses balance deltas, never a preview.
previewBorrowMax
wallet, marketId, debtReserveId, deadline

The protocol maximum: the largest borrow that keeps the health factor at 1.00 (or the market's optional hard floor) once debt has grown until the deadline, with a 0.5% margin. Capped by draw-cap headroom; 0 when any borrow gate fails.
previewBorrowRecommended
The recommended borrow at health factor 1.10 next to the protocol maximum. A display value; no contract enforces it.
quoteRepayAll
borrower, marketId, debtReserveId, deadline
The spend cap and approval amount for a repay-all included by the deadline: the debt grown to the deadline plus 0.1%, rounded up. The Adapter refunds the unused part in the same call.
previewRecredit
marketId, positionKey
The units a re-credit would add, their cap charge at the last accepted price, and whether only a rescue top-up could book them
previewRepayWithCollateral
wallet, marketId, positionKey, units, debtReserveId
Debt repaid, debt asset returned to the wallet and the health factor after, at the block's prices. Returns zeros and the current health factor when the call would revert.
Example: $100,000 of collateral at a 70% collateral factor and no debt gives a borrowing capacity of $70,000, the maximum at health factor 1.00. The recommended borrow is $70,000 / 1.10 = $63,636.
Constant
Value
LENS_MAX_PAGE
500 bps
RECOMMENDED_HEALTH_FACTOR
BORROW_MAX_MARGIN_BPS
50 bps (the 1.005 factor)
REPAY_ALL_MARGIN_BPS
10 bps (the 1.001 factor)
Error
Raised when
An Avana call is in flight
LimitTooHigh
UnknownProxy
The address is not a registered proxy of the market
UnknownDebtReserve
The debt reserve is not approved for the Spoke
UnknownDebtAsset
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. Carol uses market 3, a USDC/USDT Aerodrome Slipstream market on Base, with a collateral factor of 31.2% and USDC priced at $0.9999.

Before pledging, the app reads the price state (Live; USDC/USD 72,000 seconds old, fresh until 88,200), the cap headroom ($4,000,000 of room, minimum pledge $10), the Hub's pause state (None) and her predicted proxy address.
After a $20,000 pledge, the account view shows $20,000 of collateral, $6,240 weighted by the collateral factor, and no debt; the records view lists one record of 10,000,000,000 units.
On the borrow screen, the recommended borrow is 5,673.29 USDC (6,240 / 1.10 / 0.9999) and the maximum is 6,209.56 USDC (6,240 / 1.0050011 / 0.9999).
On the repay screen, the repay-all quote for 5,024.657535 USDC of debt is 5,029.687935 USDC; the app sets both the approval and the spend cap to it.

A keeper's liquidation preview for another account returns the gates, 1,950 USDC to cover, a 1,950 USDC flash loan with a 0.975 USDC premium, 975 expected seized vault tokens and ready-to-send parameters.
Read-only Lens views for accounts, markets, prices, risk, liquidation and borrower previews.

meta.description: How a market is deployed, registered, activated, frozen, offboarded and closed: the deployment operations, timelock delays, the offboarding ramp and relisting.

strings: Market Lifecycle
How a market is deployed, registered, activated, frozen, offboarded and closed: the deployment operations, timelock delays, the offboarding ramp and relisting.
Overview
States and Transitions
Deployment Operations
Listing Steps
Activation
Timelock Delays
Freeze
Offboarding and Wind-Down
Closure and Relisting
Debt Reserves
Example: Market 3
A market enters Avana only after a five-day public review and an on-chain match check against Aave's configuration, and leaves through a wind-down with no force-close power over borrowers.

A market is one chain, AMM protocol, pool and exact position shape. It has one vault token and one collateral reserve on one CDP Spoke. A CDP Spoke is one standard, unmodified Aave V4 Spoke per chain, Hub, AMM protocol and risk tier; at launch these are "Uniswap v3 Stable" on the Ethereum Stable LP Hub and "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" on the Base Stable LP Hub.

Every lifecycle operation runs on one chain through that chain's AvanaTimelock. Ethereum and Base each have their own timelock, governance multisig, guardian, MarketRegistry, ParameterStore and keepers. A market never moves to another CDP Spoke.
The pools and listing criteria themselves are described on the allowed pools page:
Allowed LP Pools
Registered → Active → (Frozen) → Offboarding → Closed
State
Meaning
How it is reached
Registered
Stored but not usable; every pledge reverts
The listing batch executes after the normal delay
Active
Open to pledges and borrowing
activateMarket
at the short delay, after the on-chain match check
Frozen
Active with the Aave freeze of its vault-token reserve: no pledges into it and no borrows by accounts holding it. Not stored by Avana; derived from Aave's flag
The Aave Protocol Guardian (one-way) or the Aave DAO freezes the reserve; only the Aave DAO unfreezes it
Offboarding
New pledges and borrowing blocked; repay, fees, withdrawals and liquidation continue; wind-down ramp after the notice
setMarketOffboarding
at the short delay, with the Aave freeze
Closed
Final; remaining debt-free positions stay withdrawable forever
closeMarket
by anyone once the market's total debt is zero
Cancelled
A registration that never went live; its market ID stays reserved for the pool
cancelRegistration
at the short delay, only from Registered
Offboarding and Closed are final. No MarketRegistry function returns such a market to Active.
A market is never deleted, because its vault token stays bound to its Spoke and pool and its debt-free positions stay withdrawable.

The Hub's pause state applies on top of the market's own state, and on Base so does the sequencer gate. Circuit breakers are not lifecycle states: a tripped breaker stops new activity while the market stays Active.
Three timelocked operations, each at the normal delay, bring a CDP Spoke, a market and a debt reserve into Avana.
Operation
What it does
deployCdpSpoke(p)

After the Aave payload has deployed a standard Spoke and its AaveOracle and registered it on the Hub, records the Spoke with its home Hub, AMM integration, risk tier, AaveOracle and implementation, and sets the expected liquidation configuration (target health factor 1.10 and minimum bonus 200 bps as Avana's guidance; the Aave DAO decides). Reverts unless the Spoke is registered on an Avana Hub, no CDP Spoke exists yet for that Hub, integration and tier, and the integration's LPVault is deployed.
listCollateralMarket(def)

Deploys the vault token through the factory, binds the market to the AMM integration's LPVault with its exact range, and records feeds, second sources, standby routes, issuer probes, swap routes into every debt asset, caps and the minimum pledge value. The market is Registered.
enableDebtReserve(spoke, def)

Records a debt reserve with its asset and funding Hub, checks the credit line against the coverage of the Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke), checks that every market on the Spoke has a primary and backup swap route into the asset, checks liquidation liveness and the flash source, and enables borrowing. A non-GHO asset first gets its own DebtOracle.

The Aave V4 risk service providers and Avana publish the listing package: thresholds and evidence for every listing rule, caps, the minimum pledge value, pool risk factor, each feed's published heartbeat, standby routes and issuer probes.
Avana operators deploy the market's LPOracle, which must seed a Live price at initialization, and raise the pool's observation buffer to cover the TWAP window at the chain's block time.

The governance multisig schedules one timelock batch at the normal delay. On the first market of a Spoke it includes the Spoke registration, the liquidation expectations and the first debt reserve; then new feeds, token collateral factors, tolerances and token listings; the vault-token deployment; the market registration; the market's parameters, caps and minimum pledge value; and the swap routes. Scheduling is public and starts the five-day review; any canceller can cancel the batch.

The Aave DAO executes the listing payload: the CDP Spoke and its AaveOracle on a Spoke's first market, the debt reserves, the flash-borrower role, the funded Coverage Spoke, the Hub asset with zero liquidity fee, and the vault-token reserve with borrowing off, share receiving off, liquidation fee 0, no reinvestment controller and the LPOracle as price source.
After the delay, anyone executes the batch. The MarketRegistry stores the market as Registered and runs every on-chain listing check. Operators poke the LPOracle and confirm a Live price.
Operators run the off-chain live-configuration check against the approved deployment manifest. Keepers add the market in observe-only mode.
The governance multisig schedules
at the short delay; anyone executes it.
Markets are created inactive so that no user action can reach a market whose Aave side has not been verified.
activateMarket(marketId)
reverts with
ActivationCheckFailed
The market is Registered, and the CDP Spoke's implementation and debt reserves match those recorded.
The vault-token reserve exists with the right decimals, borrowing off, share receiving off, not paused or frozen, liquidation fee 0, and a collateral factor above 0 and at most the expected value.
The reserve's price source is the market's LPOracle and the LPOracle is Live; each debt reserve's price source matches.
The vault-token asset is listed only on its CDP Spoke, every draw cap on it is 0 and Hub shares equal assets.
Both swap routes of every pool token into every debt asset are registered and usable, and the liquidation liveness inequality holds.
The configuration drift check finds nothing.

The short delay suffices because every market field except the Aave reserve identifiers was fixed at registration after the full review, and activation succeeds only when the executed Aave payload matches it. The 12 hours give cancellers time to stop an activation that looks wrong off-chain.
Class
Delay
Lifecycle operations
Normal
5 days (bounds 4 to 5 days)

Spoke registration, market listing, debt-reserve enabling and removal, token listing, feed definitions, new price sources and standby routes, new swap routes, every loosening, restoring a price route, upgrades
Short
12 hours
Activation, cancelling a registration, starting offboarding, every tightening, disabling or restoring a previously approved swap route, freezes, pauses, breaker trips, a timelock standby switch
Immediate (guardians)
None
Application freeze or pause, address freeze, breaker trips and the standby route switch; each only stops new activity or replaces a route with one reviewed at listing
Aave governance
Aave's own process
Collateral factors, bonus, collateral risk, Hub add caps, Spoke draw caps (credit lines), reserve freezes and unfreezes

A ready operation can be executed by anyone until 14 days after it became ready; after that it expires and must be proposed again. An operation takes the short delay only when every call in it is on the short-delay list, so one loosening makes the whole batch wait the normal delay.

Freezing a market is the Aave freeze of its vault-token reserve, set one-way by the Aave Protocol Guardian or by the Aave DAO. It moves an Active market to Frozen at once; only the Aave DAO unfreezes it. The RiskModule reads the flag and rejects pledges into the market and borrows by accounts holding it, while repay, withdrawals and liquidation continue. Avana keeps no market freeze of its own; a stop of new activity in one market is its market breaker.
Offboarding is a 12-hour timelock operation,
setMarketOffboarding(marketId)
, together with an Aave freeze of the market's vault-token reserve, which stops new pledges and borrowing at once. Repay, fee collection, withdrawals with and without debt, and liquidation stay open.
Public notice: at least
offboardNoticeSeconds
, 5 days, before the first wind-down step.
Ramp: after the notice, anyone can call
stepWindDown(marketId)

at most once per day. Each step lowers the reserve's liquidation threshold through Aave's dynamic configuration, linearly over 30 days, down to 50% of the listed value. The steps are pre-approved in the Aave payload, so the ramp needs no further proposal.
The final threshold is not 0, because 0 would make every borrower liquidatable in one block.
Existing debt is never cancelled and there is no force-close power. The ramp ends the wind-down by making each remaining borrower repay or become liquidatable at the final threshold.
The market's price feeds, swap routes and keeper duty stay in service until closure.
LT(t) = LT₀ − ⌊(LT₀ − LT_final) × min(t, T) / T⌋

Example: a listed threshold of 34% ends at 17%. On day 12 the threshold is 34% − ⌊17% × 12 / 30⌋ = 27.2%. An account with $10,000 of collateral and $2,000 of debt has a health factor of 1.36 on day 12 and 0.85 at the end, so it repays or is liquidated.
When the total debt of every account in the market is zero, anyone calls
closeMarket(marketId)
; it reverts with
MarketHasDebt
otherwise. The market becomes Closed and its oracle, swap-route and keeper duties end.
Debt-free positions stay in custody until their depositors withdraw them, with no time limit; a debt-free withdrawal reads no price. Zero-credit records stay releasable.

A closed market cannot reopen, and no second vault token can be deployed for the same Spoke, pool and range. The same pool and range can return only as a new market on another CDP Spoke, through the full five-day review, with a new vault token and market ID.

Moving a pool to another risk tier is the same: a new listing on the target tier's CDP Spoke and the offboarding of the old market. Users move by repaying, withdrawing and pledging again into a new proxy.
A registration cancelled before activation keeps its market ID reserved for its pool. A later listing of that pool reuses the ID and the existing vault token, which must name the same LPOracle.
GHO is the first debt reserve of each CDP Spoke and keeps Aave's fixed $1 price source. USDC, USDT or WETH can be added per Spoke with
enableDebtReserve
, each priced by its own DebtOracle.

The Aave payload lists the reserve and funds its Coverage Spoke before the Avana batch executes. The CDP Spoke's draw cap on the asset rises above 0 only after the Coverage Spoke is funded and the batch has executed.
Removing a debt reserve (
removeDebtReserve
, normal delay) reverts while any debt is drawn on it. The Aave DAO first sets its draw cap to 0 and freezes it, so borrowers repay over time while repay and liquidation stay open.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. The Base Stable LP Hub has no CDP Spoke yet. Market 3 is the USDC/USDT Slipstream pool with tick spacing 1 and the exact range fixed in the listing package, with a collateral factor of 31.2%. GHO is the first debt reserve, with a GHO Coverage Spoke funded to 24,000 GHO. Base blocks are 2 seconds.
Operators deploy market 3's LPOracle, which seeds a Live price of $2.00 per whole vault token, and raise the pool's observation buffer to 901.

Day 0: the governance multisig schedules one batch at the normal delay of 432,000 seconds with the Spoke registration, liquidation expectations (1.10 and 200 bps), the GHO debt reserve, the vault-token deployment, the market listing and its parameters with a $10 minimum pledge. The calldata is public for the review.
During the delay, the Aave DAO's Base executor runs the listing payload: the "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" Spoke, the GHO debt reserve, the vault-token reserve and the funded GHO Coverage Spoke.

Day 5: anyone executes the batch. The coverage check passes for a 120,000 GHO draw cap at a 20% coverage ratio against 24,000 GHO. The vault token deploys with 6 decimals and market 3 is Registered; a pledge still reverts.
Operators poke the LPOracle (Live) and run the live-configuration check; keepers watch market 3 in observe-only mode.
The multisig schedules
activateMarket(3)
at the short delay of 43,200 seconds; anyone executes it on day 5.5 and every match check passes.
Carol pledges a $20,000 Slipstream position: record 1 of 16.

A second debt reserve, USDC, is enabled at the normal delay with a USDC Coverage Spoke funded to 50,000 USDC. A 250,000 USDC draw cap passes; 300,000 would revert. Carol borrows 5,000 USDC; her health factor is 20,000 × 0.312 / 5,000 = 1.248.
Offboarding: the multisig schedules
setMarketOffboarding(3)
at the short delay and the Aave Protocol Guardian freezes the reserve. New pledges and borrows revert with
MarketOffboarding
; the app shows the notice end, 432,000 seconds later.

Wind-down: after the notice, anyone steps the ramp once a day from 31.2% toward 15.6%. On day 11 the threshold is 25.48% and Carol's health factor 1.0192; on day 12 it would be 24.96% and 0.9984. She repays her 5,000 USDC on day 11 and withdraws her position debt-free.
Closure: while any account owes debt,
closeMarket(3)
reverts. Once every account has repaid or been liquidated, anyone calls it. Debt-free positions left in market 3 stay withdrawable with no price read.

Relisting: market 3 never returns to Active. If the pool must come back, a new CDP Spoke is registered and the same pool and range are listed on it through the full five-day review, giving a new vault token and market ID. Carol pledges again into a new proxy.
Market states, deployment operations, delays, offboarding ramp, closure and relisting.

How to integrate with Avana: which contracts to call on Ethereum and Base, where addresses come from, the off-chain components, approval rules, deadlines and nonces, and the events to index.
Overview

Off-Chain Components

Integration Pages
Everything a wallet, app, keeper or indexer needs to work with Avana's contracts directly, without Avana's frontend.

Avana runs on Ethereum and Base. Each chain has an Avana Stable LP Hub and one CDP Spoke per AMM protocol: "Uniswap v3 Stable" for Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum and "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" for unstaked Aerodrome Slipstream positions on Base. The Hubs and Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned and configured by the Aave DAO; Avana's contracts handle custody, valuation, borrower actions and liquidation around them.

Anyone can call the contracts directly. Avana's frontend and AppKit are optional; repay, debt-free withdrawal, fee collection and liquidation never depend on them. Each chain's contracts are separate: nothing is shared across chains, and every operation runs through that chain's own timelock.
Contract
Who calls it
AaveAdapter
Borrowers, apps, anyone repaying for a borrower
Every borrower action: pledge, re-credit, borrow, repay, withdraw, partial removal, repay-all-and-withdraw, repay with collateral, fee collection, zero-credit release. One per chain.

to store price state; views for state and ages

Borrowers

Each chain has its own deployment and its own verified deployment manifest. Upgradeable contracts keep one fixed proxy address for life, and each market's vault token and LPOracle addresses are fixed at listing. Never take a contract address from an untrusted source; use the manifest or the published list.
Per-chain contract addresses are listed on the contracts reference page:
Contracts
Component
What it does
packages/protocol

Calldata builders for every AMM integration and chain, built in the browser from a bundled, verified deployment manifest. It records the Lens address and ships the upstream Aave error ABIs. Its builders request only the exact approvals listed below.
Keeper

Avana's keepers poke every oracle on schedule, record breaker breaches every block, liquidate every eligible account using the Lens liquidation preview, pay their own gas and cover small settlement gaps from their own funds.
Indexer
A Ponder indexer stores live chain events in Postgres for the app: positions, debt and health factors.
App backend
Stores app data, preferences and intent status. It never supplies a transaction target or calldata, so a compromised backend cannot redirect a user's transaction.
The off-chain code is covered by tests; the on-chain contracts re-check every input, so no off-chain component can authorize an action.
Each wallet gets one PositionProxy per CDP Spoke and market, deployed on its first pledge. The proxy address is known before deployment from the Lens or the Adapter's
predictProxy
view.
Each proxy is a separate Aave account with its own health factor. A problem in one market never makes another market of the same wallet liquidatable.
Positions are named by the AMM integration identifier and a position key: the token ID for Uniswap v3, and the token ID with the position-manager generation in its high byte for Slipstream.
A market accepts only positions whose tick range equals the market's exactly.
Users grant only two kinds of approval, each for exactly what one transaction needs:

For a pledge, an approval of exactly one position to the immutable LPVault of that AMM protocol: a per-token ERC-721 approval or permit for Uniswap v3 and Slipstream, or an exact LP-token amount for a fungible-share protocol.

For a repay, an approval to the AaveAdapter of exactly the repay amount in the debt asset, for the account being repaid. For a repay-all it is the Lens repay-all quote; the Adapter pulls it in full and refunds the rest in the same call, leaving zero allowance.

Never use an operator approval for all tokens or an unlimited allowance. Never approve the RiskModule, MarketRegistry, ParameterStore, an oracle, LPVaultSwap, a swap route, the flash source or a proxy. The AaveAdapter is the only spender a user trusts beyond the immutable LPVaults, and an exact amount limits what a faulty Adapter could pull to that one repay.

Every AaveAdapter entry point and every liquidation takes a deadline and reverts once the block timestamp passes it. Lens previews take the same deadline and add the margins (interest accrual, Aave's dust rule) that keep the transaction valid until then.
Every borrow names the proxy's current borrow nonce. The Adapter consumes it, so a borrow cannot be replayed or reordered.

Borrow, withdraw and partial removal take a minimum health factor that the caller chooses. Repay with collateral takes minimum amounts and a minimum repayment, and every swap leg also carries an oracle-derived minimum output.
There is no minimum borrow beyond a non-zero amount and no minimum debt. Each pledge must be worth at least the market's minimum pledge value ($10 at launch).

meta.title: Price Oracles
meta.description: How the LPOracle values one vault token from the position's fair composition at Chainlink prices, how routes, second sources, the TWAP check and the USD band work, and how the DebtOracle prices non-GHO debt.

strings: Price Oracles

How the LPOracle values one vault token from the position's fair composition at Chainlink prices, how routes, second sources, the TWAP check and the USD band work, and how the DebtOracle prices non-GHO debt.
Overview
Vault Token Price
Concentrated Liquidity
LPPriceMath
Chainlink Routes
Heartbeats and Age Limits
Second Source
TWAP Consistency Check
USD Band
Quote-Change Cap
Poke and Checkpoint
Base Sequencer Feed
DebtOracle
Views, Events and Errors
Changes and Upgrades
The LPOracle prices one market's vault token for Aave; the DebtOracle prices each non-GHO debt asset. Both use validated Chainlink routes and report a price state that Avana's contracts enforce.

A market is one chain, AMM protocol, pool and exact position shape, with one vault token and one collateral reserve on its CDP Spoke. Each market has its own LPOracle proxy. Each AMM protocol has one LPOracle implementation per chain, and every market of that protocol on that chain is a proxy of it. At launch that means one implementation for Uniswap v3 on Ethereum and one for Aerodrome Slipstream on Base.
The LPOracle has two layers:

A price-state core that does not depend on the AMM. It validates Chainlink prices for each of the market's tokens, selects one quote per token, runs failover, agreement, freshness, second-source, sequencer and timer rules, and serves a conservative price when the market cannot be trusted.

A pricing module per AMM protocol, compiled into that protocol's implementation. It supplies the composition of the position at an oracle price vector, the AMM consistency check and the listing checks. The AMM integration uses the same composition function, so pricing and unwinding agree.

The LPOracle does two jobs. For Aave, it returns the USD value of one whole vault token with 8 decimals, which the CDP Spoke's AaveOracle reads for health factors and seizure sizing. For Avana, its views report the price state, the source timestamp and age limits of the served price, whether a borrow may rely on the price, the disagreement pause, the recovery grace window, the last accepted price and an hourly checkpoint. The RiskModule and LPVaultSwap enforce their gates from these views.

The LPOracle applies no haircut: all risk adjustment sits in the CDP Spoke's collateral factor. It does not price debt, enforce gates, choose feeds or move tokens. No token, ETH or approval ever moves through it.
The four price states and what each one allows are described on the price states page:
Price States

The price of one whole vault token is the value of the tokens the position would hold if the pool price equalled the price implied by the oracle price vector. This is the fair composition. It is the cheapest holding the position can reach: moving the pool price can only raise the value of what the position actually holds, so a pool manipulation cannot inflate collateral and the LPOracle never needs the pool's spot price.
value = Σ amountᵢ(oracle price vector) × priceᵢ

Prices are the validated Chainlink quotes of each token, with every USD-pegged stable capped at $1.00 for valuation. A stable trading above $1 does not make the collateral safer, so the premium is never credited.
For concentrated liquidity, the oracle price ratio is clamped to the market's tick range before the amounts are computed.
Every amount is floored and then reduced by one raw unit. Every division and square root rounds down, against the borrower.
Uncollected fees are excluded: owed tokens, fee growth and any fee the AMM keeps apart from the position never count, because a wash trader can raise them within one transaction.
The result has 8 decimals and is at least 1. The price never reverts except with an out-of-gas guard and never returns 0, because Aave rejects a non-positive price.
Vault-token decimals

One vault-token base unit is one unit of the position measure the AMM integration credits: for Uniswap v3 and Slipstream, one unit of liquidity of the market's exact range. The decimals are fixed at listing as the smallest value between 6 and 18 for which one whole token is worth at least $1 at the listing prices, so a whole token is worth between $1 and $10. Listing fails if no such value exists.
Example
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.
Step
Value
Market
USDC/USDT on the tick range −10 to 10, 10 vault-token decimals
Valuation prices
Composition of one whole token
5,648,563 raw USDC and 4,348,479 raw USDT
After the one-unit deduction
Price

The concentrated-liquidity pricing module serves every Uniswap v3 market on Ethereum and every Aerodrome Slipstream market on Base. Slipstream uses the same tick, square-root price and liquidity math, so the module is shared; only the pool reads differ, and the module never reads the pool's spot state for valuation.

The two token prices are converted to a pool square-root price in 512-bit arithmetic, including the decimals factor. The conversion never reverts; an out-of-bounds result is clamped and the market is reported as Drifting.

The oracle square-root price is clamped to the range between the market's lower and upper tick. Outside its range a position holds only one token, and the clamp makes the composition exactly that one-token holding.
Amounts follow Uniswap's liquidity-amount formulas at the clamped price, rounding down at every step.

When the clamp changes the price, the oracle ratio has left the range, which for a stable pair means a token has depegged. The market is Drifting with the price-clamped reason: new pledges and new debt stop, top-ups and liquidation continue.

Example: USDC/USDT on the range −100 to 100 (about ±1%), 9 decimals. USDT depegs to $0.952 with USDC at $1. The ratio is above the range, so one whole token holds 0 USDC and 9,999,541 raw USDT and is priced at $9.52. Without the clamp, the same formulas would give 29,887,349 raw USDT, valued at $28.45, 2.99 times the real holding.

LPPriceMath is an internal library with no external calls and no storage. It holds the pure arithmetic of the price path and is compiled into every LPOracle implementation and the DebtOracle, so each formula maps to one function and one verification model. The oracles call it with values they have already validated.
Function
Computes
normalizeAnswer
A Chainlink answer scaled to 8 decimals, rounding down
routeValue
The USD price of a one-leg or two-leg route; a two-leg route takes the timestamp of its oldest leg
feedMaxAge
A leg's heartbeat plus the chain's heartbeat margin
vaultDecimals
The vault-token decimals chosen at listing
lpPrice
The price of one whole vault token from the pricing module's composition
inUsdBand
Whether a stable market is inside the USD band
servedTimestamp
The source timestamp of the served price: its oldest input
ageLimits
The borrow and liquidation age limits of the served price
servedPrice
The collateral price served in each state
debtServedPrice
The debt price served in each state, including the stress rise
secondSourceAgrees
The second-source agreement test
sequencerStatus
Up, down, grace or unknown from the sequencer-uptime feed
minObservations
The pool observation buffer needed for the TWAP window on the chain
gasForCall
The gas check made before every external read

A leg is one Chainlink aggregator read through its standard proxy. A route is one leg (TOKEN/USD) or two legs multiplied (TOKEN/X × X/USD). Each listed token has three routes, recorded in the MarketRegistry at listing under the same checks:
Route
Role
Primary
The token's direct TOKEN/USD Chainlink feed. Used whenever it is valid.
Alternate

An independent route that shares no aggregator with the primary. Used automatically when the primary is invalid, re-evaluated on every read with no transaction, role or stored flag. It never assumes a peg, such as pricing USDT as USDT/USDC × $1.
Standby
A third route that a guardian can put in place of the primary or the alternate at once. It passed every listing check of the slot it replaces, so a guardian can only choose among reviewed routes.
Leg validity

Each leg is read with a static call inside try/catch and an explicit gas amount. A leg is valid only if its decimals equal the decimals pinned at listing, its answer lies strictly between the pinned minimum and maximum answers, its timestamp is non-zero and not in the future, its age is within the leg's age limit, and its normalised answer is at least 1. A leg that fails only the age test is Stale; any other failure is Invalid or Error. A route is valid only if all its legs are valid.
Agreement check
When both routes of a token are valid, they must agree within the token's tolerance T, in basis points, compared as exact integers with no division:
|primary − alternate| × 10,000 ≤ T × min(primary, alternate)

The tolerance must be at least the deviation thresholds of every leg on both routes plus a margin of 50 bps, so honest routes never disagree. If the check fails, the market is Drifting and the quote stays the primary. When only one route is valid, no agreement check runs.
Example: with T = 225 bps, a primary of $1.0001 and an alternate of $0.9990 agree (1.1 × 10⁹ ≤ 2.248 × 10¹⁰). With the alternate at $0.9750 they disagree (2.51 × 10¹⁰ > 2.194 × 10¹⁰).
Independence rules at listing
A token's primary and alternate routes share no aggregator.
No two tokens of a market share an aggregator on their alternate routes, so one intermediate feed cannot move every token at once.
No token's second source shares an aggregator with any of its routes.
Every route stays within its pinned answer bounds and within $10,000 per token, the overflow ceiling.

A Chainlink feed publishes a new round when its answer moves by its deviation threshold or when its heartbeat elapses. A feed that is still operating is therefore never older than its heartbeat plus a publication delay. Each leg's age limit is its own published heartbeat, recorded at listing, plus the chain's heartbeat margin of 1,800 seconds on Ethereum and on Base.
feedMaxAge = feedHeartbeat + heartbeatMargin
Feed
Heartbeat
Age limit
Ethereum USDC/USD, USDS/USD
Ethereum USDT/USD, GHO/USD
Ethereum DAI/USD, ETH/USD
Base USD stablecoin feeds

A calm stablecoin feed legitimately ages up to its 23- or 24-hour heartbeat. A 20-hour-old USDC/USD answer is fresh; a borrow against it also needs the second source to agree. There is no separate heartbeat ceiling for primaries, because the agreement check and the second source bound what a feed's age can hide.
liquidationPriceMaxAge
borrowPriceMaxAge
While a token is priced from its alternate route, every alternate leg is held to its borrow age for liquidation too. Past it, the market's seizure is blocked as if Cached while the market stays Live.
The oracle reports the deadline of the served price as an age relative to its oldest input, so a slow stablecoin leg and a fast ETH/USD leg in the same market are each held to their own cadence.

A deviation-triggered feed is trusted for up to a day between rounds, so a borrow must not rely on one oracle network alone. Each token has an independent second source: another oracle network's aggregator, or a time-weighted price of a deep pool that is not the market's own pool, multiplied by the reference token's validated quote. A token is confirmed when the second source is valid and agrees with the token's quote within its tolerance, at most 500 bps.
borrowAllowed = (state == Live) ∧ sequencerReady ∧ every token confirmed ∧ (now − servedUpdatedAt ≤ borrowPriceMaxAge)
Borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt need this flag for the account's market and for the DebtOracle of the borrowed debt reserve.
The second source never gates liquidation and never changes the state, the served price or any timer, so a broken second source can stop borrowing but never protects an unhealthy account.
Each token can record a standby second source. Either guardian can switch to it at once; switching back goes through the timelock.
Example: tolerance 100 bps, quote $1.0002. A second source of $0.9940 confirms the token; $0.9890 does not, and borrowing stops while the market stays Live.

The pool's time-weighted price is an independent check on Chainlink. It gates the price and never feeds it. The check reads only the market's own pool, fixed at listing, through its observation history over the window W.
The reference tick is computed from the uncapped Chainlink quotes. The mean tick over the window is rounded toward negative infinity.
The check passes when the two ticks differ by at most the tolerance τ. One tick is a price step of 1.0001, about 1 bp. The launch tolerance is 50 ticks; it can never be set below 10.
A failed check, or an observation read that reverts or cannot cover the window, makes the market Drifting. No view reverts because of it.
Observation buffer per chain

A pool writes at most one observation per block, so an attacker who swaps dust in every block could shrink the buffer's time span. The pool must hold enough observations to cover the window at the chain's block time:
twapMinObservations = ⌈twapWindow / CHAIN_BLOCK_TIME⌉ + 1
Chain
Block time
twapWindow
twapMinObservations
Ethereum
Base
2 s
Avana raises the pool's observation cardinality at listing and pays for it, over several transactions if needed. The Ethereum value used on Base would cover only 300 seconds.

When every token moves together, through a common-mode feed error or a correlated depeg, the pool ratio and the agreement check can look normal. The USD band catches the absolute level. It applies to markets whose tokens are all USD-pegged stables, which includes every Stable LP Hub market; other markets use 0 and the maximum value, so the test always passes.
The band is 0.90 to 1.02 at launch, tested on the geometric mean of the token prices.
The lower bound is tested on the uncapped quotes, because a downward common-mode move is what the band exists for.
The upper bound is tested on the prices capped at $1, so GHO markets stay Live while GHO trades at a premium.
A breach makes the market Drifting. It blocks new borrowing and withdrawals that leave debt; pledges, repay and liquidation continue, liquidation while both routes of each token are fresh and agree.

Example: GHO at $1.047 and USDC at $1.00 is in band, because the capped prices give 1.00 against an upper limit of 1.0404; tested uncapped, it would have breached. Both tokens at $0.89 give 0.7921 against a lower limit of 0.81, so the market is Drifting.
Every AMM protocol has a per-block quote-change cap,
maxQuoteChangeBps

, set per market (100 bps, 1%, at launch). When a poke computes a price that differs from an accepted price stored in the same block by more than the cap, the LPOracle does not accept it. It emits a capped event and serves the market as Cached for that block; a later block that still computes the new price accepts it.

Example: accepted price $2.10. A quote of $2.13 in the same block is refused (3 × 10¹⁰ > 2.1 × 10¹⁰); $2.11 is accepted. A one-block move never reaches borrowing power, and a real move is accepted one block later.
Views compute the state on every read.
poke()
is the only call that writes price, timer or latch storage. It is permissionless, makes only static calls, takes no lock and returns the state.
What a poke stores
The accepted price, only when the market is Live and its inputs are newer than the last accepted price. Re-reading the same rounds never refreshes the timestamp.
The first failed read of a failure episode and the first observation of a route disagreement.
The grace latch and the recovery time after an outage that reached Expired.
The route version of each token, so a standby switch restarts the disagreement window.
The checkpoint: a copy of the accepted price, taken at most once per hour.
Who pokes
Collateralization pokes the pledged market before each pledge check.
The RiskModule pokes the account's market and every non-GHO DebtOracle of the account before a borrow or a withdrawal with debt.
LPVaultSwap pokes the collateral market and debt oracles of the account it liquidates.

Keepers poke every LPOracle and DebtOracle at least once per hour and once per heartbeat of the fastest leg in force, in every block while a market is not Live, and in the block after a standby switch, restore or sequencer change.
Repay, fee collection and debt-free withdrawal never read or poke an oracle.
Gas guard

Each external read gets an explicit gas amount: 50,000 for a feed, 100,000 for a pool or pricing-module read, 40,000 for a registry, store or token call. Before each read the oracle checks that enough gas remains to forward the full amount and reverts with
InsufficientGas
otherwise. A caller who picks the transaction's gas limit therefore cannot make a healthy feed look failed.
also requires
pokeMinGas
at entry (551,588 in the reference measurement).
Checkpoint and price-drop alert
priceCheckpoint()

returns the accepted price copied by a poke at most once per 3,600 seconds. It is always a validated Live price. Monitoring compares the served price with a checkpoint from the last two hours and alerts when it is 3% lower. The price drop is an alert to the guardians only, never an on-chain trip.
On Base, every LPOracle, DebtOracle and the RiskModule read the Chainlink L2 sequencer-uptime feed
with a grace period of 3,600 seconds. Ethereum has no sequencer feed, and the sequencer is always treated as ready there.
Sequencer status
Effect
Down
Borrowing blocked and seizure paused, because borrowers cannot react while only L1-forced transactions run
Grace (first 3,600 s after restart)
Borrowing stays blocked; only accounts below the grace health factor (0.95) can be liquidated
Unknown (unreadable feed)
Borrowing blocked; liquidation continues, so a broken uptime feed never stops liquidation
Ready
No effect
The sequencer status never changes the price state, the served price or any timer.

GHO is priced by Aave's fixed $1 source and has no DebtOracle. Each other debt asset (USDC, USDT or WETH, enabled per CDP Spoke) has exactly one DebtOracle proxy per chain, used as the Aave price source of that asset's reserve on every CDP Spoke of the chain that lends it. It applies the same leg, route, failover, agreement, freshness, second-source, sequencer and timer rules to one token, with no pool, no consistency check, no USD band and no $1 ceiling: a debt asset above $1 is priced above $1.
A debt price that cannot be trusted is never below the last accepted price, so it can only lower health factors:
State
Served debt price
Live
The fresh quote
Drifting (routes disagree)
The higher of the two routes and the accepted price
Cached
The accepted price
Expired
The accepted price raised by the asset's stress rise, rounded up
The stress rise,
debtStressRiseBps

, is set per asset between 100 and 5,000 bps at its first debt-reserve listing (500 bps for USDC at launch). LPVaultSwap repays a debt reserve in a liquidation only while its DebtOracle is Live within its liquidation age; otherwise the call reverts
DebtPriceStale
for that reserve, and the account's other reserves stay liquidatable.

Example: USDC with an accepted price of $0.9999 and a 500 bps stress rise. Once Expired, the served price is $1.049895, so 10,000 USDC of debt counts as $10,498.95 instead of $9,999 in the health factor.
LPOracle function
Returns

The served price, 8 decimals, at least 1

decimals()
Always 8

Concentrated-liquidity detail: clamp, both square-root prices, mean and reference ticks, tolerance and observation cardinality

The capped valuation price of each token, used by LPVaultSwap for its recovery floor and per-leg minimum outputs

The last accepted price and its source timestamp, used for caps, the minimum pledge value and previews
The hourly checkpoint

Age limit of the served price for borrowing; 0 when the market is failed

Age limit of the served price for liquidation; 0 when the market is failed
Evaluates and stores; returns the state

A bitmap of failed listing checks; 0 means every check passes
Every view returns the same result for every caller in the same block, and no view reverts except with the gas guard.
