(DebtOracle only)
Each LPOracle and DebtOracle is a UUPS proxy. Its admin roles can be held only by the chain's Avana timelock, and every upgrade waits the normal delay of 5 days and can be cancelled while queued.

A market's LPOracle address stays the Aave price source and the vault token's oracle for the life of the market. A new pricing model or a fix is an upgrade of that proxy, never a new address. If Aave's price source must change, the Aave payload executes only together with the matching Avana timelock operation, and liquidation keeps running on the LPOracle's own state meanwhile.
New price sources and any change to price computation take the normal delay. Tightening a tolerance or lowering a borrow age takes the short delay of 12 hours.
Only two route changes take effect without a delay: the automatic failover to the alternate, and a guardian's switch to the standby route recorded at listing.
No role can push a price or set a timer. The accepted price and every timer change only through initialization and pokes.
At listing, initialization requires every configuration check to pass and a Live price, which it seeds as the first accepted price.
How the LPOracle values vault tokens and how the DebtOracle prices non-GHO debt.

meta.title: Price States
meta.description: The four LPOracle price states (Live, Drifting, Cached, Expired), what each one serves and allows, the recovery grace window, the Base sequencer gate, the standby route switch and the oracle playbook.

strings: Price States

The four LPOracle price states (Live, Drifting, Cached, Expired), what each one serves and allows, the recovery grace window, the Base sequencer gate, the standby route switch and the oracle playbook.
Overview
Live
Drifting
Cached
Expired
Served Price by State
What Each State Allows
Disagreement Pause
Recovery Grace
Sequencer Down and Grace
Standby Route Switch
Debt Price States
Playbook P-02
Example: Oracle Expiry

Each market's LPOracle reports one of four states on every read. The state decides what the market's account can do and whether the market can be seized; repay and debt-free exits work in every state.

The LPOracle reports exactly one state, in increasing severity: Live, Drifting, Cached, Expired. The state is computed on every read from current feed and pool data plus a few stored timers, with no hysteresis. The borrow flag, the second-source result and the sequencer status are reported beside the state and never change it.

The LPOracle only reports. The RiskModule enforces the borrow-side and pledge gates, and LPVaultSwap enforces the liquidation gates. Each wallet has one PositionProxy and one Aave account per market, so a market's state decides whether that account can borrow and whether that market can be seized; other markets of the same wallet are unaffected.

A price that cannot be trusted only makes an account easier to liquidate, never harder: collateral is served at most at its last accepted price and debt at least at its last accepted price. The market whose price is in doubt is never seized at that price.
The valuation, routes and checks behind each state are described on the price oracles page:
Price Oracles

Every token has a fresh, valid primary or alternate Chainlink route and no Drifting condition holds. A market whose tokens use their alternate routes is still Live; the alternate is reported as an informational reason. The served price is the fresh price.

Live alone is not enough to borrow. A borrow also needs the second source of every token to agree, the sequencer to be ready on Base and the served price to be within its borrow age. When a second source disagrees or cannot be read, the market stays Live and pledges and liquidation continue, but borrowing and withdrawals with debt stop.
The market is not failed, but one of these conditions holds:
Reason
Cause
Notes
ANY_TOKEN_DISAGREE
A token's primary and alternate routes are both fresh and differ by more than the agreement tolerance
Starts the disagreement pause; this market's seizure waits
USD_BAND
A stable market's USD level is outside 0.90 to 1.02
Never blocks pledges and never pauses liquidation
CONSISTENCY_DEVIATION
The pool TWAP is further than the tolerance from the Chainlink-implied price
Blocks new pledges
CONSISTENCY_UNAVAILABLE
The pool's observation read fails or cannot cover the window
PRICE_CLAMPED
The oracle price ratio lies outside the market's tick range
Blocks new pledges; the position is valued as its one-token holding

While Drifting, the market serves the lower of the fresh price and the last accepted price; during a disagreement it serves the price built from each token's lower route, at most the accepted price. Borrowing and withdrawals with debt are blocked; top-ups, repay, fee collection and debt-free withdrawals stay open.
The market is failed: some token has no valid route, or a configuration, route, feed, pricing-module or token-decimals read failed, or the pool's reentrancy lock is held. For
cachedWindow
(1 hour at launch) after the first failed read, the market serves its last accepted price with its original source timestamp. Reading the same rounds again never refreshes that timestamp.

The window starts when reads actually began to fail, not at the last round and not at the first poke after the failure. For a feed that went stale, the start is computed from the feed's own timestamps: the first second after the age limit of the last of its routes to go stale.

Borrowing, withdrawals with debt, new pledges and top-ups stop. The market cannot be seized. The account's other reserves stay liquidatable, with this market at its last accepted price. A cap of 1 hour on Cached keeps one late round from turning into mass liquidation while still bounding how long a stale price is used.
After

of Cached the market is Expired. It serves 1: one unit of 10⁻⁸ USD per whole vault token, the smallest positive price, so Aave counts the collateral as worth about zero. The value never reverts and is never 0, so Aave keeps valuing positions and repay and debt-free withdrawals keep working.
Avana never seizes an Expired market, so the value 1 only lowers the account's health factor and never sizes a seizure.
Avana's own valuations keep using the last accepted price: caps, the minimum pledge value, the restore amount of a rescue top-up and Lens previews.
A non-GHO debt asset whose DebtOracle is Expired is served at its last accepted price raised by
debtStressRiseBps
, so stale debt counts higher, never lower.
The Expired latch is set only from Chainlink source timestamps, never from a caught error, a failed configuration read or a gas shortfall.
State
Collateral price served to Aave
Non-GHO debt price served to Aave
Fresh price
Fresh quote
Drifting, no disagreement
Lower of fresh and accepted
Not applicable: a DebtOracle drifts only on disagreement
Drifting, routes disagree
Price at each token's lower route, at most accepted
Higher of the two routes and accepted
Accepted price
1 (10⁻⁸ USD)
Accepted price × (1 + stress rise)

Example (full-range USDC/USDT, accepted price $1.99980000): USDT reads $1.00 on its primary and $0.975 on its alternate, which disagree. The lower-route price is $1.97483855, so the market serves that. If the market were Cached it would serve $1.99980000; once Expired, 1. Drifting on a TWAP deviation with a fresh price of $1.99999600 serves $1.99980000.

Repay, fee collection, debt-free withdrawal, debt-free partial removal and zero-credit release are open in every state, because none of them reads or pokes an oracle. Liquidation is gated per reserve: only the seized collateral market and the repaid debt reserve need fresh, agreeing prices. The table shows the account holding the market in each state.
New pledge
Top-up
Borrow
Withdraw with debt
Repay, fees, debt-free exit
Seizure of this market
Live, borrow flag true
Yes, while every input is within its liquidation age
Live, second source disagrees or unavailable

No, treated as Cached
Drifting, USD band only
Yes, while both routes of each token are fresh and agree
Drifting, TWAP deviation or unavailable, price clamped
Yes, if the Chainlink inputs are fresh
No, until the routes agree or a standby switch ends the disagreement
Recovery grace (any state)
Only accounts below health factor 0.95
Sequencer down (Base)
Yes, if the market's price is still fresh
Sequencer grace (Base)

While a market cannot be seized, the account's other reserves with fresh prices stay liquidatable, with the blocked market counted at its served price. Withdraw with debt includes partial removal with debt and repay with collateral. The full matrix, with pause states, breakers and Aave-side flags, is on the safety pages.
The first poke that sees a token's two fresh routes disagree stores that time and emits
DisagreementRecorded
. From then, seizure of this market is paused for up to
disagreementPauseMax
(3,600 seconds at launch, never more). A short disagreement is usually one route lagging a fast move.

If the routes still disagree after the pause, one route is wrong. The market is treated as Expired for its own seizure until a poke sees every token agree, a guardian switches the faulty slot to its standby route, or a fix executes through the timelock.
Meanwhile the market counts at its lower routes, so the disagreement can only make the account look less healthy, and repay and top-ups stay open.
No grace window follows a disagreement, because top-ups and repay stayed open throughout.
After an outage that reached Expired, the first fresh, valid update stores the recovery time and emits
GraceStarted
. For
graceDuration
(30 minutes at launch, at most 2 hours) LPVaultSwap liquidates an account of this market only if its health factor is below
graceHealthFactor

(0.95 at launch, never below 0.90). After the window, every account below 1.00 is liquidatable again. Borrowers get time to repay or add collateral at the recovered price before ordinary liquidations resume.
Each outage starts at most one grace window.
The recovery time is reconstructed from Chainlink's own round timestamps, so an outage that began and ended between two pokes still opens a grace window, and no caller can fake one.
When the recovering round is the first of a new Chainlink aggregator phase, the previous round is read from the previous phase's aggregator.
The window never starts before the recovery: without usable round evidence it starts at the newest input of the fresh price, and after a standby switch at the poke that observes the switch.
On Base, the sequencer-uptime feed adds two conditions that apply on top of every price state. Ethereum has no sequencer gate.

Down: only transactions forced in from L1 execute, on prices that may be hours old. Borrowing, withdrawals with debt, repay with collateral, new-account pledges and liquidation stop. Repay, top-ups with a fresh price, debt-free withdrawal and fee collection keep working, including through L1.
Grace: for 3,600 seconds after the sequencer restarts, borrowing stays closed and only accounts below health factor 0.95 can be liquidated.

Example: the sequencer goes down at 09:40; a borrow forced in from L1 reverts, a repay forced in from L1 runs. It restarts at 10:00:00 and the gate is in grace until 11:00:00. At 10:20 an account at health factor 0.9997 cannot be liquidated; after 11:00:00 it can, and borrowing reopens.

Each listed token records a standby route that passed, at listing, every check of the slot it can replace. When a feed fails or two routes disagree, the market's seizures wait for a usable price; a normal-delay fix would take at least five days, longer than the 48-hour window caps are sized for. The standby lets a guardian end the outage in minutes without choosing an unreviewed price.
Call
Effect
useStandbyRoute(token, slot)
Emergency Guardian or Aave Protocol Guardian at once; or the timelock at the short delay, cancellable only by the Aave governance executor
Puts the standby in the primary or alternate slot and increments the token's route version
cancelStandbySwitch(token)
Aave governance executor, at once
Undoes a guardian's switch
restorePriceRoute(token)
Timelock, normal delay
Restores the listed routes once the original route is healthy
useStandbySecondSource(token)
Either guardian, at once; switching back goes through the timelock
Replaces a failing second source with its standby

A switch writes no oracle state. Every oracle reading the token picks up the new route on its next evaluation, restarts its disagreement timer and keeps its failure timer. A switch never forces Live: the standby is subject to the same freshness, validity and agreement checks, and a stale or disagreeing standby leaves the market where it was.
GHO's fixed $1 source never fails. Each non-GHO debt asset's DebtOracle has the same four states, timers, grace window and standby route as a market.
LPVaultSwap repays that debt reserve only while its DebtOracle is Live and within its liquidation age; the account's other debt reserves can still be repaid against fresh collateral.
During a debt-oracle grace window, LPVaultSwap applies the grace health factor to every account with debt in that asset.

P-02 covers oracle failure, staleness, disagreement and manipulation. Monitoring pages on-call when a market is Cached or Expired, when a disagreement starts (and again 30 minutes before the pause ends), and on leg and debt-feed ages.
Identify the failing leg and route from the oracle's price state.
If the token's standby route is fresh and agrees with the healthy route, a guardian switches the failing slot to it.
If the standby also fails, a guardian trips the market breaker. The market's own seizures wait while keepers keep liquidating fresh reserves.
For a failing debt feed, the same steps apply to the DebtOracle, with the debt breaker if the standby fails.
If only a second source fails or disagrees, so borrowing stops while the price stays Live, a guardian switches to the standby second source once it agrees with the served price.
The governance multisig prepares a permanent source as a normal-delay price-source operation.

Recovery: keepers poke until the market is Live, the grace window applies per account, the listed route is restored at the normal delay once healthy, and a manual breaker is reset once the market has been Live for one cached window.
A 24-hour stablecoin feed that has not updated for 20 hours is normal, not an incident: it stays fresh for 88,200 seconds, and borrowing also needs the second source to agree.

Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing. USDT/USD has an 86,400-second heartbeat and stays fresh for 88,200 seconds. The cached window is 1 hour, the grace duration 30 minutes and the grace health factor 0.95. One whole vault token is worth $2.00.
Both USDT routes stop publishing. 88,200 seconds after the last round, a poke finds the leg stale. The market is Cached and serves the cached $2.00; the oracle emits
FailureRecorded
The RiskModule refuses borrows and withdrawals with debt with
PriceNotLive
. LPVaultSwap refuses to seize the market with
StalePrice
. Repay and debt-free withdrawal continue.
After 1 hour of Cached the market is Expired and serves 1, so Aave counts the collateral as worthless while repay and exits keep working; the oracle emits
OutageExpiredLatched
. Operators follow P-02 and may switch to the standby route.
The feed publishes again and the next poke accepts it, emitting
with an end time 1,800 seconds after the recovery.
For 30 minutes LPVaultSwap seizes only accounts below health factor 0.95; an account at 0.97 is refused with
GraceHealthFactor
. After that, every account below 1.00 can be liquidated. The Lens price-state view shows the state and grace end throughout.
A debt asset behaves the same way through its DebtOracle, except that once Expired it serves the accepted price raised by the stress rise, so debt is never undervalued.
The four price states, what each allows, grace, sequencer gate, standby switch and playbook P-02.

meta.title: AaveAdapter Entry Points
meta.description: Every borrower function of the AaveAdapter with its parameters, purpose and gates, plus deadlines, the borrow nonce, the minimum health factor, events and errors.

strings: AaveAdapter Entry Points
Every borrower function of the AaveAdapter with its parameters, purpose and gates, plus deadlines, the borrow nonce, the minimum health factor, events and errors.
Overview
Accounts and Positions
Entry Points
Gates per Function
Deadline, Nonce and Health Factor
Receiver Rule and Approvals
Views
Events
Main Errors
Upgrades and Limits
The AaveAdapter is the single entry point for every borrower action on every CDP Spoke of its chain. This page lists each function, what it checks and what it emits.

One AaveAdapter runs per chain behind one fixed address. Calls go from the wallet to the AaveAdapter, then to the wallet's PositionProxy for that market, then to the CDP Spoke. The Adapter creates proxies through the immutable ProxyManager, has Collateralization take custody and record backing, is the only minter and burner of every vault token, runs the RiskModule's checks and returns their errors unchanged.

Every entry point takes the protocol Lock first and releases it last, so no Avana call can re-enter another. The Adapter holds no token at the end of any call and charges no fee on borrowing or interest.

Repay, debt-free withdrawal and removal, repay-all-and-withdraw, zero-credit release and fee collection read no MarketRegistry state, pause state, address freeze, breaker or price. A borrower can always exit, whatever the protocol state.
An account is one PositionProxy bound to one wallet, CDP Spoke and market. Its address is a CREATE2 address known before deployment; the first pledge to a market deploys it.
Each account has its own Aave health factor. Nothing is cross-collateralized between markets of the same wallet.
An account holds at most 16 records (pledged positions) per market, so one liquidation always fits in a block.
Positions are named by a
PositionRef
made of the AMM integration identifier and the integration's position key, never by a bare NFT token ID. Token amount arrays follow the market's token order.
The borrower functions are split across two interfaces, IAaveAdapterUser and IAaveAdapterCollateral.
Function
Parameters
Purpose
pledge
marketId, position, deadline

Pledges one AMM position into a market. Creates the wallet's proxy on its first pledge, takes custody through the market's LPVault, mints vault tokens equal to the credited units, supplies them to the CDP Spoke and enables them as collateral. Returns the proxy, the record ID and the credited units.
recredit
marketId, position, topUp, deadline

Credits units added to a pledged position. For an NFT position the depositor first adds liquidity on the AMM and passes empty bytes; for fungible LP shares the bytes encode the amount. Depositor of record only.
borrow
marketId, debtReserveId, amount, receiver, deadline, minHealthFactor, expectedNonce
Borrows an approved debt asset on the caller's account for the market and sends it to the receiver. There is no minimum borrow beyond a non-zero amount and no minimum debt.
repay
borrower, marketId, debtReserveId, maxRepaySpend, repayAll, deadline

Repays one debt reserve of any borrower's account with the caller's funds. A partial repay pulls the smaller of the cap and the debt. A repay-all pulls the full cap, repays the live debt and refunds the rest in the same call, or reverts if debt would remain.
withdraw
marketId, position, units, deadline, minHealthFactor
Withdraws one record's credited units, burns them and returns the whole position, with its uncollected fees, to its depositor of record. With debt, the health check runs after the withdrawal.
repayAllAndWithdraw
marketId, position, units, debtReserveIds, maxRepaySpends, deadline
Repays each named debt reserve in full under its own cap, requires every debt reserve of the account to be at zero, then makes a debt-free withdrawal of one record, in one call.
removeLiquidity
marketId, position, units, minAmounts, deadline, minHealthFactor

Removes part of one record's credited units while the position stays in custody. The removed principal is paid to the depositor of record, each token at least its minimum. With debt, the remaining record must still be worth the market's minimum pledge value.
repayWithCollateral
RepayWithCollateralParams p

Repays one debt reserve with units released from one record, through LPVaultSwap, with no bonus and no Avana fee. LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset, repays, unwinds and swaps the units; any leftover is paid to the caller in the debt asset. While debt remains, the health factor must not fall.
collectFees

Collects the fees a custodied position has earned and pays them to the depositor of record. Principal, units and health factor are unchanged. Reverts for AMM protocols whose fees roll into the position.
releaseZeroCredit
Returns the position of a record whose credit a seizure took to zero. Mints, burns and supplies nothing. Depositor of record only.
RepayWithCollateralParams
Field
Meaning
marketId
The account's market
position
The record whose units repay
units
Credited units released from the record
debtReserveId
The debt reserve repaid
minAmounts
Least raw amount of each pool token the unwind must return
minDebtRepaid
Smallest repayment accepted, in debt-asset base units
deadline
Last valid block timestamp
minHealthFactor
Least health factor after the call while debt remains, WAD
Every swap leg also carries an oracle-derived minimum output, so the caller's minimums can only tighten it.

The Adapter enforces the deadline, the nonce, the receiver rule, proxy resolution, debt-reserve enablement, the Hub's pause state and the address freeze. The RiskModule enforces the sequencer gate, price states and ages, Aave pauses and freezes, offboarding, configuration drift, Hub share accounting, liquidation halts, circuit breakers and the health factor.
Pause state of the Hub
Other checks
Refused under Paused with reason MintPathSuspect; rescue top-ups only under Paused with reason General or for a frozen caller; refused under Frozen for an account with no debt
Registered market on an approved Spoke, matching integration, exact position shape, price state, caps, minimum pledge value ($10), breakers, 16-record limit
Same as a pledge
Top-up checks and a new cap charge
Refused unless the market's Hub and the debt reserve's funding Hub are both in state None
Receiver rule, address freeze of caller and receiver, nonce, every price and breaker gate over the market and every debt reserve of the account, health factor after the borrow
Never read
None beyond the deadline and an existing proxy
without debt
None; no price is read
with debt
Refused if the Hub is Paused
Address freeze, the RiskModule's withdraw checks, health factor after the withdrawal
Every debt reserve must end at zero
Without debt never read; with debt refused if Paused
With debt: address freeze, withdraw checks, remaining record at least the minimum pledge value, health factor
Refused only under Paused with reason MintPathSuspect; open under Frozen and Paused with reason General
Address freeze, enabled debt reserve, non-zero debt, health factor not lower than before; reads no breaker
Depositor of record only
Depositor of record only; record at zero credited units
The price-state rules behind each gate are on the price states page:
Price States
Deadline: every entry point reverts with
DeadlineExpired
when the block timestamp is past the deadline, so a transaction held back by a builder or a congested chain cannot execute later on different terms.
Nonce: each borrow names the proxy's current borrow nonce in
expectedNonce
, read from
borrowNonce(proxy)
. The Adapter consumes it and increments it; a mismatch reverts with
BadNonce
, so a signed borrow cannot be replayed or reordered. A reverted borrow leaves the nonce unchanged.
Minimum health factor: borrow, withdraw, partial removal and repay with collateral take a

in WAD. After a borrow or a withdrawal with debt, the health factor excluding rescue units must be at least the larger of 1.00, the market's optional hard floor (off by default) and this value. Pass 0 for no extra bound.
The Lens recommends borrowing to a health factor of 1.10. No contract enforces that value; a caller who passes 1.10 as the minimum gets it enforced.

A borrow's receiver cannot be the zero address, any registered proxy, the Adapter, Collateralization, any LPVault, LPVaultSwap, the payout escrow, the flash source, any Avana Hub, any approved CDP Spoke or any Spoke listed on the borrowed asset's funding Hub. A refused receiver reverts with
InvalidReceiver
Users grant only two kinds of approval:

For a pledge, an approval of exactly one position to the immutable LPVault of that AMM protocol: a per-token ERC-721 approval or permit for Uniswap v3 and Slipstream. Never an operator approval for all tokens.

For a repay, an approval to the AaveAdapter of exactly the repay amount in the debt asset. For a repay-all, the amount is the Lens repay-all quote; the Adapter pulls it in full and refunds the unused part in the same call, leaving zero allowance.
View
Returns
proxyOf
The wallet's proxy for a market, or zero
walletOf
The wallet bound to a proxy
accountOf
The binding stored at proxy creation: wallet, Spoke, market, vault token and reserve
predictProxy

borrowNonce

Event
Emitted when

CollateralSupplied
Vault-token units are supplied to the Spoke for a proxy
CollateralRecredited
Units added to a pledged position are credited
Borrowed
A debt asset is borrowed; carries the receiver, amount, nonce and health factor after
Repaid
A payer repays one debt reserve of a borrower's account; carries the amount spent and the debt after
CollateralWithdrawn
CollateralReduced
Part of a record is removed and its principal paid to the depositor
RepaidWithCollateral
A debt reserve is repaid with released units; carries health factors before and after
CollateralDisabled
The vault-token reserve is disabled as collateral for a proxy whose supply reached zero
SeizedUnitsBurned
LPVaultSwap has the Adapter burn seized units during a liquidation
Error
The block timestamp is past the deadline
The expected nonce differs from the proxy's borrow nonce
ApplicationFrozen

ApplicationPaused

AddressIsFrozen
NoProxy
The wallet has no proxy for the market

The borrow receiver is refused by the receiver rule
ZeroAmount

A repay-all found debt above the cap; nothing moved

Repay with collateral would leave a lower health factor
UnitsMismatch
BackingMismatch

SupplyIncomplete
Supplied shares did not rise by exactly the credited units
LengthMismatch

Errors raised by the RiskModule, Collateralization, the LPVault and Aave pass through unchanged, for example
PriceNotLive
HealthFactorTooLow
BelowMinPledge
TooManyRecords
BreakerTripped
SequencerDown

The AaveAdapter is a UUPS proxy. Its admin roles can be held only by the chain's Avana timelock; every upgrade waits the normal delay of 5 days and can be cancelled by the governance multisig, the Emergency Guardian, the Aave Protocol Guardian or the Aave governance executor. It has no setters: every address change is an upgrade.
PositionProxies and the ProxyManager are immutable and carry no logic, so an Adapter upgrade changes account behaviour without touching any proxy.

What a faulty Adapter could do is bounded by the Aave DAO's Hub add caps and Spoke draw caps, by exact approvals, and by the delay: a borrower who sees a harmful upgrade queued can repay and withdraw before it executes, because those paths read no gate.
Liquidation does not go through these entry points. LPVaultSwap runs it and asks the Adapter only to burn seized units.
Every AaveAdapter borrower function, its gates, call bounds, events and errors.

meta.title: Glossary
meta.description: Definitions of Avana terms in alphabetical order, from AaveAdapter and Avana Umbrella to vault tokens, with the terms that are no longer part of the design.

strings: Glossary
Definitions of Avana terms in alphabetical order, from AaveAdapter and Avana Umbrella to vault tokens, with the terms that are no longer part of the design.
A – B
D – F
G – L
M – P
R – S
T – V
No Longer Used
Disclaimers
AaveAdapter

The upgradeable entry point on each chain for every borrower action: pledge, borrow, repay, withdraw, partial removal, re-credit, repay with collateral and fee collection. It creates proxies, mints and burns vault tokens, runs the RiskModule's checks and has the proxy call the Spoke.
Address freeze

A per-chain stop of one wallet's new activity, set by a guardian and lifted only by a normal-delay timelock operation. A frozen wallet keeps repay, debt-free withdrawal, fee collection and rescue top-ups, and its positions can still be liquidated.
AMM integration

Avana's code for one AMM protocol: its LPVault and pricing library. It takes custody of positions, reads their token amounts at a given price, removes exact units, collects separated fees and reports range and pool-share data.
AMM protocol

A DEX family whose positions Avana can accept. At launch: Uniswap v3 on Ethereum and Aerodrome Slipstream on Base. Uniswap v2, Curve, Balancer and Uniswap v4 are supported by the core and are listed only after their readiness checks pass.
Application pause state

The state of one Hub held by the chain's MarketRegistry: None, Frozen or Paused, with a pause reason of General or MintPathSuspect. It stops new activity only; repay, fee collection, debt-free withdrawal and liquidation stay open.
Avana Hub

A standard Aave V4 Hub owned by the Aave DAO that holds the vault tokens of its markets and the liquidity of its credit lines. There are three tiers, Stable LP, Correlated LP and Volatile LP; at launch Ethereum and Base each have an Avana Stable LP Hub.
Avana Umbrella

Avana's protocol safety module, named after Aave's Umbrella, whose design inspired it. It is the Coverage Spoke of one Hub and debt asset, funded by Avana Labs and controlled by the Aave DAO, and it covers recorded deficits in that asset.
AvanaTimelock

The immutable, self-administered timelock on each chain through which every privileged Avana change executes. Normal delay 5 days (never below 4), short delay 12 hours for a fixed set of calls, 14-day grace window, public execution and two proposers.
Backing invariant

For each market, vault-token supply is at most the credited units plus the pending-settlement units, and equal while every seizure is settled in the same call. Every vault token in circulation is therefore backed by liquidity in custody.
Backing record
Collateralization's entry for one pledged position: depositor, proxy, market, position key, credited units and status. An account holds at most 16 open records per market.
Borrower surplus
The part of a liquidation's recovery above the oracle value of the seized units. It is paid to the borrower's wallet in the debt asset.
CDP Spoke

A standard Aave V4 Spoke per chain, Hub, AMM protocol and risk tier, owned by the Aave DAO. It lists several markets as collateral reserves and the approved debt reserves. Launch Spokes: "Uniswap v3 Stable" on Ethereum and "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" on Base.
Circuit breaker
An automatic stop of new activity in one market or one debt reserve. A temporary gate clears after 30 minutes of healthy observations; a security freeze reopens only after an authorized reset.
Collateral factor (CF)

The Aave V4 factor that sets how much of a reserve's value can support debt. For a vault-token reserve it is the lowest of its tokens' collateral factors multiplied by the pool risk factor, rounded down.
Collateral Risk
A per-reserve value set in the Aave listing that sets the borrower's risk premium. It is not a haircut on collateral value. The borrowing rate is the base rate times one plus the risk premium.
Collateralization
The immutable, AMM-neutral backing ledger on each chain. It keeps every backing record, the largest-first seizure lists, the exposure counters per Hub and the pending-settlement balance.
Coverage ratio

The required size of a First-Loss Reserve: funded balance times 10⁴ must be at least the coverage ratio in bps times the sum of draw caps on that Hub and asset. It is set in the funding ARFC; 20% is an illustrative guide.
Coverage Spoke
A DAO-controlled, supply-only Spoke holding Avana-funded supply of one asset on one Hub, the First-Loss Reserve of that pair. One per Hub and debt asset per chain; also called the Avana Umbrella.
Credit line
A capped amount of one asset that the Aave DAO treasury supplies through the Lend Spoke. It is a draw cap per Hub, asset and CDP Spoke; the draw caps sum to at most the line.
Credited units
The units read from the AMM integration when a position was pledged, less units removed by liquidation and partial removal, plus units added by re-credit. Vault tokens exist only against them.
Cross-Hub credit line
A debt reserve whose funding Hub is not its CDP Spoke's home Hub. It is fully specified and off at launch on every chain.
Debt reserve

A borrowable reserve of a CDP Spoke, recorded with its asset, funding Hub, price source, Coverage Spoke and swap routes. GHO is the first; USDC, USDT or WETH can be enabled per Spoke through the enable-debt-reserve operation.
DebtOracle

The upgradeable Aave price source of one non-GHO debt asset on one chain, with primary, alternate and standby routes, failover, an agreement check and Cached and Expired states. Once Expired it serves its last price raised by a stress rise.
Deficit

Debt that Aave records as unbacked on the funding Hub, per debt reserve and in its own asset, when a liquidation leaves an account with no collateral. Only the Coverage Spoke of the same Hub and asset clears it.
Delay classes

How fast each privileged change can happen: immediate guardian actions (pause, freeze, breaker trips, standby switch, cancel), the 12-hour short delay for a fixed set of risk-reducing calls, the 5-day normal delay for everything else, immutable values and Aave governance.
Deployment operations

The three timelock operations that add a CDP Spoke, a market and a debt reserve: deployCdpSpoke, listCollateralMarket and enableDebtReserve. Each runs at the normal delay and is followed by a short-delay activation.
Depositor of record
The wallet that owned and pledged a position. Only it receives the position back and its separated fees, and it is the bound wallet of its PositionProxy.
Drift check

Avana's on-chain comparison of the live Aave configuration with the values Avana's sizing assumes, including the three required settings and the collateral factor. A mismatch stops new borrowing in the affected market while liquidation continues.
Emergency Guardian

A 3-of-5 Safe on each chain, with signers separate from the governance multisig and the Aave Protocol Guardian. It can pause or freeze Hubs, freeze addresses, trip and reset breakers, switch to standby price routes and cancel queued operations; it cannot upgrade or change parameters.
First-Loss Reserve

Avana-funded supply of one asset in the Coverage Spoke of one Hub, funded before any draw cap on that pair rises above 0. It is Avana's only on-chain loss layer and covers recorded deficits within 72 hours.
Flash source

The per-chain contract through which LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset from the Aave V3 Pool, single asset. Its premium must be at most 10 bps, and it is never the funding Hub of the reserve being liquidated.
Freshness
A feed is fresh while its age is at most its own heartbeat plus a 1,800-second margin. Chainlink stablecoin feeds have heartbeats of 82,800 to 86,400 seconds.
Funding Hub
The Hub a debt reserve draws from. It bears the reserve's deficits, and its pause stops the reserve's borrows.
Governance multisig

A 4-of-7 Safe on each chain with at most 3 Avana Labs signers, at least three organizations and three jurisdictions. With the Aave governance executor it proposes timelock operations; it has no instant power.
Grace

For 30 minutes after a price recovers from Expired, and for 1 hour after a Base sequencer restart, an account can be liquidated only below health factor 0.95. Borrowers get time to act on prices they could not see.
Health factor (HF)

Aave V4's measure of one account on one Spoke: collateral value times collateral factor, divided by total debt value. Below 1.00 the account can be liquidated. In Avana each market has its own account and health factor.
Home Hub
The Hub where a CDP Spoke's collateral reserves live, recorded when the Spoke is registered.
Incident window

The 48-hour longest liquidation stop that caps are sized for: an Aave-side reserve pause or Hub halt, or an oracle price-state pause. Avana's own pause states, breakers and address freeze never stop liquidation.
InKindEscrow

The small immutable payout escrow on each chain. It holds a liquidation payout that a token refused to deliver (the borrower's surplus, Avana's fee or a keeper's reward) until the recipient claims it to an address of its choice.
Keeper
An address on a chain's LPVaultSwap keeper list. Each chain has at least one, Avana's own keeper, and at most 32. A standby keeper on separate infrastructure can be added through the timelock.
Keeper reward
The liquidation caller's payout: the oracle gain after Avana's 20% share, up to what the swaps realized. It is paid in the debt asset repaid.
Lend Spoke
The DAO-owned, supply-only Spoke on each chain through which credit lines are supplied to Hub and asset pairs, GHO first. Public lender deposits are not offered at launch.
Lens

A read-only periphery contract on each chain, outside the audited core, that gives views and previews: accounts, price states, cap headroom, borrow and repay quotes and liquidation previews. No core contract calls it.
Liquidation bonus
The extra collateral Aave seizes per unit of debt repaid, set by the Aave DAO on each CDP Spoke. Avana recommends a minimum bonus of at least 2% and a target health factor of 1.10.
Lock

The immutable reentrancy lock shared by Avana's contracts on one chain. Its two members are the AaveAdapter and LPVaultSwap; custody contracts accept value-moving calls only while one of them holds it.
LPOracle
The upgradeable price feed of one market, with 8 decimals. It prices one vault token by fair composition at Chainlink prices, checks the pool TWAP and a second source, and never reverts or returns 0.
LPVault

The immutable custodian of every pledged position of one AMM protocol on one chain. It validates the exact shape, records the depositor of record, unwinds exact units and returns positions only to their depositor.
LPVaultSwap

The liquidation contract on each chain and the only address the vault token accepts seized collateral to. It flash-borrows the debt asset, calls Aave's liquidation, has the seized units unwound and swaps them into the debt asset in one transaction.
Market

One pool of one AMM protocol on one chain with one exact position shape, with its vault token and its collateral reserve on one CDP Spoke. For concentrated liquidity the shape is the exact tick range.
MarketRegistry
The upgradeable registry on each chain of Hubs, CDP Spokes, markets and their status, debt reserves, price and swap routes, the pause state of each Hub, breaker state and the address freeze set.
Minimum pledge
The smallest USD value a pledge or top-up can add, $10 per market by default. A rescue top-up needs only $10 or the minimum, whichever is lower.
Offboarding

A market status that blocks new pledges and borrowing. After 5 days of notice the liquidation threshold steps down daily over 30 days to half its listed value; repayment, withdrawal and liquidation stay open throughout.
Oracle gain
The oracle value of the units seized in a liquidation, less the debt repaid and the flash premium. Avana's fee is 20% of it, capped by the realized surplus.
ParameterStore
The upgradeable store on each chain of every risk parameter with its bounds, a tightening setter at the short delay and a loosening setter at the normal delay.
Partial removal
Removing part of a pledged position's credited units: the matching vault tokens are burned and the principal goes to the depositor while the position stays pledged.
Pending-settlement balance

Token amounts Collateralization removed for vault tokens Aave seized but that were never settled. They back those vault tokens until anyone calls the pending settlement, which sends the recovered value to the Coverage Spoke.
Permissionless liquidation
The liquidation entry point open to any address, the Aave DAO included. It uses the primary-then-backup swap routes only and pays no gas reimbursement.
Pool risk factor

A per-pool discount in the collateral factor formula, from 1 to 4,000 bps, set by the Aave V4 risk service providers in the listing payload. It reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth and liquidation cost.
Pool-share cap
An optional cap on Avana's combined share of a pool's liquidity on a chain. It is off by default and applies only where a pool's listing sets one; a share above 25% raises a monitoring alert.
Position key
The identifier of a position within its AMM integration. With the integration ID it names a position on a chain.
PositionProxy
One logic-free immutable account per wallet, CDP Spoke and market, created with CREATE2. It is the Aave account for that market and executes only calls from the chain's AaveAdapter.
Price states
Live, Drifting (TWAP or route disagreement), Cached (both routes stale, up to 1 hour) and Expired (after 1 hour). They gate borrowing and seizure; repay and debt-free withdrawal work in every state.
ProxyManager
The immutable contract on each chain that creates PositionProxies at their predicted addresses on the AaveAdapter's request. It refuses a frozen wallet and holds no proxy code that can change.
Re-credit
Crediting liquidity the depositor added to a pledged position through the AMM protocol, with every top-up check. Units anyone adds are not counted until the depositor re-credits them.
Recovery floor
The minimum amount of the debt asset a liquidation's unwind and swaps must return: the oracle value of the seized units less the allowed slippage (1% by default) and small rounding allowances.
Repay with collateral
Repaying debt from part of one pledged position in one flash-funded call. No bonus or Avana fee applies, and the health factor after the call cannot be lower than before it.
Required Spoke settings

Three values the listing sets on every vault-token reserve: receive-shares disabled, liquidation fee 0 or paid to Avana's fee recipient, and no reinvestment controller. Together with the vault token's transfer rule they make LPVaultSwap the only liquidator.
Rescue top-up
A pledge into an indebted account below health factor 1.10, capped at the amount that restores 1.10. It passes containment, and its rescue units count in liquidation but never support new debt.
RiskModule

The upgradeable contract that runs Avana's pledge and borrow-side checks: health factor with rescue units excluded, price freshness and agreement, sequencer state, Aave flags, drift and circuit breakers. It holds no tokens.
Sequencer grace
On Base, the 1-hour period after a sequencer restart during which borrowing is refused and only accounts below health factor 0.95 can be liquidated.
Shortfall top-up
Debt asset a liquidation caller adds from its own funds when the swaps land below the recovery floor, within its own limit. It also pays any rounding gap at final settlement.
Standby route
A price route approved at listing that a guardian can switch a token to at once. The Aave governance executor can undo the switch at once; switching back otherwise takes the normal delay.
Stress floor
The lowest whole-vault-token price used for cap charges and Hub supply-cap sizing, $1.00 by default. It keeps every pledge Avana accepts within Aave's supply cap.
Stress valuation

The conservative price Aave sees for a reserve whose own price is failing: an Expired market at the smallest price, a disagreeing market at the lower route, Expired debt raised by its stress rise. Nothing is seized or repaid at it.
Swap route
A fixed path recorded per market, token and debt asset, with a primary and a backup, that LPVaultSwap uses to swap an unwound token into the debt asset. It never trades through the market's own pool.
Target health factor
The health factor Aave sizes each liquidation toward, one value per CDP Spoke. Avana recommends 1.10; the Aave DAO decides.
Top-up
Top-up slice
A part of each market's cap, 10% by default, reserved for rescue top-ups so that a full market never stops a borrower adding collateral.
Vault token

The immutable, owner-less, collateral-only ERC-20 of one market. One base unit equals one credited unit; only the AaveAdapter mints and burns it, and it moves only between a registered proxy, the Hub and LPVaultSwap.
Vault-token fee receiver
The Aave treasury Spoke registered on each vault-token Hub asset, with supply and draw caps of 0 so that it never holds vault tokens.
VaultTokenFactory
The immutable contract on each chain that deploys vault tokens with CREATE3 at predictable addresses, called only by the timelock, and keeps the write-once token and LPVault registries.
Borrow Spoke
The earlier name for a CDP Spoke.
Full-position settlement
Removed. Every liquidation is partial: Aave sizes the seizure, and the borrower keeps the rest of the position and all of its fees.
In-kind settlement
Removed. Every liquidation swaps the unwound tokens into the debt asset in the same transaction or reverts; no keeper takes the unwound tokens.
SettlementBudget
Removed. No Avana contract pays rounding gaps; the liquidation caller sizes its funding up front and pays any rounding gap through its shortfall top-up.
No Investment Advice:
Avana is a software protocol. This documentation does not constitute investment advice.
Status:
The public sandbox uses simulated assets and makes no onchain transactions.
Risk of Loss:
Users can lose funds through smart contract vulnerabilities, market volatility, impermanent loss, liquidation, or oracle failure.
Regulatory Status:
The regulatory status of Avana and its tokens (if any) is not guaranteed and may vary by jurisdiction.
No Warranty:
The software is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.

meta.title: Key Concepts
meta.description: The concepts behind Avana: markets, vault tokens, per-market accounts, Hubs and Spokes, debt reserves, oracles and price states, collateral and health factors, liquidation, Avana Umbrella, pauses and the timelock.

strings: Key Concepts

The concepts behind Avana: markets, vault tokens, per-market accounts, Hubs and Spokes, debt reserves, oracles and price states, collateral and health factors, liquidation, Avana Umbrella, pauses and the timelock.
LP Collateral
Market
Vault Token
PositionProxy and Account
CDP, Lend and Coverage Spokes
Hubs
Debt Reserves
Oracles and Price States
Collateral Factor
Health Factor
Liquidation Paths
Avana Umbrella
Pauses and Breakers
AvanaTimelock
One short section per concept. Each links to the page that covers it in full.

Token collateral is usually a balance of one asset. An LP position is a changing combination of assets: trades change its inventory, prices change its value, and fees accrue over time. A concentrated-liquidity position also depends on its range and becomes one-sided as prices move out of it. Avana therefore sets risk parameters per market, keeps the liquidity in its pool, and gives each market its own Aave account per borrower.

A market is one pool of one AMM protocol on one chain with one exact position shape. For concentrated liquidity the shape is the exact tick range. Each market has one vault token and is one collateral reserve of exactly one CDP Spoke for life.
A position is accepted only if its range equals the market's exactly. A market listed at [−10, 10] refuses a position at [−9, 10], even though they overlap.
One pool listed with two ranges is two markets.
At launch: Uniswap v3 stablecoin pools on Ethereum and unstaked Aerodrome Slipstream stablecoin pools on Base, such as USDC/USDT and pools containing GHO.
Each market is listed through the AvanaTimelock at the normal delay of 5 days together with the Aave DAO listing payload, which sets its collateral factor, bonus curve and caps.

A vault token is the transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20 of one market. One base unit equals one unit of credited liquidity. Its decimals are fixed at listing between 6 and 18 so that one whole token is worth between $1 and $10 at listing prices. Only the AaveAdapter mints and burns it, and it can move only from a registered proxy into the Hub, from the Hub back to a proxy, or from the Hub to LPVaultSwap on a seizure. It has no owner, admin or emissions.
The full rules are in
Custody and Vault Tokens

Each wallet gets one PositionProxy per CDP Spoke and market, created at a predictable CREATE2 address on its first pledge into that market. The proxy is the Aave account: it holds the market's vault tokens and the debt of every debt reserve the account borrows, under one health factor. It is logic-free and immutable, and it executes only calls from the AaveAdapter; the wallet acts through the AaveAdapter.

Because every market has its own account, nothing is cross-collateralized. Example from the specification: Alice pledges a USDC/USDT position and a GHO/USDC position on "Uniswap v3 Stable" and gets two proxies. She borrows 3,000 GHO on the first. If the GHO/USDC feed goes stale, the second account cannot borrow, while the first keeps borrowing and cannot be liquidated because of the second.
Spoke
What it does
CDP Spoke

One standard Aave V4 Spoke per chain, Hub, AMM protocol and risk tier. It lists several markets as non-borrowable collateral reserves and the approved debt reserves. Launch: "Uniswap v3 Stable" on Ethereum and "Aerodrome Slipstream Stable" on Base.
Lend Spoke
One supply-only Spoke per chain through which the Aave DAO treasury supplies each credit line. No public deposits at launch.
Coverage Spoke
One supply-only Spoke per Hub and debt asset, the Avana Umbrella of that pair, holding Avana-funded First-Loss Reserve supply.

Every Spoke is owned and configured by the Aave DAO. The listing sets three values on every vault-token reserve: receive-shares disabled, liquidation fee 0 (or paid to Avana's fee recipient) and no reinvestment controller. Avana's drift check enforces them. Details are in
Hubs and Spokes

An Avana Hub is a standard Aave V4 Hub owned by the Aave DAO that holds the vault tokens of its markets and the liquidity of its credit lines. There are three tiers: Stable LP, Correlated LP and Volatile LP. At launch Ethereum and Base each have one Avana Stable LP Hub. Each CDP Spoke has one home Hub for its collateral, and each Hub has its own pause state and per-Hub token and depositor caps.

A debt reserve is a borrowable reserve of a CDP Spoke, funded by a capped credit line. GHO is the first debt reserve on each launch Spoke. USDC, USDT or WETH can be enabled per CDP Spoke through the enable-debt-reserve operation, once the Aave DAO approves the credit line, caps, price source and swap routes. Each debt reserve records its funding Hub, its price source and its Coverage Spoke.

Credit line: the Lend Spoke supply cap equals the line, and CDP Spoke draw caps on it sum to at most the line. Launch line: 2,000,000 GHO on Ethereum, with the final value and the Base line set in the funding ARFC.
Each draw cap stays within the flash liquidity of its asset in the Aave V3 Pool and the depth of its swap routes, so every borrowed amount can be liquidated in one transaction.
A cross-Hub credit line, where the funding Hub differs from the Spoke's home Hub, is specified and off at launch.

Each market has an LPOracle that prices one vault token by fair composition: the token amounts the units would hold if the pool traded at the Chainlink prices, valued at those prices. A trade in the pool cannot move the valuation. Each non-GHO debt asset has a DebtOracle with the same route model; GHO debt uses Aave's fixed $1 price.
value = Σ amountᵢ(oracle prices) × priceᵢ
Each token has a Chainlink primary route, an alternate route with automatic failover and a standby route approved at listing. A feed is fresh for its own heartbeat plus 1,800 seconds.
The pool's 30-minute TWAP is a consistency check, not the price. Borrowing and withdrawals with debt also need an independent second source to agree.
On Base every price also reads the sequencer-uptime feed.
State
Meaning
Effect
Live
Fresh prices that agree
Normal operation
Drifting
TWAP disagreement, or the primary and alternate routes disagree
Borrowing and withdrawals with debt blocked; route disagreement also pauses seizure in that market
Cached
Both routes of a token stale, for up to 1 hour
Last accepted price served; pledges, borrowing and seizure of this market wait
Expired
Cached for more than 1 hour
Collateral counts as worthless in Aave; seizure waits for a fresh price or a standby switch
For 30 minutes after a price recovers from Expired, only accounts below health factor 0.95 can be liquidated. Repayment, fee collection and debt-free withdrawal work in every state. More detail is in
Price States
CF_LP = floor(min CFᵢ × poolRiskFactor / 10⁴)

Each token's factor comes from the Aave V4 Core Hub, except that a GHO leg uses an explicit factor set at listing. The pool risk factor is set per pool by the risk service providers and is at most 40%. With two tokens at 78% and the 40% ceiling, CF_LP is 3,120 bps (31.2%). Collateral Risk sets the borrower's rate premium: borrowing rate = base rate × (1 + risk premium). See
Collateral Factors

Aave V4 computes one health factor per account, so per market. The only on-chain borrow limit is Aave's 1.00, plus the minimum health factor the borrower passes with each call. The Lens shows a recommended borrow at 1.10 next to the maximum at 1.00. An account holds at most 16 positions per market, and there is no minimum debt. See

When an account's health factor is below 1, it is liquidated through Aave's standard liquidation call, always partially, by LPVaultSwap. The vault token accepts seized collateral only to LPVaultSwap, so every other caller of the Aave liquidation reverts.
Path
Notes
liquidate
Approved keepers, including Avana's own keeper on each chain
Every swap-route mode
liquidatePermissionless
Any address, including the Aave DAO
Primary-then-backup swap routes only; no gas reimbursement
repayWithCollateral
The borrower
Repays from part of its own position; no bonus and no Avana fee

In one transaction LPVaultSwap flash-borrows the debt asset from the Aave V3 Pool, repays the debt, receives and burns the seized vault tokens, has the LPVault unwind exactly those units, swaps each token into the debt asset with oracle-derived minimums, repays the flash loan and pays out. If the swaps cannot settle, the call reverts and nothing changes. No Avana pause, breaker or freeze stops liquidation. See
Liquidation

Avana Umbrella is Avana's protocol safety module, named after Aave's Umbrella, whose design inspired it. Each Hub and debt asset has one: a Coverage Spoke controlled by the Aave DAO and funded by Avana Labs in that asset, holding the pair's First-Loss Reserve. When a liquidation empties an account while debt remains, Aave records a deficit on the funding Hub, and the Umbrella of the same Hub and asset covers it within 72 hours. It is Avana's only on-chain loss layer. A deficit larger than the reserve is a loss to that Hub asset's suppliers.
Avana's containment tools stop new activity only. Repayment, fee collection, debt-free withdrawal and liquidation stay open in every state.

Pause state per Hub: None, Frozen or Paused. Frozen blocks new accounts and borrowing. Paused, with the reason General, also blocks top-ups other than rescue top-ups, withdrawals with debt and repay with collateral. A pause with the reason MintPathSuspect also refuses every top-up.

Circuit breakers per market and per debt reserve. Temporary gates (price, pool share, pool depth) clear after 30 minutes of healthy observations. Security freezes (an outstanding deficit above 10,000 GHO, issuer action, configuration drift, a guardian's manual trip) stay until an authorized reset.
Address freeze: a per-chain freeze of one wallet's new activity, at most 20 per guardian per rolling 24 hours, lifted only by a normal-delay operation.
The Emergency Guardian (a 3-of-5 Safe per chain) and the Aave Protocol Guardian can use these tools at once. See
Emergency Controls

Every privileged change to an Avana contract on a chain executes through that chain's AvanaTimelock, with no bypass. The governance multisig (4-of-7) and the Aave governance executor propose. Anyone executes a ready operation within its 14-day grace window.
Delay
Value
Used for
Normal
5 days (never below 4 or above 5)
Upgrades, listings, loosening parameters, keeper additions, role changes
Short
12 hours
Only a fixed set of risk-reducing, activity-stopping or restoring calls
Grace
14 days
Window to execute a ready operation

The governance multisig, the Emergency Guardian, the Aave Protocol Guardian and the Aave governance executor can cancel. Only the Aave governance executor can cancel a role change or an operation that restores reviewed configuration. See
Governance
The concepts behind Avana: markets and vault tokens, per-market accounts, Hubs and Spokes, debt reserves, oracles, collateral and health factors, liquidation, Avana Umbrella, pauses and the timelock.

strings: Liquidation Examples
Worked Avana liquidations with full numbers: Uniswap v3 on Ethereum, Aerodrome Slipstream on Base with sequencer grace, fee and surplus variants, a dust gap and a GHO-debt walkthrough.

Worked liquidations with every number: seizure, recovery floor, swaps, flash repayment and payouts.
Example values; each market's parameters are set at listing.
Each example liquidates one account, which holds one market, against one debt reserve. Amounts are in the repaid debt asset. The formulas used here are on the flow page:
Liquidation Flow

Common symbols: D is the debt Aave repays, c the vault tokens seized, φ the flash premium, V the oracle value of the seizure, R the debt asset recovered, Y the realized surplus, A Avana's fee, Kr the keeper reward, B the borrower surplus and keeperOut the caller's payout.
Bob has a USDC/USDT Uniswap v3 position on the Uniswap v3 Stable CDP Spoke of the Ethereum Stable LP Hub and owes USDC. His health factor is below 1.
Setup
Value
Vault-token price
$2.10 per vault token (18 decimals)
Debt reserve
USDC, reserve 2, funded by the Stable LP Hub's USDC credit line, priced by the USDC DebtOracle at $1.00
Aave bonus
10,500 bps (5%), liquidation fee 0
Slippage allowance
100 bps
Floor rounding allowance
1 USDC
Flash premium
5 bps: the FLASH_BORROWER role is not yet granted; maxFlashFeeBps is 10
Application state
Frozen, which stops new pledges and borrowing but not this liquidation
Avana's keeper K1 calls the Lens preview, which returns a repayment of 1,950 USDC and a payout of 70.02 USDC.

K1 calls liquidate through private order flow with debtToCover 1,950 USDC, keeperFunds 0, flashAmount 1,950 USDC, PrimaryThenBackup, a deadline 120 s ahead, minPayout 69 USDC (more than 1% below the preview) and maxShortfall 0.

LPVaultSwap checks the deadline, takes the lock, checks K1 is approved, confirms the health factor is below 1, and pokes the LP Oracle and the USDC DebtOracle, which is Live. It does not read the pause state.
Flash checks: the source can lend 1,950 USDC, and the premium of 0.975 USDC passes because 975,000 × 10,000 = 9,750,000,000 is at most 10 × 1,950,000,000. The Aave V3 Pool lends 1,950 USDC.
Aave repays D = 1,950 USDC and seizes c = 1,950 × 1.05 / 2.10 = 975 vault tokens, sent to LPVaultSwap.

The AaveAdapter burns them and the LP Vault unwinds about 1,030.25 USDC and 1,010 USDT. The USDC leg enters R directly, and the USDT leg's primary route returns 1,010.05 USDC at or above its per-leg minimum. R = 2,040.30 USDC.

Floor: V = 975 × 2.10 = 2,047.5 USDC. The slippage term is ⌈2,047.5 × 0.99⌉ = 2,027.025 USDC, U = 2 base units, so the floor is 2,027.025 − 0.000002 − 1 = 2,026.024998 USDC. R is above it, and the rounding gap is max(0, 1,950 + 0.975 − 0 − 2,040.30) = 0.
Waterfall
Calculation
USDC
Realized surplus Y
Oracle gain G
Avana fee A
Keeper reward Kr
Borrower surplus B
Y − A − Kr
keeperOut

Payout order: 1,950.975 USDC to the flash source, 19.305 USDC to the fee recipient, 0 to Bob, and 70.02 USDC to K1, which is at least minPayout. USDC is conserved: 1,950 + 2,040.30 = 3,990.30 in, and 1,950 + 1,950.975 + 19.305 + 0 + 70.02 out. No GHO moves at any point.
Events include FlashLoanServed, FlashLoanUsed, SeizedUnitsBurned, RecordDebited, SeizureSettled, UnitsUnwound and LiquidationSettled. A payout that fails to deliver goes to the payout escrow.
Same liquidation as above, with different route results. The oracle gain G stays 96.525 USDC, so Avana's fee stays 19.305 USDC while the realized surplus covers it.
Routes return R
Outcome
Recovery beat the oracle value: 4.5 USDC goes to Bob's wallet and K1 receives 77.22 USDC.
A caller that sandwiched its own routes down to just above the floor still pays the full fee. Its reward falls to 56.72 USDC, so it settles only with a minPayout at or below that.
keeperOut is 64.72 USDC, below minPayout of 69, so the call reverts with PayoutTooLow.
PayoutTooLow only adds a revert. It changes no amount, route or recipient, and the floor is still computed from oracle prices alone.

Market 3 is a USDC/USDT Aerodrome Slipstream market (tick spacing 1, exact range, unstaked position) on the Aerodrome Slipstream Stable CDP Spoke of the Base Stable LP Hub, priced at $2.00 per vault token. Carol owes 20,000 USDC. Aave's bonus is 2%. The FLASH_BORROWER role is pending on Base, so the Base Pool charges 5 bps against Base's maxFlashFeeBps of 10.

The Base sequencer restarts at 10:00:00. At 10:20:00 Carol's health factor is 0.9997. A keeper call reverts with SequencerGrace, because 0.9997 is not below the grace threshold of 0.95. The USDC/USD feed last published 21 hours earlier (75,600 s, within 88,200 s), so the price is fresh. An account at a health factor of 0.93 is liquidated at 10:20.

At 11:00:02, the first 2 s Base block after the 3,600 s grace period, keeper K2 calls the Lens preview (a repayment of 2,000 USDC) and then liquidate with debtToCover 2,000 USDC, keeperFunds 0, flashAmount 2,000 USDC, PrimaryThenBackup, a deadline 120 s (60 Base blocks) ahead, minPayout 25 USDC and maxShortfall 0.
The flash source can lend well above 2,000 USDC. The premium is 1 USDC, and 1,000,000 × 10,000 = 10,000,000,000 is at most 10 × 2,000,000,000.

Aave repays D = 2,000 USDC and seizes c = 2,000 × 1.02 / 2.00 = 1,020 vault tokens. The Slipstream LP Vault checks the pool lock through Slipstream's own slot layout, then unwinds about 1,020 USDC and 1,020 USDT.

Floor: costsBps = 5 and s = min(100, ⌊10,000 × 195 / 10,200⌋) = 100. V = 2,040 USDC and φD = 1 USDC. The floor is 2,019.6 − 0.000002 − 1 = 2,018.599998 USDC. The USDT route returns 1,018.50 USDC, so R = 2,038.50 USDC.

The Pool pulls 2,001 USDC. Conservation: 4,038.5 in equals 2,000 + 2,001 + 7.8 + 29.7 out. If the fee recipient were blocklisted by USDC's issuer, the 7.8 USDC would go to the payout escrow and be claimed later with claim.

Market 1 is a USDC/USDT 0.01% Uniswap v3 market with an exact range on the Uniswap v3 Stable CDP Spoke of the Ethereum Stable LP Hub. The vault token has 6 decimals and is priced at $2.00. The debt reserve is USDC at $1.00 with a 1 USDC floor rounding allowance, a 100 bps slippage allowance and Avana's 20% share. Avana holds FLASH_BORROWER on the Ethereum Core Pool, so the premium is 0. Aave's bonus is 10,200 bps with a liquidation fee of 0.
The keeper flash-borrows 9,800 USDC with keeperFunds 0.
Aave repays D = 9,800 USDC and seizes 9,800 × 1.02 / 2.00 = 4,998 vault tokens.
The pool sits at tick 3 and the oracle at tick 2. No spot check applies; the unwound tokens are worth at least V at oracle prices.
Floor: s = 100 bps, V = 9,996 USDC, U = 2 base units, floor 9,895.039998 USDC.
The LP Vault returns about 4,998 USDC and 4,998 USDT. The USDC leg needs no swap. The USDT route returns 4,952 USDC, above its leg minimum of 4,946.030395 USDC. R = 9,950 USDC.
Case
Base case
Routes beat the oracle
Weaker routes

Routes beat the oracle: Kr is capped at the oracle gain after the fee, 156.8, and the remaining 14 USDC goes to the borrower's wallet. If the wallet is on USDC's blocklist, the 14 USDC goes to the payout escrow credited to the wallet.
Weaker routes: with minPayout set to 110 USDC, the call reverts with PayoutTooLow(95,800,000, 110,000,000). A is unchanged at 39.2.

The same account can be liquidated by any address through the permissionless path, with debtToCover 9,800 USDC, callerFunds 0, flashAmount 9,800 USDC, a deadline 120 s ahead and minPayout 110 USDC. With R = 9,950 USDC the caller receives 110.8 USDC and Avana's fee is 39.2 USDC.
Same market. The account's last 0.3978 vault token (397,800 units) is seized for D = 0.78 USDC.
V = 0.7956 USDC and the slippage term is ⌈795,600 × 0.99⌉ = 787,644 base units.
The floor is max(0, 787,644 − 2 − 1,000,000) = 0. Without the rounding allowance, the floor of 0.787644 USDC would revert every attempt and the deficit would never be recorded.
A route returns R = 0.77 USDC. The rounding gap is 0.78 − 0.77 = 0.01 USDC.
Caller settings
Flash-funded, maxShortfall 0.02 USDC
The caller pays 0.01 USDC through the top-up. R′ = 0.78 USDC, Y = 0 and keeperOut = (0 + 0.78 + 0.78) − (0.78 + 0.78) = 0.
Flash-funded, maxShortfall 0
Reverts with InsufficientProceeds: the gap, not the floor, is short. The keeper resubmits with keeperFunds of 0.01 USDC, which closes the gap.
Caller-funded 0.78 USDC, no flash loan
The gap is 0, Y = 0 and keeperOut = (0.78 + 0.77) − 0.78 = 0.77 USDC: a 0.01 USDC loss the caller accepts through minPayout.
In every case the caller pays the rounding gap. No protocol balance is drawn, and any deficit the call records is reported normally.

Same market 1. GHO is debt reserve 0, drawn by the CDP Spoke from the Stable LP Hub's GHO credit line at Aave's fixed $1 price, with a floor rounding allowance of 1 GHO. The vault-token reserve is reserve 1, with a Collateral Factor of 2,812 bps, a maximum bonus of 10,500, a bonus factor of 4,000, a health factor for the maximum bonus of 0.90 and a target health factor of 1.10. Alice's proxy P holds 141,232 vault tokens (282,464 USD) and owes 79,452.85 GHO.

A USDT move takes P's health factor to 282,464 × 0.2812 / 79,452.85 ≈ 0.9997. Keeper K1 calls the Lens preview for P and reserve 0: bonus 10,200, debt to target (1.10 × 79,452.85 − 79,428.88) / (1.10 − 1.02 × 0.2812) ≈ 9,800.2 GHO. The Ethereum Pool's idle GHO covers 9,800 GHO, so the preview sets flashAmount to 9,800 GHO and keeperFunds to 0.

K1 calls liquidate for P, market 1 and reserve 0 with debtToCover 9,800 GHO, keeperFunds 0, flashAmount 9,800 GHO, PrimaryThenBackup, a deadline 120 s ahead, minPayout 110 GHO and maxShortfall 0. LPVaultSwap checks the deadline, takes the lock, and checks the keeper, the proxy, the reserve and that 0 + 9,800 ≥ 9,800. It does not read the pause state.

LPVaultSwap reads the registry, pokes the LP Oracle (Live; USDC/USD and USDT/USD answers 20 hours and 3 hours old, within 88,200 s), finds the sequencer gate open on Ethereum, reads the health factor 0.9997, the bonus 10,200 and a liquidation fee of 0, and confirms the Hub's shares equal its assets.

LPVaultSwap calls the flash source for 9,800 GHO. The source checks the GHO reserve is active and flash-enabled, idle GHO covers 9,800 and the premium is 0 (role granted), then calls the Pool's flashLoan. The Pool sends 9,800 GHO to the source and calls it back; the source forwards 9,800 GHO to LPVaultSwap and calls onFlashLoan, which runs the next five steps.
Collateralization's beginSeizure snapshots P's 141,232,000,000 supplied shares.

LPVaultSwap approves the Spoke for 9,800 GHO and calls the liquidation for collateral reserve 1, debt reserve 0 and P, with receiveShares false. Aave restores D = 9,800 GHO to the Hub and the Hub transfers 4,998 vault tokens to LPVaultSwap. No deficit.

The AaveAdapter burns the 4,998 vault tokens. Collateralization checks that the share drop and the supply drop both equal c, debits P's largest record, and has the Uniswap v3 LP Vault unwind 4,998,000,000 units. The LP Vault collects only the principal, about 4,998 USDC and 4,998 USDT, to LPVaultSwap.

The floor in GHO is 9,895.0399980002 GHO (U = 0.0000019998 GHO). The USDC→GHO and USDT→GHO primary routes, through fixed DEX pools, return 4,976 and 4,974 GHO: R = 9,950 GHO and the rounding gap is 0.
onFlashLoan sends 9,800 GHO back to the flash source and returns; the source approves the Pool for 9,800 GHO, which pulls it.

Waterfall: Y = 150, A = 39.2, Kr = 110.8, B = 0 and keeperOut = 110.8 GHO, at least minPayout. LPVaultSwap sends 39.2 GHO to the fee recipient and 110.8 GHO to K1, emits LiquidationSettled and releases the lock.

After the transaction P holds 136,234 vault tokens (272,468 USD) against 69,652.85 GHO, a health factor of 272,468 × 0.2812 / 69,652.85 = 1.09999. Alice keeps the rest of her position and all of its fees. Had K1 called the Spoke's liquidation function directly, the Hub's vault-token transfer to K1 would have reverted with UnauthorizedRecipient.
What happens
Expired market

An account in Expired market 7 holding $20,000 of vault tokens and owing 6,400 GHO has a health factor near 0, because Expired collateral counts as almost 0. A call naming market 7 reverts with StalePrice until a fresh price or a standby price route arrives; the keeper then liquidates at the fresh price.
Stale debt price
USDC accepted at 0.9999 and Expired, with a 500 bps stress rise, counts at 1.049895 USD. The account can still be liquidated against its GHO debt; a call repaying USDC waits for a fresh USDC price.
Pool moved before the call

The pool is pushed to 2 USDT per USDC. The $10,000 position now holds tokens worth $10,606.60 at oracle prices. The liquidation unwinds at that price; each leg must still meet its oracle minimum, and the floor uses V = 10,000.
Third-party liquidation call

An attacker holding 1 USDC calls the Spoke's liquidation directly on an account at a health factor of 0.98. Aave sizes a seizure of 510,000 units, and the Hub's transfer reverts with UnauthorizedRecipient. The account is unchanged.
A 1,950 USDC whole-debt close sized at 2,047.5 USDC still settles after a 1-wei repayment: Aave pulls 1,949.999999 USDC and the caller payout is 1 wei lower.
Dust leg

USDC debt at $0.70 and a DAI leg of 0.000007349976535931 DAI at $0.05000016: the leg is worth less than one USDC base unit, so it is sent to the caller unswapped, R = 0, the floor is 0, and a caller-funded call repays the dust debt.
Small account on Base
An account owing 40 USDC with one record uses 1,550,000 gas. The keeper's part of the bonus is 0.54208 USDC, and Avana's keeper liquidates it whether or not that covers the gas.
Whole-debt close and record cap

An account owing 320 USDC whose preview returns a whole-debt close of 336 USDC is liquidated in one call with debtToCover 336 USDC. An account with 16 records uses 5,150,000 gas, still one transaction.
Worked Avana liquidations with full numbers, from Uniswap v3 on Ethereum and Slipstream on Base to fee variants, a dust gap and a GHO-debt walkthrough.
